abstract: Despite advances in early recognition, aetiology-directed therapy, intensive cardiovascular care and short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS), cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high mortality and morbidity. MCS can restore systemic perfusion and stabilise patients as a bridge to recovery or advanced heart failure therapies, or as a bridge-to-decision when the final therapeutic destination remains uncertain. However, appropriate patient and device selection remains challenging. The optimal timing of support is uncertain, as both premature implantation and delayed use in advanced shock may limit benefit while increasing complications. Device selection should therefore be individualised according to the predominant patient phenotype, including left ventricular, right ventricular or biventricular failure, concomitant respiratory failure, vascular access and anatomical considerations. Randomised trials have focused predominantly on acute myocardial infarction-related CS, whereas data in heart failure-related and acute-on-chronic CS remain limited. Recent trials have also shown that greater haemodynamic support does not uniformly translate into improved survival, highlighting the importance of matching device physiology to shock phenotype and clinical trajectory. MCS is associated with clinically relevant complications, including major bleeding, haemolysis, limb ischaemia, stroke, thrombosis and vascular injury. Accordingly, its use should be considered within a strategy integrating reversibility, neurological prognosis, recovery potential, a realistic definitive therapeutic strategy, technical feasibility and anticipated complication risk. This Mini Review summarises contemporary indications, devices and complications of MCS in CS, with emphasis on phenotype-guided selection, timing, intensive care management and current evidence gaps.
title: Update in short-term mechanical circulatory support: indications, devices and complications.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) have a markedly high mortality. Although ticagrelor has demonstrated superiority over clopidogrel in the AMI population, its efficacy and safety in elderly patients with AMI-CS remain uncertain. This study aimed to compare the associations of ticagrelor and clopidogrel with early in-hospital clinical outcomes in elderly patients with AMI-CS.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 839 patients aged ≥65 years with AMI-CS who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at participating hospitals in China within the Improving Care for Cardiovascular Disease in China-Acute Coronary Syndrome (CCC-ACS) project between November 2014 and December 2020. Patients with missing information on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), those who did not receive DAPT within 24 hours of first medical contact, and those with combined use of or switching between P2Y12 inhibitors during hospitalization were excluded. Patients were grouped according to the P2Y12 inhibitor received: ticagrelor (n=314) or clopidogrel (n=525). The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major bleeding during the first 15 days of hospitalization; major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, propensity score matching (PSM), and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for potential confounders.
RESULTS: Compared with clopidogrel, ticagrelor was associated with higher risk of all-cause mortality [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.52, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.05-2.21, P=0.03] and MACE (adjusted HR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.09-2.01, P=0.01) during the first 15 days of hospitalization, without a statistically significant difference in major bleeding (adjusted HR 1.76, 95% CI: 0.68-4.52, P=0.24). Subgroup analyses generally showed a similar direction of association for all-cause mortality. The associations with mortality and MACE remained statistically significant after PSM; the corresponding IPTW estimates were directionally similar but not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: Among elderly AMI-CS patients undergoing PCI, ticagrelor did not confer a clinical benefit over clopidogrel and was associated with increased in-hospital mortality and MACE without a significant increase in major bleeding. These findings highlight the need for cautious selection of P2Y12 inhibitors in this high-risk population and further prospective studies to guide individualized therapy.
title: Association of ticagrelor versus clopidogrel with in-hospital early outcomes in elderly patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock: findings from CCC-ACS project.

abstract: The autonomic nervous system (ANS) and insulin resistance (IR) are linked through a bidirectional pathogenic cycle established during the normoglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic phase of metabolic disease, years before conventional glucose thresholds are crossed. This review identifies the ANS and IR as convergent therapeutic targets for breaking this vicious cycle, synthesising evidence from autonomic physiology, clinical diabetology, and neuroscience into an integrated mechanistic framework. Two mechanistically distinct arms sustain the cycle: a fast, potentially reversible functional arm driven by hyperinsulinaemia - mediated sympathoexcitation via hypothalamic insulin-signalling pathways, and a slow, progressively irreversible structural arm driven by hyperglycaemia-induced autonomic neuropathy. Experimental evidence demonstrates that inducible peripheral sympathetic blockade prevents overnutrition-induced insulin resistance, establishing sympathetic overactivity as a primary causal driver rather than a consequence. Cross-sectional data have identified cardiac autonomic dysfunction in normoglycaemic individuals with elevated 1-hour post-load glucose who meet no pre-diabetes definition, revealing a population undetectable by current screening criteria. Prospective data from a landmark randomised prevention trial confirmed that autonomic improvement independently predicts diabetes prevention beyond weight loss, with hazard ratios of 0.84-0.85 for incident diabetes. Cardiac autonomic neuropathy, detectable via heart rate variability analysis, is present in 9-39% of pre-diabetic populations and confers a pooled relative mortality risk of 2.14 across 15 studies. Therapeutic interventions targeting both autonomic rebalancing and insulin sensitisation - including structured exercise, bariatric surgery, vagal nerve stimulation, renal denervation, and metabolic pharmacotherapy - converge on identifiable nodes of this feedback loop, enabling stage-matched targeting. We propose a risk stratification framework integrating autonomic assessment with glycaemic staging, including a proposed "Stage 0" category for normoglycaemic individuals with elevated 1-hour post-load glucose, to guide early, targeted intervention when the cycle remains breakable.
journal: Diabetes, metabolic syndrome and obesity : targets and therapy
title: Sympathovagal Imbalance and Insulin Resistance: The Autonomic Nervous System as a Convergent Therapeutic Target for Breaking a Bidirectional Pathogenic Cycle.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pheochromocytoma is a rare cause of cardiogenic shock with diverse cardiovascular manifestations. Although catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy is well recognized, presentations closely resembling fulminant myocarditis are uncommon and diagnostically challenging. The role of cytokine-mediated inflammatory activation in such presentations is not well defined.
CASE SUMMARY: A previously healthy woman in her 30s presented with fever, ventricular arrhythmias, and severe left ventricular dysfunction, rapidly progressing to cardiogenic shock requiring venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and Impella support. Fulminant myocarditis was initially suspected based on clinical, electrocardiographic, and biomarker findings, and immunomodulatory therapy was initiated. Although transient improvement was observed, endomyocardial biopsy showed minimal inflammatory infiltration. Subsequent computed tomography revealed a left adrenal mass, and biochemical testing confirmed markedly elevated catecholamines. Notably, interleukin-6 (IL-6) was also markedly elevated relative to C-reactive protein. Despite initiation of α-blockade, the patient developed recurrent haemodynamic collapse, necessitating emergency adrenalectomy. Pathological examination confirmed a necrotic pheochromocytoma, but the patient died of refractory multiorgan failure.
DISCUSSION: This case illustrates how pheochromocytoma can closely mimic fulminant myocarditis, with a risk of diagnostic anchoring. The coexistence of marked IL-6 elevation and catecholamine excess raises the possibility of concomitant inflammatory activation, although a causal role of IL-6 cannot be established. Recognition of this pattern is important to prompt reconsideration of endocrine aetiologies in myocarditis-like cardiogenic shock.
title: Pheochromocytoma masquerading as fulminant myocarditis with marked interleukin-6 elevation: a case report.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the mortality and postoperative complications of patients undergoing Bentall-DeBono surgery at the Cardiovascular Surgery Service of the National Cardiovascular Institute, EsSalud, Lima, Peru, between 2019 and 2024.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective, descriptive, case series observational study of patients undergoing composite valve-conduit replacement (Bentall-De Bono procedure) for aortic root pathology between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary objective was to determine all-cause mortality and major complications.
RESULTS: Sixty-three patients underwent Bentall-De Bono surgery. The median age was 58 years (IQR: 40-71), and 19% of patients had Marfan syndrome. The 30-day mortality rate was 7.9% (5 patients). The main complications were: stroke (6.3%), perioperative myocardial infarction (4.8%), permanent pacemaker implantation (11%), and excessive postoperative bleeding (6.3%). The median length of hospital stay was 17 days, and the median length of stay in the ICU was 4 days. In a median follow-up of 745 days (403-1060), the mortality rate was 14%, the stroke rate was 7.9%, the myocardial infarction rate was 4.8%, and the definitive pacemaker implantation rate was 14%.
CONCLUSIONS: Our results for the Bentall-De Bono procedure are acceptable and comparable to those reported in the international literature.

abstract: The conventional pacing-over-the-wire technique in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) results in high impedance and voltage thresholds, which may cause loss of capture and valve embolisation. Our team reported that coronary wire pacing, in which a coronary wire is placed in the left coronary artery (anode) and a left ventricular wire (cathode), is associated with extremely low impedance and pacing voltage thresholds in patients who are at high risk of coronary obstruction. Moreover, coronary wire pacing is simple and reliable. In this study, we illustrate the coronary wire pacing technique in a patient to provide a new approach to wire pacing in TAVR.
title: Pacing during TAVR through a coronary wire in the coronary artery and left ventricular wire.

abstract: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) remains an important limitation in patients with a small aortic annulus undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. The Yang technique (Y-incision) has recently emerged as an effective alternative for achieving greater aortic annular enlargement while maintaining favorable perioperative outcomes. We report the first case of aortic annular enlargement using the Yang technique performed at our institution in a 56-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and a small aortic annulus. Intraoperative evaluation revealed a 19-mm aortic annulus. After enlargement via a Y-incision and reconstruction with a bovine pericardial patch, a 23-mm mechanical prosthesis was successfully implanted without perioperative complications. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated adequate prosthetic function, with a significant reduction in transvalvular gradients. Our initial experience suggests that the Yang technique is a safe, reproducible, and feasible option for centers introducing this procedure into their surgical practice. Although limited to a single case, the favorable outcome has encouraged our team to continue performing this technique in carefully selected patients.

abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality despite significant advances in its management. This study aimed to synthesize recent advances in HF management, including the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and advances in gene therapy. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for original research (2020-January 2026) on recent advances in HF management, including AI and gene-based therapies. While guideline-directed management and therapy (GDMT) substantially reduce mortality and hospitalization in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), utilization of such therapies is frequently constrained by delayed initiation, incomplete titration, noncompliance, and cost. Beyond foundational therapy, finerenone, sodium glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) across the ejection fraction (EF) spectrum, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) for obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) extend phenotype-directed options. Transcatheter mitral and tricuspid repair/replacement has shifted mitral and tricuspid regurgitation from a bystander lesion to a treatable contributor to improvement of symptoms and quality of life. Adjunctive transcatheter mitral interventions have expanded treatment options for selected symptomatic HFrEF patients with secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) despite optimized GDMT, improving MR severity, functional status, and reducing HF hospitalizations. Donor-derived cell-free DNA rejection surveillance, donation after circulatory death to expand donor supply, and refinement of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) antithrombotic strategies are evolving in advanced HF. AI tools and gene therapies are showing promising results but require further large-scale studies for validation and clinical adoption. Contemporary HF management is increasingly phenotype- and trajectory-guided, but its clinical adoption is limited by optimal implementation and access barriers. Future research should focus on outcomes-based validation with a clear patient-selection framework to enable durable real-world implementation to improve outcomes further.

abstract: Heart failure (HF) continues to be a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Despite optimized medical therapy (OMT), a significant portion of patients will progress to advanced stages of HF to which OMT is no longer sufficient. Myocardial revascularization remains a cornerstone for patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy, with evidence showing significant survival benefits over OMT alone. Valvular interventions address secondary mitral and aortic disease that contribute to declining cardiac function. For patients with end-stage failure or cardiogenic shock, mechanical circulatory support devices and ventricular-assist devices serve as bridge or destination therapy.

abstract:
AIMS: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), often necessitating atherectomy-based debulking devices that increase procedural complexity and risk. We aimed to develop and externally validate a Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) to predict atherectomy device use during PCI and compare its performance with that of blinded human readers, including general cardiologists and PCI experts.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective multicentre study included 498 calcified coronary lesions from 419 patients who underwent PCI after preprocedural CCTA. Data from 12 institutions were used for training and validation with four-fold cross-validation, and data from two independent institutions (97 lesions) served as an external test cohort. The model combined a convolutional neural network feature extractor with Transformer-based multiple instance learning, and clinical variables were evaluated for incremental value. In the external test cohort, the CCTA-only model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.788 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.691-0.873) for predicting atherectomy device use. Adding clinical variables resulted in an AUC of 0.805 (95% CI, 0.713-0.886), indicating limited incremental value. In the reader comparison, the model showed higher accuracy than general cardiologists (0.742 vs. 0.619; P = 0.029) and numerically similar accuracy to PCI experts (0.742 vs. 0.670; P = 0.230).
CONCLUSION: A Transformer-based deep learning model using preprocedural CCTA showed clinically relevant performance for predicting atherectomy device use during PCI in an independent external test cohort. These findings suggest that the model may support lesion assessment and procedural planning.
title: A transformer-based deep learning model for predicting the use of atherectomy devices during PCI from preprocedural cardiac computed tomography angiography.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional tricuspid regurgitation (fTR) is usually caused by annular dilation and leaflet tethering secondary to right atrial (RA) or right ventricular (RV) remodelling. Rarely, extrinsic factors may impair annular motion.
CASE SUMMARY: We report a 83-year-old woman with constrictive pericarditis who presented with right-sided heart failure and moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Multimodality imaging revealed a thickened pericardium, preserved RA and RV size, and a non-dilated, saddle-shaped annulus with markedly reduced motion. Following pericardiectomy, tricuspid annular mobility normalized, right-sided pressures decreased, and TR improved from moderate to mild. We introduce the term non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid regurgitation to describe this rare mechanism of isolated annular dysfunction caused by pericardial tethering.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights a novel, distinct, and reversible form of fTR caused by pericardial constraint rather than chamber remodelling. We propose the term non-atrial/non-ventricular fTR to describe this mechanism. Recognizing this entity may guide surgical decision-making and avoid unnecessary tricuspid valve intervention.
title: Non-atrial/non-ventricular functional tricuspid valve regurgitation: a case report.
Right mainstem intubation improves transoesophageal echocardiographic guidance during mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The no-reflow phenomenon during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is commonly associated with distal embolization from high-risk coronary plaques, including lesions with intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-defined attenuation. Histopathological analysis of embolic debris captured during PCI is rarely reported and may provide additional insights into the relationship between plaque characteristics and coronary flow outcomes.
CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man presented with acute coronary syndrome and decompensated heart failure. Coronary angiography demonstrated severe multi-vessel coronary artery disease, including a long right coronary artery lesion with extensive IVUS attenuation. Given the high risk of distal embolization, PCI was performed using a distal protection device. Drug-eluting stents were successfully implanted, and Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction flow grade 3 was maintained throughout the procedure without slow flow or no reflow. Histopathological examination of debris captured by the distal protection device demonstrated predominantly fibrin- and collagen-rich thrombotic material with macrophage infiltration and no apparent abundant lipid component. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery and was discharged without procedural complications.
DISCUSSION: The composition of retrieved embolic debris captured during PCI differed from the expected imaging phenotype. This case highlights the potential discrepancy between intracoronary imaging appearance and embolized material and underscores the multifactorial nature of coronary slow flow and no reflow. Careful interpretation of IVUS attenuation and embolic pathology is warranted when assessing procedural risk.
title: Long IVUS-attenuated plaque without no-reflow: histological findings of captured embolic debris and implications for the interpretation of IVUS attenuation: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an important cause of ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), which affects young women. Treatment with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is indicated in clinically and haemodynamically unstable patients. Late coronary artery perforation (CAP) is an uncommon, but potentially fatal complication of a PCI that can occur 30 min to 9 days after the procedure.
CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital with STEMI. Coronarography showed a type 2A SCAD of the LAD. We proceeded with PCI-stenting and the result appeared optimal. After 3 days of uneventful postinterventional stay, the patient became hypotensive and clinically unstable, with echocardiography revealing a cardiac tamponade. We performed an urgent pericardiocentesis and coronarography, detecting a type 3 coronary artery perforation of the LAD in-stent, which we covered with a graft stent. Following the intervention, the patient had pericardial inflammation for the next month with intermittent fever and persisting pericardial effusion. After administering Colchicine for 3 months, the effusion completely subsided, with control echocardiographies showing normal pericardium.
DISCUSSION: PCI in patients with SCAD-induced STEMI can be challenging and has a risk of complications. Late CAP is a rare complication that can easily be overlooked, especially when we think that the result of the intervention was optimal. In our case, we think that the cause of CAP is the post-dilatation with a high-pressure non-compliant balloon. The goal of this case report is to remind us of the possibility of CAP even if three days have passed following the procedure.
title: Late coronary artery perforation with subsequent cardiac tamponade 3 days after primary percutaneous coronary intervention in a young woman with spontaneous coronary artery dissection-induced ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a case report.

abstract: We present the case of a 68-year-old man with stable angina and complex multivessel coronary artery disease. Computed tomography revealed a critically calcified stenosis of the left anterior descending artery and an anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the left coronary sinus, with an interarterial course and severe calcification. Following initial revascularisation of the left anterior descending artery using rotational atherectomy, the right coronary artery was treated in a staged procedure. Because the severe stenosis and challenging ostial anatomy precluded advancement of an intracoronary imaging catheter, angiography-guided intravascular lithotripsy was performed. This approach enabled effective plaque modification and the successful implantation of two drug-eluting stents, with an optimal angiographic result. This case highlights the safety and effectiveness of intravascular lithotripsy as an alternative treatment for anomalous coronary anatomy and severely calcified lesions when intracoronary imaging guidance is not feasible.

title: Anomalous coronary origin and severe calcification: a challenge for percutaneous coronary intervention. Case report.

abstract: Severe coronary artery calcification reduces vessel compliance and predisposes to failed predilatation and stent underexpansion; intracoronary imaging is therefore essential to guide and verify lesion preparation. We report a 61-year-old man with hypertension and angina. Coronary CT angiography showed extensive circumferential calcification of the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Coronary angiography revealed a 60% stenosis in the proximal-to-mid LAD, and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) confirmed 360° circumferential calcium, a minimum lumen area of 3.35 mm², and failure of predilatation with a non-compliant balloon. Intravascular lithotripsy was performed using a 3.25 × 12 mm balloon, delivering 60 pulses at 6 atm. IVUS subsequently showed deep calcium fractures, enabling implantation of a drug-eluting stent and achieving 97% stent expansion, a final minimum lumen area of 12.56 mm², and an optimal angiographic result. This case highlights the role of intravascular lithotripsy integrated with intracoronary imaging in restoring vessel compliance and achieving adequate stent expansion in circumferential calcification that is not amenable to dilation with conventional strategies.
