abstract:
AIMS: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) may cause cardiotoxicity, mainly myocarditis, with potential life-threatening consequences. To date, large-scale prospective data on cardiac imaging after ICI are still lacking. Thus, our primary aim was to assess the diagnostic value of speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) for ICI-related cardiotoxicity according to current international recommendations, while our secondary aims were to assess the prognostic value of STE for adverse clinical outcome and evaluate the agreement between STE and CMR in patients with ICI-related myocarditis.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective study, cancer patients referred for cardiologic evaluation before ICIs initiation were enrolled. Patients with known cardiac dysfunction (LV ejection fraction < 40%) were excluded. All patients underwent clinical, biohumoral and echocardiographic evaluation completed by STE at baseline and at ∼6 months after immunotherapy. Patients with suspected myocarditis underwent CMR. Then, over a longer follow up, the clinical events were registered: all-cause or cardiovascular death, acute myocarditis, acute heart failure, pulmonary embolisms, acute coronary syndromes, atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, extra-cardiac toxicity. We enrolled 122 patients (65 ± 14 years) referred for ICIs. Over 7 ± 6 months follow up, mean LV GLS showed a slight reduction after therapy with ICI (-20 ± 4% at baseline vs. -18 ± 7%), although remaining within the normal ranges. During 22 ± 17 months of follow up, 65 patients developed events. Among ICI-related myocarditis, 4 patients showed a significant reduction of GLS with a regional distribution similar to regional myocardial injury at CMR (97 ± 7% agreement), the fifth had a minimal involvement of the right ventricle, with normal LV GLS.
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that multimodality imaging combining different techniques may optimize the subclinical diagnosis of cardiotoxicity and the overall management of cancer patients undergoing ICIs.
title: Multimodality imaging for the detection of cardiotoxicity in cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.

abstract: Heart failure is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Patients with acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, and end-stage chronic heart failure may benefit from a variety of device therapies. These devices may serve as a rescue, a bridge to recovery, a bridge to further therapy, or heart replacement therapy. The appropriate utilization of these devices is an ongoing area of research. In this review, we provide an overview of the available literature for device therapy in both the acute and chronic heart failure settings. We will present landmark trials, guidelines, and ongoing areas of research. Our goal is to aid in the appropriate selection of both devices and patients who will benefit.
journal: The International journal of angiology : official publication of the International College of Angiology, Inc
title: Device Therapy in Heart Failure.

abstract: Background Breathlessness is a leading cause of emergency hospital attendances, and its multifactorial nature often reflects overlapping cardiopulmonary pathologies such as pulmonary embolism (PE), heart failure (HF), and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is frequently used, often without documented pretest probability assessments. This audit primarily assessed the diagnostic yield of CTPA for suspected PE against the Royal College of Radiologists (RCR) standard of ≥15% and secondarily described biomarker testing, imaging, and outcomes across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways in patients referred to cardiology with acute breathlessness. Methods We conducted a retrospective audit of 70 adults referred to cardiology with breathlessness through the electronic patient record or multiprofessional team list (MPTL) referral systems at a district general hospital in the United Kingdom between March 1 and June 30, 2025. Biomarker testing for D-dimer, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and high-sensitivity troponin I (hs-TnI), together with imaging and outcomes, was reviewed and described across the PE, HF, and ACS pathways, with diagnostic yields restricted to CTPA for suspected PE and coronary angiography for suspected ACS. Yields were reported with Wilson 95% CIs and compared using exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Additional analyses examined biomarker concentrations by outcome and overlap in biomarker and imaging use. Results Seventy patients were included (median age, 69.5 years; 52.9% male). D-dimer, NT-proBNP, and hs-TnI were tested in 68.6%, 58.6%, and 81.4% of patients, respectively. Overall, seven of 54 CTPAs performed for suspected PE were positive (13.0%, 95% CI, 6.4-24.4), numerically below the RCR benchmark of ≥15%. A clinically relevant alternative diagnosis was reported in 44.4% (target, ≥50%), and pretest probability was documented in 22.2% (target, 100%). PE yield was 15.0% (6/40) among patients with an elevated D-dimer, 0% (0/4) among those with a normal D-dimer, and 10.0% (1/10) among those without D-dimer testing (p = 1.000 for both comparisons). Left ventricular systolic dysfunction (LVSD) was found on transthoracic echocardiography in 40.0% (8/20) of patients with elevated NT-proBNP, 23.1% (3/13) of those with non-elevated NT-proBNP, and 26.3% (5/19) of those without testing (p = 0.456 and p = 0.501, respectively). Of 47 patients with elevated hs-TnI, 10 (21.3%) underwent coronary angiography for suspected ACS, with percutaneous coronary intervention performed in four (40.0%). Overall, 29 of 57 patients tested (50.9%) had hs-TnI levels above the sex-specific 99th-percentile upper reference limit. Conclusions Cardiology-referred breathlessness frequently involved multiple biomarker and imaging pathways during the same admission. CTPA yield, alternative diagnosis rates, and pretest probability documentation fell below RCR standards. LVSD was more frequent with elevated NT-proBNP, although differences were not statistically significant. No hs-TnI comparison was possible because all patients undergoing angiography for suspected ACS had elevated levels. Given the small, single-center sample and selective imaging, these findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy or pathway effectiveness. Larger multicenter studies are needed. The findings support reviewing pretest probability documentation and investigation decisions, followed by reaudit against RCR standards.
title: Biomarker Testing, Imaging, and Outcomes in Cardiology-Referred Acute Breathlessness: A Retrospective Clinical Audit.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hybrid coronary revascularization (HCR) is minimally invasive coronary artery bypass surgery in patients with multivessel disease. This study compared the clinical outcomes of robot-assisted HCR patients with those receiving conventional on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in the Netherlands.
METHODS: We included 117 HCR and 2,160 CABG patients between January 2015 and December 2021. We performed a 1:3 propensity score matching (PSM) analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) at ≤30 days of follow-up. Secondary outcomes included red blood cell transfusions, length of stay, and the individual components of MACCE, which were mortality, perioperative myocardial infarction, revascularization of the target vessel (TVR), kidney failure, and in-hospital ischemic cerebrovascular accidents. Mortality and TVR at midterm follow-up were also included.
RESULTS: After PSM, 115 HCR and 342 on-pump CABG patients were included. HCR patients underwent a mean ± standard deviation of 1 ± 0 distal anastomosis, whereas CABG patients had a mean of 3.6 ± 1.1 distal anastomoses. At ≤30 days of follow-up, no differences in MACCE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.27, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.48 to 2.88, P = 0.57) or in the individual secondary outcomes were found. HCR resulted in a shorter hospital stay (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.99 to 1.0, P = 0.02). At a median of 35 months (interquartile range [IQR], 23 to 45) of follow-up in the HCR group and 34 months (IQR, 22 to 45) in the CABG group, all-cause mortality and TVR did not differ.
CONCLUSIONS: HCR provides excellent short-term and midterm outcomes, comparable to conventional CABG, while also offering faster recovery.
title: Hybrid Coronary Revascularization Versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: The Dutch Experience.

abstract: This protocol describes a pulmonary artery thrombectomy technique that combines stent deployment and negative pressure aspiration to achieve rapid thrombus removal and restore pulmonary arterial perfusion. Prolonged obstruction may lead to right heart dysfunction and hemodynamic instability. The pulmonary artery thrombectomy stent system provides a rapid approach to thrombus removal and restoration of pulmonary perfusion, thereby alleviating respiratory distress and hypoxemia while reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular strain. This technique is applicable for patients with intermediate- to high-risk pulmonary embolism, particularly those with contraindications to thrombolysis. Preoperative computed tomography imaging revealed pulmonary artery emboli involving both the left and right pulmonary arteries and their branches. Following thrombectomy using the pulmonary artery interventional thrombectomy stent system, postoperative imaging confirmed complete clearance of the thrombi and full restoration of pulmonary artery blood flow.
title: Pulmonary Artery Interventional Thrombectomy Stent System: Combined Application of Stent and Negative Pressure Aspiration.

abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a leading cardiovascular event, yet the metabolic signatures that precede its onset and their value for long-term risk prediction remain incompletely characterized. Using NMR metabolomics data from 271 430 UK Biobank participants without baseline AMI, this study evaluated 168 absolute metabolite measures in relation to incident AMI. Cox proportional hazards models identified 60 AMI-associated metabolites after adjustment for conventional risk factors, and CatBoost modeling with SHAP interpretation and forward selection further defined eight metabolite profiles, including glycine, albumin, glycoprotein acetyls, creatinine, triglycerides in large LDL, free cholesterol in chylomicrons and extremely large VLDL (XXL-VLDL-FC), cholesteryl esters in IDL, and cholesteryl esters in HDL. Integrating these metabolite profiles with conventional risk factors modestly improved 10-year AMI discrimination in both machine learning and survival models, with a CatBoost AUC of 0.741 and a Cox C index of 0.761 in validation analyses. SHAP analyses suggested sex- and age-related heterogeneity in metabolite contributions, particularly for HDL-related and inflammatory traits. A nested case-control trajectory analysis showed persistently lower levels of glycine and albumin, and higher levels of glycoprotein acetyls, large LDL triglycerides, and creatinine during the decade before diagnosis. This study identifies NMR-derived metabolic patterns associated with AMI risk and provides a basis for further investigation of their potential contributions to metabolomics-informed cardiovascular risk assessment.
title: NMR-Derived Metabolic Profiles Associated with Incident Acute Myocardial Infarction and Pre-Diagnostic Metabolic Trajectories in the UK Biobank.
Transcatheter Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Mitral valve-in-valve procedures are generally associated with a lower risk of LVOTO because of the predictable geometry provided by the surgical bioprosthesis, yet severe obstruction may still occur and precipitate abrupt hemodynamic collapse.
CASE: A 79-year-old woman with a degenerated 27-mm Carpentier-Edwards Perimount mitral bioprosthesis presented with acute decompensated heart failure due to severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Following multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, she was considered not a candidate for redo mitral valve surgery and underwent urgent transseptal valve-in-valve TMVR with a 26-mm balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve.
INTERVENTION: Immediately after valve deployment, severe LVOTO developed, with an invasive peak-to-peak LV-aortic gradient of 120 mmHg. A mechanism-guided percutaneous rescue strategy was undertaken. Correction of the structural component of obstruction reduced the gradient to 60 mmHg. Persistent obstruction suggested a significant dynamic contribution, prompting selective septal branch coil embolization, which further reduced the gradient to 20 mmHg and resulted in immediate hemodynamic stabilization.
CONCLUSION: Severe LVOTO after valve-in-valve TMVR may reflect both structural and dynamic mechanisms. Persistence of significant obstruction after structural correction should prompt consideration of a dynamic component and may guide effective rescue therapy.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Percutaneous Rescue of Acute Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction After Mitral Valve-In-Valve Replacement.

abstract: RotaWire delivery can be challenging in severely calcified device-uncrossable coronary lesions when conventional wire exchange through a microcatheter is not feasible. We report a 76-year-old man with a severely calcified mid-left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) lesion in which neither a microcatheter nor a 0.75 mm balloon could cross. A second channel was created using a penetration wire through a dual-lumen microcatheter, allowing direct RotaWire crossing. However, the RotaWire could not be advanced sufficiently into the distal LAD. After intentional proximal pullback of the dual-lumen microcatheter, the microcatheter and RotaWire were held together and advanced as a single unit, enabling adequate distal RotaWire positioning and successful rotational atherectomy. This case highlights a distinct challenge after successful direct RotaWire crossing and demonstrates coupled advancement with a dual-lumen microcatheter as a potential bailout technique when distal RotaWire advancement remains difficult.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: When the RotaWire Crosses but Cannot Advance: Dual-Lumen Microcatheter-Assisted RotaWire Delivery.

abstract: Coronary obstruction is a rare but catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) associated with high mortality. While acute and delayed presentations have distinct pathophysiological mechanisms, their occurrence in the same patient is exceedingly rare. We present a unique case of a 91-year-old female who developed acute left main coronary artery (LMCA) obstruction immediately following native TAVI using a balloon-expandable valve, which was successfully treated with bail-out percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Three months later (> 60 days, classified as "Very Late" coronary obstruction), she presented with severe angina and heart failure. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed extrinsic compression of the previously implanted coronary stent caused by a localized aortic wall hematoma. A repeat PCI with a stent-in-stent technique restored coronary flow, leading to complete clinical recovery. This case expands the known mechanical spectrum of very late coronary obstruction according to recent classification frameworks and highlights the vital role of intravascular imaging and multimodality assessment in diagnosis and management.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Sequential Coronary Obstruction After Native TAVI: Immediate Acute Occlusion and Very Late Stent Compression by Aortic Wall Hematoma.

abstract: Vasospastic angina can cause myocardial infarction and malignant ventricular arrhythmias, but a persistent coronary occlusion in a patient with established vasospasm creates an acute diagnostic and procedural dilemma. A man with recurrent troponin-positive presentations and prior non-obstructive coronary angiography developed 99% mid-left anterior descending artery narrowing in 2024 that markedly regressed after intracoronary nitrate; ergonovine provocation was subsequently positive. In April 2026, at age 42, he presented with anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction after irregular use of vasodilator therapy. Angiography showed total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery at the previously nitrate-responsive segment. Intracoronary nitrate did not restore flow, and ventricular fibrillation occurred during the procedure. Bailout drug-eluting stent implantation restored flow. A proximal right coronary artery occlusion was also identified during the same procedure and treated with stenting. In June 2026, angiographically confirmed stent thrombosis required repeat percutaneous coronary intervention; an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was subsequently implanted after multidisciplinary review. This case highlights the need to consider superimposed thrombotic or structural mechanisms when coronary occlusion in a patient with established vasospastic angina does not resolve after intracoronary nitrate. Bailout revascularization may be necessary when flow cannot be restored in a hemodynamically unstable patient, but it does not eliminate the underlying vasomotor disorder.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: High-Risk Vasospastic Angina With Recurrent Ischemic and Arrhythmic Events: A Case Report.

abstract: Oral anticoagulation has a very strong evidence base for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at elevated thromboembolic risk. Direct oral anticoagulants have improved the safety and convenience of treatment, yet important limitations remain, including residual ischaemic stroke, major bleeding, treatment discontinuation, and patient refusal. Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) offers an alternative strategy for selected patients by excluding the principal anatomical source of AF-related cardiac thrombi. However, the appropriate role of LAAC remains controversial, particularly in patients who can and do tolerate anticoagulation. This viewpoint argues for a more individualized approach that distinguishes absolute contraindications from modifiable bleeding risks, treatment refusal or non-persistence, and stroke occurring despite adequate anticoagulation.
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
title: Beyond anticoagulation: defining the role of left atrial appendage closure in stroke prevention for atrial fibrillation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.
METHODS: This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.
RESULTS: Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.
CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.
title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Characteristics of future culprit lesions according to artificial intelligence-guided quantitative computed tomography (AI-QCT) are unknown.
OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to characterize and derive thresholds to predict future culprit lesions from coronary computed tomography angiography using AI-QCT.
METHODS: A total of 2,169 patients/13,772 lesions undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography at Turku University Hospital, Finland, (derivation) and 553 patients/3,948 lesions from Amsterdam University Medical Center, the Netherlands, (validation) were analyzed with AI-QCT. Lesions from vessels undergoing early revascularization were excluded. Lesion-level total plaque volume (TPV) and noncalcified plaque volume (NCPV) thresholds were derived and externally validated to predict lesion-level and patient-level acute coronary syndrome (ACS).
RESULTS: Future culprit lesions from both cohorts (n = 69 validation; n = 15 derivation) had consistently higher median TPV (101 mm3 validation; 115 mm3 derivation; P = 0.811) and NCPV (65 mm3 validation; 74 mm3 derivation; P = 0.709) compared with control lesions (P < 0.001) and were nonobstructive in 69.6% (derivation) and 40.0% (validation). Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived and associated with significantly higher adjusted rates of lesion-level (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 12.09; 95% CI: 6.95-21.04; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 10.82; 95% CI: 6.22-18.80; P < 0.001) and patient-level ACS (TPV ≥55 mm3: adjusted HR: 2.92; 95% CI: 1.65-5.16; P < 0.001; NCPV ≥32 mm3: adjusted HR: 5.11; 95% CI: 2.49-10.46; P < 0.001) with consistent results in the validation cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.
title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
14-Year Serial Optical Frequency Domain Imaging After Absorb Bioresorbable Vascular Scaffold Implantation.
Percutaneous Pulmonary Thrombectomy for Massive Fat Embolism Syndrome Following Abdominoplasty: The Dark Side of Esthetic Surgery.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular leak (PVL) after surgical mitral valve replacement is an uncommon but clinically significant complication. Redo surgery carries a high risk, making transcatheter closure a viable and less invasive alternative.
CASE SUMMARY: We report 2 cases of mitral PVL following prior surgical valve replacement who presented with signs and symptoms of heart failure. After echocardiographic evaluation, a transcatheter approach was undertaken to deploy a Konar-multifunctional (MF) ventricular septal defect (VSD) occluder under fluoroscopic guidance. Following the procedure, both patients showed significant clinical improvement with complete resolution of PVL.
DISCUSSION: This case series emphasizes the feasibility and favorable outcome of transcatheter closure using the Konar-MF VSD occluder, off-label as an alternative to redo surgery in high-risk surgical patients with mitral PVL. Larger studies are warranted to evaluate the safety and efficacy of this off-label approach across a broader patient population.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: New-onset symptoms of heart failure and hemolytic anemia even after years of surgical mitral valve replacement warrant careful and timely evaluation for PVLs. In select high-risk patients who are not ideal candidates for redo surgery, off-label use of the Konar-MF VSD occluder is a feasible alternative for closure of PVLs.
title: Transcatheter Mitral Paravalvular Leak Closure With a Multifunctional Ventricular Septal Defect Occluder.
Blue Babies Grown Old: Aspirational Care for an Older Patient With ACHD.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a stepwise dual-device bailout strategy for posterior leaflet perforation during mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
KEY STEPS: After a new high-velocity leaflet-body jet was identified, direct annular-side resealing was infeasible because tissue between the perforation and annular hinge was minimal. A first PASCAL ACE device was implanted lateral to the perforation to eliminate residual lateral mitral regurgitation and shorten the anteroposterior diameter, approximating the basal leaflet segments. A second device was advanced medially with a reduced opening angle to avoid posterior left ventricular wall interference and achieve deep near-annular sealing.
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Perforation-associated jets may be mistaken for residual coaptation-line mitral regurgitation, and repeated regrasping may fail or worsen leaflet injury when annular-side tissue is insufficient.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: When direct resealing is not feasible, valve geometry modification with a first device may facilitate definitive sealing with a second device.
title: Leaflet Perforation During Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Stepwise Dual-Device Strategy Leveraging Valve Geometry Modification.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) diagnosis in adulthood is often delayed and can lead to severe coronary sequelae.
CASE SUMMARY: A 23-year-old man who first developed clinical manifestations of KD at age 18 years developed a medium-sized coronary artery aneurysm because of delayed initial treatment. Antithrombotic therapy, including warfarin, was prescribed but later discontinued during follow-up. At age 23 years, he presented with acute myocardial infarction complicated by lethal ventricular arrhythmias requiring mechanical circulatory support. Emergency coronary angiography revealed concurrent thrombotic occlusions of the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries. Emergent percutaneous coronary intervention of both vessels restored coronary flow, resulting in favorable neurologic and clinical recovery.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights that interruption of antithrombotic therapy in patients with KD-related coronary aneurysms may precipitate catastrophic multivessel thrombosis.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patients with persistent KD-related coronary artery aneurysms require follow-up and antithrombotic therapy tailored to thrombotic risk.
title: Catastrophic Multivessel Coronary Thrombosis After Discontinuation of Antithrombotic Therapy in Adult-Onset Kawasaki Disease.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We describe mechanical leaflet traversal as an alternative to electrosurgical traversal for BICORN during valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a patient with unfavorable cardiac orientation and extreme bilateral coronary obstruction risk.
KEY STEPS: The ShortCut device created targeted basal splits in both coronary leaflets. The left coronary cusp split was crossed using a Pilot 100 guidewire (Abbott) and microcatheter with an EBU 3.5 guide catheter (Medtronic) and Agilis steerable introducer (Abbott) support. After balloon dilation, the left coronary cusp was translocated with an 18-mm True Dilatation Balloon (BD). A 20-mm SAPIEN 3 Ultra transcatheter heart valve (Edwards Lifesciences) was then advanced through the right coronary cusp split and deployed within the pre-existing 23-mm SAPIEN 3 valve (Edwards Lifesciences).
POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Mechanical traversal requires precise targeting. Leaflet translocation may cause embolization, severe aortic insufficiency, or hemodynamic compromise, requiring readiness for immediate valve deployment.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Mechanical traversal may facilitate BICORN when cardiac rotation, unfavorable catheter trajectory, neosinus malalignment, eccentric coronary takeoffs, or leaflet fibrocalcification make electrosurgical traversal challenging.
title: First-in-Human Mechanical Bilateral Iatrogenic Coronary Leaflet Obstruction Risk Nullification (BICORN) for Transcatheter Aortic Valve-in-Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bioprosthetic aortic valve degeneration can present as isolated regurgitant failure, and an eccentric jet may raise the transmitral gradient, mimicking mitral stenosis.
CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man presented with acute heart failure 12 years after surgical aortic valve replacement. Echocardiography showed a degenerated Trifecta bioprosthesis with an immobile leaflet causing severe eccentric aortic regurgitation, whose jet impinged on the anterior mitral leaflet and produced severe functional mitral stenosis. Given high surgical risk, the heart team performed transfemoral valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
DISCUSSION: Trifecta leaflet tear causes regurgitant rather than stenotic failure; an eccentric jet can raise the transmitral gradient independent of the Austin Flint murmur. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement eliminated the regurgitation, improved leaflet mobility, and reduced the mean mitral gradient from 17 to 6 mm Hg, with complete symptom resolution.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Eccentric aortic regurgitation can cause a reversible rise in transmitral gradient; treating it can resolve apparent mitral stenosis without mitral intervention.
title: Dynamic Transmitral Gradient From Eccentric Aortic Regurgitation Resolved by Valve-in-Valve TAVR.

abstract: A 76-year-old woman noticed reduced vision with a central scotoma in her left eye one week after coronary angiography for angina pectoris. Best-corrected visual acuity in the left eye was 0.5. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed a hyperreflective lesion of the inner nuclear layer inferior to the macula, and paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) was diagnosed. OCT angiography was unremarkable in the acute phase. Fluorescein angiography revealed delayed arterial perfusion inferior to the macula, consistent with a transient branch retinal artery occlusion. Cardiovascular work-up showed carotid stenosis and dyslipidemia; lipid-lowering therapy was intensified. After 3 months, visual acuity in the left eye was 1.0, but a central scotoma persisted. OCT showed atrophy of the inner nuclear and outer plexiform layers, and OCT angiography showed capillary rarefaction of the deep capillary plexus. PAMM is a rare complication of coronary angiography. In patients with a new central scotoma after cardiac catheterization, PAMM should be considered and a comprehensive cardiovascular work-up initiated.
title: [Paracentral acute middle maculopathy after transient branch retinal artery occlusion following coronary angiography].

abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders. A multidisciplinary Heart Team is essential to ensure the clinical success of TMVR, and imaging specialists play a central role in the preprocedural assessment for patient and device selection, during the procedure, to guide and monitor the implantation, and after the procedure, for follow-up and for the correct diagnosis of short- or long-term complications. Echocardiography is required for initial diagnosis, for assessment of valve hemodynamics, intraprocedural guidance and monitoring. However, a multimodality approach including CT and/or MRI is frequently needed to correctly manage the phase of preprocedural planning and the diagnosis of complications. This consensus document, developed by a working group of experts from the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI), provides evidence-based recommendations for CT and cardiac MRI acquisition and post-processing in procedural planning and postprocedural evaluation in patients undergoing TMVR. Emphasis is placed on the technical requirements and standardization of imaging protocols, which must account for the heterogeneity of imaging equipment used in clinical settings. The document also outlines recommendations for all necessary preprocedural measures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and effective communication among specialists. KEY POINTS: Question How can CT and MRI acquisition, measurement, and reporting for TMVR be standardized to support accurate procedural planning, device selection, and follow-up? Findings This expert consensus provides recommendations for standardized CT and MRI protocols, key measurements, and structured reporting throughout TMVR planning and follow-up. Clinical relevance CT and MRI assessment may improve patient selection, procedural planning, multidisciplinary communication, and detection of postprocedural complications, supporting safer and more consistent TMVR practice across centers.
title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) remains a commonly used temporary mechanical circulatory support device because it is relatively easy to implant, less invasive, and well established in clinical practice. Previous studies have focused primarily on the physiological mechanisms, indications, clinical outcomes, and complications of IABP, whereas its technological evolution and industrial research have not been systematically examined.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize the global technological and industrial evolution of IABP; identify current research priorities and underdeveloped areas; and relate patent innovation to unresolved needs in hemodynamic support, vascular safety, counterpulsation accuracy, prolonged bridging, and patient transport.
METHODS: Patent documents related to IABP were retrieved from the PatSnap database using a combined search strategy based on keywords and International Patent Classification (IPC) codes. The search was limited to documents published by August 18, 2026. After screening and deduplication, simple patent families were used as the unit of analysis. Patentometric analysis and technology function matrix analysis were performed to characterize the technological evolution, geographical distribution, and major innovation directions of IABP technology.
RESULTS: A total of 1235 IABP-related patent families were identified. The United States, China, Japan, and Europe were the principal countries or regions of origin, together accounting for 89.1% (1100/1235) of the included simple patent families. China contributed 326 simple patent families, representing 26.4% of the global total, and showed particularly rapid growth over the past 5 years. IABP technology evolved through an embryonic stage (1968-1985), a steady development stage (1986-2012), and a rapid development stage beginning in 2013. Patent families were mainly classified as balloon components (n=552, 44.7%), catheters and accessories (n=416, 33.7%), and counterpulsation timing and control (n=161, 13%). The technology function matrix indicated that structural optimization and control precision are the current priorities in research and development, while balloon folding and compression, fiber-optic pressure sensing, and adaptive control algorithms have emerged as important hotspots.
CONCLUSIONS: IABP innovation has focused on balloon catheter design, pressure sensing, and adaptive control to improve hemodynamic support and counterpulsation accuracy. However, safety and complication reduction remain underdeveloped, particularly for prolonged support and transport. Future systems should integrate durable, low-profile designs with sensing, adaptive timing, and failure monitoring and be evaluated in specific patient populations and clinical settings.
title: Trends in Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Technology: Patentometric Analysis.

abstract: Right heart failure (RHF) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs). While right coronary artery infarction is a recognized cause of acute RHF, the ventricular consequences of left coronary system infarction in LVAD-supported patients are not well characterized. We describe two patients supported with HeartMate III LVADs who developed acute RHF within 24-48 hours after successful revascularization of acute left coronary system occlusions (mid-left anterior descending artery and left main coronary artery). Both had previously stable LVAD function and no evidence of advanced RHF. After revascularization, each developed hypotension, rising central venous pressure, reduced LVAD flows, and echocardiographic evidence of severe right ventricular (RV) dilation and dysfunction with septal shift toward the left ventricle. Hemodynamic deterioration reversed with inotropic support, diuresis, and LVAD speed adjustment, without mechanical RV support. These cases suggest left coronary acute myocardial infarction (AMI) may precipitate acute RHF in LVAD-supported patients through septal ischemia with impaired ventricular interdependence, acute increases in RV afterload, and relative RV ischemia despite patent right coronary arteries. Heightened surveillance and early echocardiographic assessment after left-sided AMI in LVAD recipients may enable prompt recognition and timely intervention.
journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
title: Acute Right Heart Failure Following Left Coronary Myocardial Infarction in Left Ventricular Assist Device-Supported Patients: A Case Series and Mechanistic Insight.
A Natural Occluder? Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation With Congenital Absence of the Left Atrial Appendage.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a nontraumatic, noniatrogenic dissection of a coronary artery.
OBJECTIVE: This narrative review provides emergency clinicians with a focused overview of the presentation, evaluation, and management of SCAD.
DISCUSSION: SCAD is an underrecognized and potentially deadly disease that can result in coronary artery occlusion and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). It traditionally affects young-to-middle aged females, with increased risk in the peripartum period. Patients with SCAD most commonly present with signs and symptoms consistent with ACS, and a significant proportion of patients will have ST elevation myocardial infarction on electrocardiogram. Emergent cardiology consultation for angiography is necessary for diagnosis. Following diagnosis, a conservative approach is often followed, as most lesions heal spontaneously without intervention. Revascularization in the form of percutaneous coronary artery intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting is necessary in those with ongoing or recurrent ischemia with electrocardiogram or troponin changes, hemodynamic instability, ventricular dysrhythmias, or dissection of the left main coronary artery. Patients can have recurrence of SCAD, and noninvasive imaging modalities, such as coronary computed tomography, may be considered to diagnose recurrence.
CONCLUSIONS: Emergency physicians should consider SCAD in patients presenting with ACS, particularly younger women and those without traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Early recognition and prompt consultation with cardiology to guide selection of conservative vs. revascularization strategies are essential to optimize patient outcomes.
title: Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection: An Emergency Medicine-Focused Narrative Review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: In adolescents with high-energy blunt chest trauma, electrocardiography (ECG) findings suggestive of myocardial infarction together with markedly elevated cardiac enzymes should raise immediate suspicion for traumatic coronary artery dissection (TCAD).
CASE REPORT: We report the case of a 16-year-old male who sustained blunt chest trauma in an electric bicycle accident. During venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support, non-ECG-gated contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) was performed. Thin-slice (1.25 mm) delayed-phase images incidentally revealed a double-lumen sign from the left main coronary artery to the proximal left anterior descending artery, along with diffuse myocardial hypoperfusion. These findings prompted angiographic confirmation and urgent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). WHY SHOULD AN EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN BE AWARE OF THIS?: This case highlights that, in hemodynamically unstable trauma patients, when ECG-gated coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) is not feasible, careful evaluation of routinely obtained contrast-enhanced CT images, particularly coronary root morphology and myocardial perfusion, may provide critical diagnostic clues to this life-threatening condition.
title: Traumatic Left Main Coronary Artery-Left Anterior Descending Artery Dissection in an Adolescent: A Case Report.

abstract:
AIM: Despite RapidAI's widescale adoption for acute stroke management, gaps remain in validating its real-world diagnostic impact. Given local observations of RapidAI overestimating infarct size for equivalent images, we evaluated the reliability of RapidAI versus neuroradiologists at a Canadian comprehensive stroke centre.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Computed tomography (CT) head and carotid studies (Jan 2020-Aug 2021) from acute stroke activations were retrospectively reviewed. Repeat presentations, no follow-up imaging within 10 days, bilateral infarcts, non-middle cerebral artery (MCA) strokes, or haemorrhage were excluded. Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Scores (ASPECTS) from RapidAI and neuroradiologists were compared to follow-up magnetic resonance (MR) or CT imaging using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). A linear mixed-effect model was adjusted for age and sex. Subgroup analyses examined infarct burden and infarct location (cortical vs deep).
RESULTS: In total, 481 patients (49% female; median age: 74 years) were included. Neuroradiologists had higher agreement with the reference standard than RapidAI (ICC: 0.627 vs 0.546). RapidAI had a smaller adjusted difference (β = -0.10; P = 0.198) than neuroradiologists (β = 0.74; P < .001). Although agreement was poor across both groups, RapidAI showed higher agreement in extensive ischaemia (ASPECTS: 0-4: 0.194 vs 0.115; ASPECTS: 0-2: 0.083 vs 0.059), whereas neuroradiologists had higher agreement in threshold, ASPECTS: 5-7 cases (0.141 vs 0.068). Neuroradiologists showed superior agreement in deep infarcts (ICC: 0.612 vs 0.452).
CONCLUSION: Neuroradiologists maintain higher overall agreement in mid-range ASPECTS cases and deep infarcts, but RapidAI exhibited higher agreement in lower ASPECTS cases. RapidAI demonstrates context-dependent accuracy, serving as an adjunct requiring cautious use alongside neuroradiologist interpretation for clinical judgement.
title: RapidAI compared to RapidAI-assisted neuroradiologist interpretation in evaluating acute ischaemic stroke: A local experience.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral embolic protection (CEP) devices have been developed to reduce postoperative neurological outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI); however, their effectiveness remains controversial.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of CEP use during TAVI on the occurrence in clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Databases were used to search for randomized clinical trials. The occurrence of all strokes, of disabling strokes specifically, transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), all-cause mortality, and vascular complications were analyzed. Conventional meta-analysis was conducted using fixed-effects modeling and trial sequential analysis (TSA: type I error of 5%, power of 90%). The systematic review protocol was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420251081075).
RESULTS: In total, eight clinical trials were included, gathering 11,589 patients randomized between those who used the devices (5,943) and those who did not (5,646). The meta-analysis demonstrated no significant association between CEP use and reduced odds of all-cause stroke (OR = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.73-1.15, p = 0.46) and disabling stroke (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.57-1.13, p = 0.20). The sequential analysis identified a lack of evidence for all strokes (required sample size [rSS] = 38,626; 10.53%), disabling strokes (rSS = 59,732; 17.05%). In terms of mortality, there was no significance in the use of devices (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.71-1.69, p = 0.69), reaching evidence for support (rSS = 7,053; 42.25%).
CONCLUSION: The data on the use of CEP is insufficient to support meta-analytic conclusions regarding cerebrovascular outcomes. Nevertheless, TSA demonstrated evidence supporting futility regarding mortality reduction.
title: Safety and efficacy of cerebral embolic protection devices during TAVI: a meta-analysis and sequence analysis of trials.

abstract: Plasma ceramide levels are elevated in cardiovascular disease and predict recurrent adverse events and mortality after myocardial infarction (MI). However, mechanisms driving post-MI ceramide accumulation and pharmacologically actionable targets to counteract ceramide-driven myocardial damage are still lacking. Here, we identify FK506-binding protein 5 (FKBP5) as a druggable immunometabolic regulator of ceramide metabolism in cardiac macrophages, linking FKBP5 suppression to interrupted pathological crosstalk among sphingolipid remodeling, mitochondrial impairment and post-MI inflammatory injury. Using murine MI models and FKBP5-deficient cells, we examined FKBP5 inhibition or deficiency reduced infarct size and fibrosis, improved cardiac function, and protected against adverse remodeling. Mechanistically, FKBP5 was associated with the sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 3 (Smpd3) promoter region and contributed to the regulation of its transcriptional activity after MI, thereby promoting ceramide accumulation. Specifically, FKBP5-mediated ceramide 24:1 (Cer24:1) upregulation impaired mitochondrial redox homeostasis by disrupting electron transport chain integrity, thereby reinforcing M1 polarization and exacerbating myocardial injury. Elevated Cer24:1 directly bound the mitochondrial TU translation elongation factor (TUFM), disrupting electron transport chain integrity and mitochondrial respiration, providing a defined link between ceramide species and mitochondrial dysfunction. Notably, in vivo treatment with Cer24:1 attenuated the cardioprotective effects of FKBP5 inhibition after MI. Collectively, we describe a previously unrecognized FKBP5-Smpd3-Cer24:1-TUFM signaling axis in cardiac macrophages. FKBP5-governed ceramide metabolism drives macrophage immunometabolic reprogramming, marking FKBP5 as a promising pharmacological target for ischemic heart disease. Our findings support the role of the FKBP5-ceramide axis in mediating post-infarct myocardial dysfunction and highlight pharmacological FKBP5 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy against post-MI cardiac injury.
title: Targeting the FKBP5-ceramide axis driven mitochondrial reprogramming in cardiac macrophages attenuates post-infarct cardiac injury.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elderly patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma and cardiovascular disease are frequently treated with regimens incorporating non-PEGylated liposomal anthracycline to mitigate cardiotoxicity while preserving antitumor efficacy. However, considering their unique pharmacokinetics, validation of a cardiovascular risk stratification tool for these patients is much needed.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with newly diagnosed non-Hodgkin lymphoma treated with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, non-PEGylated liposomal doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone (R-COMP) between 2014 and 2025. Baseline demographics, cardiovascular history and medications, echocardiographic and laboratory parameters were recorded. Patients were stratified into risk categories according to the Heart Failure Association International Cardio-Oncology Society (HFA-ICOS) score. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS) and incidence of cardiovascular events defined as asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, new-onset or worsening heart failure and acute coronary syndrome.
RESULTS: The cohort consisted of 265 patients [median age 73 years (69-77); 51% males]; 41% were classified as moderate risk, 55% as high risk, and 4% as very high risk. During a median follow-up of 29 months, 38 patients (14%) died. OS and cardiovascular events occurrence significantly differed across the three HFA-ICOS risk categories; in particular, very high-risk patients exhibited substantially higher hazards of mortality (HR 5.8) and cardiovascular events (HR 40.4). Cardioprotective therapy at baseline appears not influence cardiovascular outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: The HFA-ICOS score effectively stratifies mortality and risk of cardiovascular events among patients treated with R-COMP. Despite the limited number of very-high risk patients and the heterogenous, non-randomized cardioprotective strategies at baseline, our findings may provide evidence supporting its integration into practice.
title: Cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing liposomal anthracycline: Association with cardiovascular outcomes and overall survival.
Antiplatelet pretreatment in acute coronary syndromes: Bridging the gap between guideline recommendations and clinical practice.
Secondary mitral regurgitation in HFrEF: Predicting reversibility on medical therapy before intervention.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries up to a 15% risk of complete heart block (CHB) within 30 days, but the mechanisms driving recurrent heart block after the apparent initial conduction system recovery post-TAVR remain incompletely understood. Phase 4 atrioventricular block, a pause-dependent phenomenon occurring when supraventricular or ventricular impulses encounter diseased His-Purkinje fibers during diastolic depolarization, may contribute to post-TAVR conduction disturbances. We present an instructive case of a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic valve stenosis who developed CHB in the setting of phase 4 atrioventricular block following TAVR. Despite recovering sinus rhythm with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction within 12 hours post-procedure, she experienced recurrent ventricular standstill upon temporary pacemaker removal, ultimately requiring permanent pacemaker implantation. This case illustrates the multiple mechanisms and temporal patterns of post-TAVR conduction system disorders, the potential unreliability of early apparent conduction recovery as a predictor of durable atrioventricular conduction, and the necessity for careful and more prolonged patient monitoring before and after temporary pacemaker removal.
title: Phase 4 Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Unmasking Latent Conduction Disease.
Association of pre-existing sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor therapy with outcomes in cardiogenic shock: a multicentre cohort study.

abstract: The study aimed to evaluate whether a half-dose heparin flush strategy during intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support improves safety compared with the standard-dose strategy in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 128 CS patients who received IABP support between January 2023 and December 2024 were included. Sixty-eight patients received a standard-dose heparin flush, and 60 received a half-dose flush. The primary endpoints were clinically relevant bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium 2, 3, or 5) and thrombocytopenia (platelet count < 100 × 109/L). Multivariable logistic regression was conducted, adjusting for dual antiplatelet therapy and renal dysfunction. The incidence of clinically significant bleeding events and thrombocytopenia was significantly lower in the half-dose group than in the standard-dose group (P < .05). Compared with the standard-dose group, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was significantly associated with a lower risk of clinically significant bleeding (odds ratio = 0.15; 95% confidence interval = 0.03-0.68). Among the secondary outcomes, the half-dose group had a significantly lower transfusion requirement than the standard-dose group (P < .001). No significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in activated partial thromboplastin time, activated clotting time, in-hospital mortality, or catheter-related occlusion events. In patients with CS receiving IABP support, the half-dose heparin flush strategy was associated with lower incidences of thrombocytopenia, clinical bleeding, and transfusion requirements. No device-related thrombotic events were observed in either group, suggesting that the half-dose heparin flush strategy may contribute to optimizing anticoagulation management during the peri-support period.
title: Comparison of anticoagulation efficacy and safety of different heparin dosages in cardiogenic shock patients supported by intra-aortic balloon pump: A retrospective cohort study.

abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that inflammatory mechanisms may play a key role in linking psychological disorders to cardiovascular outcomes. This study aimed to explore the association between anxiety and depression levels and two inflammatory markers, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI), in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS). This retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted on 1498 patients with ACS who underwent coronary angiography (CAG) in Rasht, Iran, between January 2022 and June 2023. SII and SIRI were calculated for all patients. Patients' psychological status regarding anxiety and depression was evaluated using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). All data analyses were conducted using SPSS version 22. The mean age of the patients was 58.49 ± 11.14 years, with males comprising 57.5% of the sample. Male participants exhibited significantly higher levels of anxiety and depression compared to females (P < .05). Individuals with comorbidities showed significantly lower anxiety scores (P < .05). Anxiety levels varied significantly based on CAG findings (P = .004). In multivariable ordinal logistic regression analyses, neither SII nor SIRI was significantly associated with depression severity (SII: OR = 1.029, 95% CI: 0.70-1.49; SIRI: OR = 1.012, 95% CI: 0.86-1.03) or anxiety severity (SII: OR = 0.906, 95% CI: 0.63-1.29; SIRI: OR = 1.005, 95% CI: 0.98-1.03). Systemic inflammation indices (SII and SIRI) did not show significant associations with anxiety or depression severity in cardiac patients, highlighting their limited utility as psychological predictors.
title: Association of SII and SIRI with anxiety and depression severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome: A retrospective cross-sectional study.

abstract: ABSTRACT Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered‐stent implantation can restore large‐bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon‐assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87‐year‐old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic‐isthmus stenosis with a peak‐to‐peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same‐session covered‐stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29‐mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18‐mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic‐valve predilation with a 23‐mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re‐expansion of the stent, a 23‐mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic‐isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon‐assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.
title: Covered‐Stent Migration During Same‐Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable‐polymer sirolimus‐eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM. Aims In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5‐year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus‐eluting stent (EES). Methods TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non‐stratified outcomes in DM versus non‐DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia‐driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis. Results Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non‐DM patients, TLF ( p < 0.001), cardiac death ( p < 0.001), TVMI ( p = 0.002), ischemia‐driven TLR ( p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis ( p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM. Conclusion This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.
title: Final 5‐Year Results of Abluminal Groove‐Filled Biodegradable‐Polymer Sirolimus‐Eluting Stent Versus Durable‐Polymer Everolimus‐Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dual‐lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid‐exchange (RX) port and an over‐the‐wire (OTW) port, within a single low‐profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non‐CTO lesions. Methods This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non‐CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations. Results Five applications are presented: (1) aorto‐ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side‐branch re‐entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions. Conclusions DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM‐assisted strategies in complex non‐CTO lesions.
title: Dual‐Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non‐CTO Lesions
