HTK was associated with a lower incidence of cardiac arrhythmia (OR 0.75; 95% CI 0.58-0.98; p=0.035; I 2 =0%) but a longer cardiopulmonary bypass time (MD 2.12 min; 95% CI 0.45-3.80; p=0.013; I 2 =40.3%). No significant differences were observed for all-cause mortality (OR 0.92; 95% CI 0.62-1.38; p=0.696; I 2 =0%), acute kidney injury requiring dialysis (OR 0.85; 95% CI 0.50-1.47; p=0.567), neurological complications (OR 0.94; 95% CI 0.57-1.57; p=0.817; I 2 =0%), postoperative atrial fibrillation (OR 0.56; 95% CI 0.25-1.28; p=0.170; I 2 =69.0%), or aortic cross-clamp time (MD 0.91 min; 95% CI –6.01 - 7.84; p=0.796; I 2 =96.5%). Conclusion: In this meta-analysis, HTK cardioplegia in heart valve surgery was associated with lower rates of cardiac arrhythmia, suggesting improved myocardial protection. However, HTK was associated with a slightly longer CPB time, with no significant benefits in major postoperative outcomes. Newer RCTs are still needed before any conclusions or recommendations can be drawn.
title: Abstract 15579: Clinical and Surgical Outcomes of Histidine-Tryptophan-Ketoglutarate versus Blood Cardioplegia in Valvular Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an alternative stroke-prevention strategy for selected patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but randomized comparisons with oral anticoagulation (OAC) or contemporary medical therapy have yielded mixed results across different control strategies and patient populations. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC or best medical care in adults with AF. Meta-analysis of five randomized studies analyzing 5,404 patients was performed using study-level, longest-follow-up event counts. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled Mantel-Haenszel risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for outcomes including all-cause mortality, cardiovascular or unexplained mortality, all stroke, ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding. Results: Across the analyzed populations, LAAC, compared with OAC, was associated with higher risk of ischemic stroke (RR 1.46, 95% CI 1.14-1.86; I 2 = 0%; p=0.01). No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups for all-cause death, cardiovascular or unexplained mortality, all stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, systemic embolism, and major bleeding. Conclusion: In randomized evidence, LAAC was associated with a higher risk of ischemic stroke than control therapy, while other hard clinical outcomes were not significantly different. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of trials, differing comparator strategies, nonuniform follow-up durations, and heterogeneity in endpoint definitions.
title: Abstract 15599: Left Atrial Appendage Closure versus Oral Anticoagulation or Medical Therapy in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is increasingly recognized in pediatric populations, particularly among children with congenital heart disease (CHD) and prior cardiac interventions. However, contemporary national data describing hospitalization trends and in-hospital outcomes among pediatric patients with AF in the United States remain limited. Aims: We aim to evaluate national trends in pediatric AF hospitalizations and identify predictors of major adverse in-hospital events (MAIE), mortality, healthcare utilization, and discharge outcomes using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS). Methods: We performed a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the NIS database from 2017 to 2022. Pediatric hospitalizations involving patients younger than 18 years with AF were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes. Hospitalizations involving atrial flutter or cardiac repair/replacement procedures were excluded. The primary outcome was MAIE, defined as a composite of in-hospital mortality, invasive mechanical ventilation, cardiac arrest, and cardiogenic shock. Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay, hospitalization costs, and non-home discharge. Survey-weighted regression models accounting for the complex NIS sampling design were used to assess temporal trends and predictors of adverse outcomes. Results: Among 3,650 weighted pediatric AF hospitalizations, AF hospitalization rates increased from 9.7 per 100,000 pediatric hospitalizations in 2017 to 13.3 per 100,000 in 2019 before stabilizing thereafter. The mean age was 12.0 years, 66% were male, and 17% had structural CHD. MAIE occurred in 16% of hospitalizations, without significant temporal change during the study period (p=0.11). In-hospital mortality increased significantly from 1.0% in 2017 to 6.6% in 2022 (p=0.009). Structural CHD was independently associated with higher odds of MAIE (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21-3.56, p=0.008), longer length of stay (β +4.5 days, p=0.024), and higher hospitalization costs (exp[β] 2.01, p<0.001). Younger age was associated with increased MAIE risk (OR 0.94 per year increase, 95% CI 0.91-0.98, p=0.001), while Medicaid insurance was associated with higher odds of MAIE compared with private insurance (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.03-2.84, p=0.040). Each successive study year was independently associated with increased odds of in-hospital mortality (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.03-1.74, p=0.030). Conclusions: Pediatric AF hospitalizations are associated with substantial morbidity and increasing in-hospital mortality, particularly among children with structural CHD. These findings highlight the growing national burden of pediatric AF and underscore the need for improved risk stratification, surveillance, and management strategies in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 15611: Atrial Fibrillation Admission Rates and Clinical Outcomes Among Children in the United States: A Nationwide Inpatient Sample Analysis (2017-2022)

abstract: Background: Patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain at high residual cardiovascular risk despite guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated cardiometabolic benefits, but their incremental role in patients already on quadruple GDMT remains poorly defined. We sought to evaluate cardiovascular outcomes associated with GLP-1RA use in this high-risk population. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global federated research network. Adult patients (≥18 years) with ischemic cardiomyopathy, HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%), T2DM, and BMI ≥27 kg/m 2 on quadruple GDMT (beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, SGLT2 inhibitor, and ACEi/ARB/ARNI) were identified. Patients receiving GLP-1RA therapy were compared with those not receiving GLP-1RA. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 1,075 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were assessed over 1 year and included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), heart failure exacerbation, atrial fibrillation/flutter, ventricular arrhythmias, and myocardial infarction (MI). Results: At 1 year, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly improved outcomes MACE 5.6% vs 15.7% (HR 3.15; p<0.001), Heart failure exacerbation: 14.2% vs 22.7% (HR 1.80; p=0.008), Atrial fibrillation/flutter 7.2% vs 11.1% (HR 1.65;p=0.015), Ventricular arrhythmias 6.5% vs 10.4% (HR 1.79; p=0.008), Myocardial infarction 4.6% vs 11.2% (HR 2.71; p=0.001), Kaplan-Meier analyses consistently demonstrated higher event-free survival in the GLP-1RA cohort across all endpoints. Conclusion: In patients with ischemic HFrEF and T2DM already receiving quadruple GDMT, the addition of GLP-1RA therapy is associated with significant reductions in major cardiovascular events at 1 year. These findings suggest a meaningful incremental benefit of GLP-1RA beyond contemporary GDMT, supporting further prospective evaluation of GLP-1RA as an adjunctive strategy in populations with advanced heart failure.
title: Abstract 15618: Incremental Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Therapy in Patients with HFrEF and Type 2 Diabetes on Quadruple GDMT

abstract: Background: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a non-atherosclerotic cause of myocardial infarction that predominantly affects young women. The complex genetic architecture of SCAD has a significant polygenic component, including loci with sex-specific associations. There is also evidence that SCAD genetic risk is inversely associated with risk of atherosclerosis. However, the phenotypic associations and sex-specific manifestations of SCAD polygenic risk are not fully understood. Hypothesis: We hypothesized that SCAD polygenic risk would be associated with cardiovascular conditions, including an inverse relationship with atherosclerotic disease, and would demonstrate sex-specific associations. Methods: We performed a phenome-wide association analysis in the UK Biobank using a SCAD polygenic risk score (PRS SCAD ) derived from a large meta-analysis. Phenotypes were defined using phecodes based on International Classification of Diseases codes. Associations were evaluated in combined-sex and sex-stratified analyses, and statistical significance was defined using Bonferroni correction. Enrichment analyses were performed using predefined phecode categories and Fisher’s Exact test with false discovery rate correction. Sex differences in PRS-phenotype associations, including category enrichment testing, were assessed using sex-heterogeneity z-statistics. Results: There were nine phenotypes that were significantly associated with the SCAD PRS after multiple testing correction (Figure A). Circulatory system phenotypes were enriched among significant associations (Figure B). SCAD polygenic risk demonstrated inverse associations with atherosclerotic phenotypes and positive associations with aneurysm phenotypes (Figure C). Migraine was also positively associated with SCAD polygenic risk, consistent with prior observations. Category enrichment testing of phenotypes meeting nominal significance for sex-heterogeneity demonstrated nominally significant enrichment of circulatory system phenotypes. In sex-stratified analyses, peripheral vascular disease demonstrated a stronger inverse association with SCAD polygenic risk in females than males (Figure C). Conclusion: SCAD polygenic risk is associated with a broader spectrum of vascular phenotype, including an inverse relationship with atherosclerotic disease. These findings support pleiotropic effects of SCAD genetic susceptibility and provide evidence for sex-dependent differences in vascular phenotype associations. Further studies are needed to define the biological mechanisms underlying these associations and their implications for vascular disease risk.
title: Abstract 15627: Phenome-Wide Analysis of SCAD Polygenic Risk Defines Vascular Pleiotropy and Sex-Specific Associations

abstract: Background: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a prevalent cause of angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Endothelium-independent CMD can be categorized using coronary flow reserve (CFR) and hyperemic microvascular resistance (hMR). Whether these phenotypes have a distinct long-term prognosis, specifically beyond endothelium-dependent function, remains unclear. Methods: Consecutive ANOCA patients with invasive Doppler-based coronary physiology were classified: Normal Endothelium-Independent Function (Normal EIF, CFR >2.5, hMR <2.5), Functional CMD (CFR ≤2.5, hMR <2.5), Structural CMD (CFR ≤2.5, hMR ≥2.5), and Normal-CFR High Resistance (CFR >2.5, hMR ≥2.5). hMR was calculated as mean aortic pressure during adenosine hyperemia divided by the hyperemic average peak velocity (MAP/hyperemic APV). MACE was all-cause death, heart failure (HF) hospitalization, nonfatal myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or revascularization. Sensitivity analyses were performed in patients with preserved endothelium-dependent vasodilation (coronary blood flow augmentation ≥50% with acetylcholine). Results: Among 2,002 patients (age 51.4±12.5 years, 66% female), 1,346 (67%) had Normal EIF, 554 (28%) had Functional CMD, 49 (2%) had Structural CMD, and 53 (3%) had Normal-CFR High Resistance. Structural and Normal-CFR High Resistance patients were older and more hypertensive, while the Normal-CFR High Resistance group had a lower proportion of women (all p≤0.01). Functional CMD demonstrated the highest resting average peak velocity (APV 30 [25–37] cm/s) compared with Structural CMD (19 [17–24] cm/s) and Normal-CFR High Resistance (15 [13–19] cm/s; p<0.001), consistent with differential resting flow states across endotypes. Over a median follow-up of 8.1 [3.2–14.9] years, Structural and Normal-CFR High Resistance groups had higher MACE (41.3% and 42.9% vs. 22.5%; p<0.001) and HF hospitalization (10.2% and 7.5% vs. 5.8%; p<0.001) compared to EIF, with Kaplan-Meier analysis confirming graded separation in event-free survival (log-rank p<0.001). Prognostic differences persisted in the endothelium-dependent vasodilation subgroup (MACE: 18.7%, 36.3%, 33.3%, 40.0%; p<0.001). Conclusions: CFR–hMR cross-classification identifies four prognostically distinct endotypes in ANOCA. The Normal-CFR High Resistance endotype carries a long-term MACE risk comparable to Structural CMD (~43%) and demonstrates that CFR alone systematically misclassifies this group as low risk. Prognostic differences persisted in preserved endothelium-dependent vasodilation. These findings support integrating resistance-based metrics alongside CFR and endothelial-dependent function in the physiological assessment of ANOCA and highlight the Normal-CFR High Resistance endotype as a potential target for future mechanism-guided therapeutic strategies.
title: Abstract 15628: Coronary Physiological Endotypes in Angina with Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries: Prevalence, Phenotypic Characterization, and Long-Term Prognosis

abstract: Background: Despite advances in drug-coated balloons and drug-eluting stents, restenosis remains a clinically relevant limitation of coronary and peripheral endovascular interventions. Thalidomide has anti-inflammatory, anti-angiogenic, and antiproliferative properties that may modulate vascular repair after arterial injury. We investigated whether localized intramural thalidomide delivery attenuates neointimal hyperplasia and adverse vascular remodeling after balloon angioplasty. Methods: Balloon injury was induced in iliac arteries of New Zealand White rabbits followed by local intramural administration of saline vehicle, dimethylformamide (DMF), thalidomide (1 mg/mL), or cycloheximide (0.5 mg/mL). At 21 days, histomorphometry, intima-to-media (I/M) ratio, extracellular matrix staining, and TUNEL assays were performed. Complementary in vitro studies evaluated proliferation, apoptosis, and cytotoxicity in primary rabbit vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Results: Balloon angioplasty induced progressive neointimal formation, with the I/M ratio increasing from 0.40±0.10 at day 7 to 1.54±0.18 at day 21 in vehicle-treated arteries. Local thalidomide significantly attenuated neointimal hyperplasia, reducing the I/M ratio by 46% from 1.37±0.15 in DMF controls to 0.74±0.12 (p=0.01), comparable to cycloheximide (0.66±0.11; p=0.01). Efficacy was achieved without significant necrotic cytotoxicity. Histology showed reduced neointimal thickness, decreased collagen and elastin accumulation, preserved luminal architecture, and maintained medial integrity without aneurysm formation or vessel wall injury. Mechanistic studies demonstrated marked suppression of VSMC proliferation. In cultured VSMCs, thalidomide reduced BrdU incorporation to 23±4% of control (p<0.05), corresponding to a 77% reduction in proliferation. Apoptosis increased concentration-dependently, reaching approximately 80% of the actinomycin-D positive control at the highest concentration. Both R- and S-thalidomide enantiomers produced comparable antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects. Therapeutic concentrations caused minimal LDH release (8±2.1% vs. 3±1.2% in controls; p>0.05), indicating preserved membrane integrity. In vivo TUNEL analyses showed low apoptotic activity across groups without significant differences. Conclusions: Localized thalidomide delivery significantly reduces neointimal hyperplasia and adverse vascular remodeling after balloon-induced arterial injury. The effect is associated with potent VSMC growth inhibition, favorable extracellular matrix remodeling, and programmed cell death without significant necrotic toxicity. These findings support further translational development of targeted vascular drug-delivery platforms.
title: Abstract 15631: Localized Thalidomide Delivery Reduces Neointimal Hyperplasia After Balloon Injury A Novel Strategy for Restenosis Prevention

abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) carries a high early mortality, approaching 50%, driven by inadequate cardiac output and end-organ hypoperfusion. Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) and inotropic agents work to restore tissue perfusion by augmenting cardiac output. Lactate, a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism, serves as a marker of hypoperfusion severity in CS - with elevated admission levels reflecting greater disease burden and failure of lactate clearance predicting worse outcomes. In patients with CS, what different trajectories of lactate clearance exist, and how do these phenotypes inform outcomes? We conducted a single-center cohort study of 887 patients with a primary diagnosis of CS, using manually reviewed, prospectively entered data. Patients with post-cardiotomy CS were excluded due to the fundamentally different origin and presentation of shock state. Lactate trajectories were identified using group-based trajectory modeling. Because the primary interest was the persistence of elevated lactate over time rather than absolute lactate values, lactate measurements were categorized as binary outcomes: elevated (>2 mmol/L) versus normal (≤2 mmol/L). Patients were required to have at least three lactate measurements available for inclusion in the trajectory analysis. The final model identified three distinct lactate status trajectories based on model fit, classification performance, and clinical interpretability. The identified trajectory groups were subsequently used to compare baseline characteristics, treatment patterns, and clinical outcomes. Three distinct phenotypes of lactate clearance are evident in patients with CS: those who present with an initial elevated lactate and do not quickly clear (high-persistent); those who present with an initial elevated lactate and quickly clear (high-resolving); and those who have a low-level lactatemia that remains low (low stable). Predictably, patients with low-stable lactatemia and those with high-resolving lactatemia had lower in-hospital mortality when compared to the high-persistent cohort (17.67% and 26.98% vs 55.78% p<0.001). In patients with CS, phenotypes of low-stable lactatemia and high-resolving lactatemia portend a more favorable prognosis when compared to patients with high-persistent lactatemia.
title: Abstract 15643: Phenotyping Lactate in Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background: Current guidelines support the use of left ventricular unloading (LVU) in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS); however the clinical benefits of routine LV unloading during percutaneous intervention (PCI) in STEMI remains uncertain. Objectives: We aim to evaluate clinical outcomes of percutaneous LV unloading in addition to PCI compared with PCI alone in patients with STEMI without cardiogenic shock. Methods: We searched PUBMED, Embase and Cochrane for studies comparing LVU plus PCI versus PCI alone in STEMI patients without CS. The main outcomes were all-cause mortality (ACM), infarct size, major bleeding and TIMI-3 flow. Statistical analysis was performed using R software 4.5.1. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics. Results: We included 1501 patients from 5 RCTs. 736 (49.0%) patients were treated with LVU plus PCI. There was no significant difference in ACM (RR 0.79; 95% CI 0.46-1.37; p = 0.345; I 2 = 0%), TIMI-3 flow (RR 1.02; 95% CI 0.97-1.08; p = 0.407; I2 = 40.9%) or Infarct size (as percentage of LV mass) between the two groups (MD 1.34; 95% CI -4.19 to 6.87; p = 0.066; I 2 = 70.4%). LVU showed nonsignificant trend toward increase in major bleeding in the LVU group (RR 2.68; 95% CI 0.96-7.47; p = 0.0597; I 2 =88.0%;). Conclusion: In this RCT-only meta-analysis, LVU with PCI in STEMI was not associated with significant improvements in mortality, TIMI-3 flow, or infarct size. However, LVU demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward increased major bleeding.
title: Abstract 15653: Left Ventricular Unloading with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention versus Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Alone in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Without Cardiogenic Shock: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: Early restoration of infarct-related artery patency before primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) may improve outcomes in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). However, the clinical value of preprocedural unfractionated heparin administration remains uncertain. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and propensity score-matched (PSM) studies comparing preprocedural unfractionated heparin administration before primary PCI versus standard in-hospital anticoagulation. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary angiographic outcomes were initial TIMI 2-3 flow and final TIMI 3 flow. Clinical outcomes included short-term mortality and major bleeding. Results: We included 6 studies (4 RCTs and 2 PSM cohorts) comprising 5,789 patients. The study population was predominantly male (72.0%-82.0%), aged 57 to 65 years, with radial access utilized in 70.6% to 95.8% of contemporary procedures. Early heparin significantly increased the likelihood of initial TIMI 2-3 flow before PCI (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.09-1.53; p=0.003; I 2 =43%). No significant difference was observed in final TIMI 3 flow (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.99-1.03; I 2 =0%). Early heparin was not associated with lower short-term mortality (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.72-1.19; I 2 =0%) or major bleeding (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.56-1.59; I 2 =40%). Conclusions: Among patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI, early unfractionated heparin improved preprocedural coronary patency but did not improve final reperfusion or short-term mortality. Importantly, early administration was not associated with an increased risk of major bleeding.
title: Abstract 15662: Early versus Deferred Unfractionated Heparin in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Undergoing Primary PCI: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Propensity Score-Matched Studies

abstract: Background: Routine venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) has failed to improve survival in randomized trials of cardiogenic shock despite substantial resource utilization and complication burden. Whether selective shock team-guided ECMO allocation provides greater economic value than routine ECMO remains unknown. Methods: A lifetime Markov state-transition model was developed using clinical inputs from ECMO-CS and ECLS-SHOCK. Three strategies were compared: usual care, routine early ECMO, and multidisciplinary shock team-guided selective ECMO allocation. Analyses were conducted from the German statutory health insurance perspective. Outcomes included discounted costs, life-years (LYs), quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed. Results: Routine ECMO increased costs substantially while providing minimal health gains. Compared with usual care, routine ECMO increased lifetime costs by є28,700 and generated only 0.08 additional QALYs, resulting in an ICER of є358,750/QALY. In contrast, shock team-guided ECMO allocation improved outcomes while reducing overall costs. The strategy increased discounted QALYs by 0.59 and LYs by 0.83 while lowering lifetime costs by є4,518 per patient, representing a dominant strategy. Shock team allocation reduced ECMO utilization, shortened ICU length of stay, and lowered complication-related expenditures. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated a >99% probability of cost-effectiveness at willingness-to-pay thresholds of є30,000-50,000/QALY. Findings remained robust across extensive deterministic and scenario analyses. Conclusions: Routine ECMO in unselected cardiogenic shock populations appears economically unattractive under contemporary randomized evidence. In contrast, multidisciplinary shock team-guided selective ECMO allocation improves health outcomes while reducing healthcare expenditures. These findings support systems-based shock care and targeted ECMO deployment rather than routine escalation of mechanical circulatory support.
title: Abstract 15663: Shock Team-Guided ECMO Allocation versus Routine ECMO in Cardiogenic Shock: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Loeffler endocarditis (LE) is a rare eosinophilic cardiomyopathy (CMP) that progresses through necrotic, thrombotic, and fibrotic stages. Early disease may remain subclinical until thromboembolic complications or advanced heart failure develop. We present an atypical case of late-stage LE manifesting as mixed ischemic and nonischemic CMP. Case presentation: A 55-year-old man with a remote anterior STEMI complicated by LV thrombus 16 years prior presented with progressive dyspnea on exertion and fatigue. Workup revealed severe biventricular heart failure with biventricular apical thrombi. At the time of his prior MI, he reported a flu-like illness and recent helminthic infection, although no records were available. He was treated medically with warfarin and aspirin without PCI, but later self-discontinued anticoagulation after being lost to follow-up. On current presentation, physical exam revealed elevated JVP, right upper quadrant tenderness, and bilateral lower extremity edema. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated acute kidney injury, transaminitis, NT-proBNP 6,670 pg/mL, a normal eosinophil count, and mild lactic acidosis. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe biventricular systolic dysfunction (LVEF 15%) and concern for biventricular thrombi. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) demonstrated severe biventricular failure with diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and confirmed biventricular apical thrombi. Coronary angiography demonstrated ostial LAD occlusion with collateralization, proximal OM occlusion, and diffuse RCA disease. Diagnosis and Management: The characteristic diffuse subendocardial LGE pattern extending beyond a single coronary territory, along with extensive intracardiac thrombi and prior helminthic infection, were highly suggestive of late-stage LE with superimposed ischemic CMP. Endomyocardial biopsy and corticosteroid therapy were deferred as CMR findings demonstrated chronic fibrosis without active inflammation. Due to the patient’s end-stage heart failure complicated by cardiogenic shock, PCI was deferred and the patient was started on anticoagulation before being referred for transplant evaluation. Discussion: In this case, a prior helminthic infection was suspected to have triggered a hypereosinophilic syndrome, with the initial MI possibly cardioembolic in origin. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for LE in patients without traditional risk factors presenting with intracardiac thrombi, cardioembolic phenomena, or unexplained CMP, even in the absence of peripheral eosinophilia. Left untreated, progression to the fibrotic phase results in irreversible endomyocardial damage and limited therapeutic options; cardiac transplantation or LVAD implantation remain options in advanced, refractory cases.
title: Abstract 15678: When Ischemic Meets Non-Ischemic: A Rare Presentation of End-Stage Loeffler Endocarditis

abstract: Introduction: Survivors following hospitalization for cardiogenic shock (CS) continue to have consequences of non-cardiac complications of their critical care stay, which may include impact on cognitive, physical, mental health and quality of life domains. Impact on CS survivors with these domains have not been well described following index hospitalization. Research Question: What are the health-related quality of life (QOL) indices from CS survivors following hospital discharge after index hospitalization for CS? Methods: The Multicenter Collaborative to Enhance Biological Understanding, Quality and Outcomes in Cardiogenic (VANQUISH Shock) registry is a prospective observational registry which follows all patients with CS from 5 North American centres with multidisciplinary shock programs. Health-related QOL assessments, which include cerebral performance category (CPC) and Short-Form (SF-36) health surveys were completed at 1, 6 and 12 months following discharge from hospital. Domain scores range from 0-100, where 0 signifies the highest possible disability and 100 indicates perfect health without limitations. Results: Between May 25, 2022- May 25, 2026, 1196 patients were enrolled. From this cohort, 983 82.2%) patients were discharged alive from hospital. At 30 days, 742 patients were alive. At 6 months, 669 patients were alive, and at 1 year, 639 patients were alive. The CPC score 1.6 + 0.94, 1.35 + 0.69, and 1.27 + 0.64 at 1, 6 and 12 months respectively which improved over time. The 8 distinct health domains along with the total score from the SF-36 questionnaire can be found in table 1, with a noted improvement of median scores over the time period for most domains, clearly seen in physical function, role limitations due to physical health, energy/fatigue, social functioning and total score. Conclusions: Survivors of CS report an improvement of CPC score at 1 year following discharge. There is a trend of improvement across some of the domains of the SF-36 including the total score also shows a trend in improvement at 1 year. Further analyses are needed to account for survival bias and address trends between patients.
title: Abstract 15706: Patient Reported Health Related Quality of Life Measures Following Index Admission for Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Background Adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) remain vulnerable to cardiogenic shock, yet contemporary national data regarding temporary mechanical circulatory support (MCS) utilization and outcomes are limited. Methods We analyzed ACHD hospitalizations complicated by cardiogenic shock in the National Inpatient Sample from 2021-2022. Temporary MCS included extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), Impella, and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). Survey-weighted multivariable regression evaluated associations between MCS utilization and in-hospital mortality after adjustment for age, sex, APRDRG severity, and APRDRG mortality risk. Propensity score matching and ECMO-excluded sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Among 2,641 ACHD hospitalizations with cardiogenic shock, 736 (27.9%) received temporary MCS. Compared with patients managed without MCS, MCS recipients had higher crude mortality (21.8% vs 18.2%), longer median length of stay (16 vs 10 days), and greater median hospitalization charges ($563,122 vs $239,692). Patients receiving MCS demonstrated greater illness severity, including APRDRG Severity Level 4 (86.4% vs 76.4%) and APRDRG Mortality Risk Level 4 (93.1% vs 79.3%). Patients with the highest mortality-risk profiles were more than three times as likely to receive MCS (OR 3.26, 95% CI 2.22-4.80). Device utilization included IABP (52.9%), Impella (47.8%), and ECMO (22.6%). Device-specific mortality was highest with ECMO (41.6%), followed by Impella (22.4%) and IABP (18.3%).After multivariable adjustment, overall MCS utilization was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 1.11, 95% CI 0.89-1.39; p=0.346). Findings were consistent in a propensity score-matched cohort of 1,408 patients (p=0.507). However, in a sensitivity analysis excluding ECMO recipients, temporary MCS was independently associated with lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.56-0.94; p=0.015). MCS utilization remained independently associated with 29.7% longer hospitalization and 137.7% higher hospitalization charges (both p<0.001). Conclusions Temporary MCS is utilized in nearly one-third of ACHD patients presenting with cardiogenic shock and is associated with substantially increased healthcare resource utilization. Although overall MCS utilization was not independently associated with mortality, exclusion of ECMO recipients revealed lower mortality among patients receiving non-ECMO temporary MCS, suggesting that the high-risk ECMO population may obscure potential benefits of less invasive support strategies.
title: Abstract 15708: Differential Outcomes of ECMO and Non-ECMO Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Adults with Congenital Heart Disease Presenting with Cardiogenic Shock

abstract: Keywords: light-chain amyloidosis, supraventricular tachycardia, cardiac amyloidosis, voltage-mass mismatch, daratumumab Introduction: Cardiac involvement occurs in ~80% of AL amyloidosis patients and drives prognosis. Amyloid infiltration of the myocardium and conduction system predisposes to arrhythmias and restrictive heart failure. SVT may be the presenting manifestation, and ECG-echocardiographic discordance is critical for timely diagnosis and avoidance of contraindicated therapies. Patient Information: A 65-year-old male with chronic diarrhea, 30-pound weight loss, lower extremity edema, and prior pulmonary embolism presented with dizziness, hypotension, and SVT. Family history included amyloidosis. GI biopsies confirmed amyloid deposition; bone marrow biopsy demonstrated plasma cell dyscrasia consistent with AL amyloidosis. Clinical Findings & Timeline: ECG showed low-voltage QRS complexes. Echo revealed severe concentric LVH, LVEF 30%, reduced RV function (TAPSE 1.3 cm), and moderate pericardial effusion. Voltage-mass mismatch between low-voltage ECG and severe LVH was characteristic of infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Atrial amyloid infiltration likely served as the arrhythmogenic substrate for SVT. Diagnostic Assessment: Low-voltage ECG with severe LVH — voltage-mass discordance — distinguished this from hypertensive or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Tissue confirmation and echocardiographic features established AL amyloidosis with advanced cardiac involvement (Stage IIIb). Therapeutic Interventions: Calcium channel blockers were discontinued due to contraindication from amyloid fibril binding, risking heart block and cardiogenic shock. Amiodarone 400 mg BID achieved SVT control per the 2023 ACC Expert Consensus. Daratumumab-based therapy (ANDROMEDA regimen) was planned given survival benefit (HR 0.62; P=0.0121). Anticoagulation was considered for thromboembolic risk from atrial infiltration. Follow-up & Outcomes: SVT control was achieved on amiodarone without adverse events. Daratumumab-based chemotherapy was initiated during hospitalization. Outpatient follow-up was planned for serial cardiac biomarker monitoring and hematologic response assessment. Discussion: SVT with voltage-mass discordance should prompt evaluation for cardiac AL amyloidosis. CCBs and digoxin are contraindicated; amiodarone is preferred for rate and rhythm control. Early daratumumab-based therapy and deep hematologic response are critical for cardiac recovery and survival.
title: Abstract 15712: Supraventricular Tachycardia Unmasking Advanced Cardiac Involvement in Light-Chain Amyloidosis

abstract: Introduction Recurrent pericarditis remains a therapeutic challenge, particularly in patients with severe inflammatory phenotypes, recurrent hospitalizations, or corticosteroid dependence. Although contemporary guidelines increasingly support interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibition, biologic therapy is often introduced only after multiple treatment failures. We describe a five-patient case series utilizing a fast-track pathway consisting of short-term inpatient anakinra induction followed by rapid transition to maintenance rilonacept. Clinical Five patients aged 47-83 years with recurrent or incessant pericarditis were treated at a tertiary referral pericardial center. Etiologies included Dressler syndrome (n=1), post-pericardiotomy syndrome following surgical aortic valve replacement (n=1), idiopathic pericarditis (n=2), and autoimmune-associated pericarditis (n=1). Prior to referral, patients experienced 11 recurrent episodes and 8 pericarditis-related hospitalizations despite treatment with traditional anti-inflammatory agents. High-risk features included large pericardial effusions (n=2), cardiac tamponade requiring pericardiocentesis (n=1), severe active inflammation on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (n=4), medication intolerance, and persistent symptoms despite standard therapy. Management Given ongoing disease activity and concern for recurrent corticosteroid exposure, all patients underwent inpatient initiation of anakinra with rapid transition to outpatient rilonacept maintenance. Conventional anti-inflammatory therapies were subsequently tapered and discontinued when clinically appropriate. Follow At follow-up ranging from 9 months to 3 years, no patient experienced recurrent pericarditis after initiation of the fast-track IL-1 pathway. All patients demonstrated marked clinical improvement with resolution of chest pain and restoration of functional status. Inflammatory markers normalized when available, and follow-up imaging demonstrated improvement or resolution of pericardial inflammation. Corticosteroids were successfully avoided or discontinued in all patients, while NSAIDs and colchicine were subsequently tapered or discontinued in most cases. Discussion This case series highlights the potential role of a fast-track IL-1 inhibition strategy in high-risk recurrent pericarditis. Early inpatient anakinra induction followed by rapid transition to rilonacept allowed avoidance of prolonged corticosteroid exposure while achieving durable disease control across diverse pericarditis phenotypes. These findings support earlier implementation of IL-1 blockade in appropriately selected patients and provide real-world evidence for a steroid-sparing treatment paradigm in recurrent pericarditis.
title: Abstract 15718: Fast-Track IL-1 Inhibition in Recurrent Pericarditis: A Five-Patient Case Series of Anakinra Induction Followed by Rilonacept Maintenance

abstract: Background: Electrocardiographic lead misplacement may produce false-positive or false-negative ischemic patterns, potentially obscuring acute coronary occlusion and delaying reperfusion therapy. Prompt recognition of technical electrocardiographic errors is essential in patients presenting with suspected STEMI. Case Presentation: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and a smoking history presented with 20 minutes of epigastric pain associated with nausea, diaphoresis, and palpitations. Family history was notable for maternal death from myocardial infarction (MI) at age 59. She was hemodynamically stable on presentation. Initial differential diagnoses included acute coronary syndrome, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and aortic dissection. High-sensitivity troponin peaked at 1250 ng/L, while the chest radiograph was unremarkable. Initial ECG demonstrated ST-segment elevation in leads I and aVL with a negative P-wave in lead III, raising concern for lateral ischemia but with discordant ECG findings. She received aspirin, ticagrelor, and high-intensity statin with emergent cath lab activation. Shortly after the initial ECG, left arm-left leg limb reversal was identified. Repeat ECG demonstrated inferior ST-segment elevation with greater ST elevation in lead III than II, concerning for right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. Nitrates were withheld because right ventricular infarction is preload dependent, and nitrate administration may precipitate severe hypotension. Emergent coronary angiography revealed complete proximal RCA occlusion, and the patient underwent successful PCI with placement of two stents within the guideline-recommended reperfusion time. Discussion: This case demonstrates how limb lead reversal can obscure the true localization of MI and create diagnostic uncertainty despite elevated cardiac biomarkers and ongoing ischemic symptoms. Recognition of the corrected inferior STEMI pattern was clinically important because ST elevation greater in lead III than II increased suspicion for RCA involvement and possible right ventricular infarction, directly influencing hemodynamically tailored management. Conclusion: Recognition of technical errors is essential in patients with suspected STEMI when ECG findings are discordant with clinical presentation. Early identification of lead misplacement may prevent diagnostic delay and facilitate timely reperfusion therapy in acute MI.
title: Abstract 15743: Limb Lead Reversal Obscuring Inferior ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Case Report

abstract: Introduction: Vascular EDS (vEDS) is an inherited connective tissue disorder associated with defective type III collagen synthesis and vascular fragility. Pregnancy in women with vEDS carries high risk of arterial rupture or dissection, uterine rupture, severe hemorrhage, and maternal mortality. Data on optimal peripartum management of patients with vEDS is limited. Patient Information (De-Identified): A 32-year-old G6P2032 female presented to Maternal Fetal Medicine (MFM) clinic at 8 weeks gestation. She has history of prothrombin gene mutation, splenic infarction after her first pregnancy likely due to splenic artery dissection, and vEDS (pathogenic COL3A1 c.3966delG variant), diagnosed after her second pregnancy, following uterine rupture during vaginal birth after cesarean delivery and NSTEMI 5 months postpartum due to spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) requiring LAD and RCA stents. Clinical Findings & Timeline: The patient was counseled regarding pregnancy termination given high maternal risk and offered antenatal fetal genetic testing, which she declined. Cardiology referral was placed. TTE showed normal biventricular function, mild diastolic dysfunction, and normal aortic dimensions. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: A multidisciplinary meeting was held with Cardiology, MFM, and Obstetric Anesthesia to discuss peripartum management. For preeclampsia prevention, history of SCAD, and prothrombin gene mutation, she was maintained on antiplatelet therapy and prophylactic low molecular-weight heparin. She received beta blocker therapy to lower hemodynamic stress. She had surveillance TTE each trimester, and magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis 3rd trimester confirmed no large vessel dissection or aneurysm. Cesarean delivery was planned at 36 weeks with vascular surgery on backup. Avoidance of vasoconstrictive agents including certain uterotonics was advised. Postpartum management included telemetry monitoring, strict hemodynamic goals, and extended inpatient surveillance due to high risk of complications. Therapeutic Interventions: The patient was asymptomatic with stable functional status during pregnancy. She had an uncomplicated cesarean delivery at 36 weeks’ gestation with 5 days of inpatient monitoring. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: TTE at discharge showed no interval change. She remains event-free on follow-up. Postnatal genetic testing confirmed her neonate carried the same COL3A1 variant. Discussion & Synthesis: While pregnancy in vEDS is associated with high risk of vascular events, successful pregnancy outcomes may be achievable through multidisciplinary care, serial multimodality imaging, close peripartum planning, and hemodynamic optimization. Antenatal and extended postpartum surveillance are critical for early detection and treatment of cardiovascular complications.
title: Abstract 15761: A Delicate Matrix: Cardio-Obstetric Management of Pregnancy in Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome with Prior Arterial Complications

abstract: Introduction: Papillary fibroelastoma (PFE) is a rare primary cardiac tumor, most commonly involving the aortic and mitral valves. Although histologically benign, PFEs are clinically significant due to their potential for embolization, most frequently leading to neurological manifestations ranging from transient ischemic attack to ischemic stroke. Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is another well-established risk factor for ischemic stroke through paradoxical embolism. The coexistence of PFE and PFO in acute ischemic stroke creates a diagnostic and management challenge because both may represent potential embolic pathways. Case description: A 48-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia presented with sudden expressive aphasia, right hemiparesis, and right facial droop. Imaging demonstrated ischemic penumbra in the left frontotemporal region. Intravenous thrombolytic therapy was administered, with clinical improvement. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a right-to-left shunt. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) confirmed PFO (figure 1) and identified a mobile, frond-like echogenic mass attached to the aortic valve (figure 2), suggestive of PFE. Lower-extremity venous Doppler ultrasonography was negative for deep venous thrombosis. Given concern for recurrent embolic risk, the patient underwent combined surgical excision of the aortic valve mass and PFO closure. Histopathology confirmed PFE (figure 3). The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and at 1-year follow-up she remained free of recurrent neurologic events. Discussion: This case highlights the importance of early cardiac evaluation in acute ischemic stroke when an embolic mechanism is suspected. Both potential cardioembolic abnormalities were identified during the initial stroke workup, allowing for timely multidisciplinary intervention during the index hospitalization. The patient underwent combined surgical resection of PFE and PFO closure during a single operative session. Identification of a structural cardiac abnormality such as PFE can significantly alter clinical management, particularly when a mobile left-sided valvular mass is discovered in the setting of acute ischemic stroke. Early TEE was central to diagnosis and helped guide definitive management. Conclusion: In patients with cryptogenic or embolic-appearing stroke, comprehensive cardiac evaluation, particularly early use of TEE, can identify actionable cardiac abnormalities that may be missed or incompletely characterized by transthoracic imaging. When PFE and PFO coexist, multidisciplinary collaboration may permit simultaneous treatment of dual potential embolic mechanisms and may reduce the risk of recurrent neurologic events.
title: Abstract 15762: Early Identification of Dual Cardiac Embolic Sources: Papillary Fibroelastoma and Patent Foramen Ovale Presenting as Acute Ischemic Stroke

abstract: INTRODUCTION: Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm (LVP) is an exceedingly rare but life-threatening mechanical complication of myocardial infarction, occurring in 0.1%-0.3% of cases. Untreated LVP carries a 30%-45% risk of rupture, while surgical repair is associated with 20%-36% mortality. We report a case of a large posterobasal pseudoaneurysm following an unrecognized inferior wall myocardial infarction, presenting with non-specific constitutional symptoms. This case underscores the importance of early recognition using multimodality imaging to guide timely surgical intervention. CASE PRESENTATION: A 66-year-old man without routine medical care for over 8 years presented with a 2-month history of fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and intermittent chest pain that began after lifting a heavy air conditioner and recurred with snow shoveling. Revealed new-onset diabetes mellitus, mild elevations in troponin and BNP, elevated inflammatory markers, and ECG consistent with an acute lateral and prior inferior MI. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) showed a LV ejection fraction of 40-45% with severe regional wall-motion abnormalities and concern for LVP without pericardial free flow. Coronary angiography showed severe multivessel coronary artery disease. Cardiac CT identified a 66 х 50 х 41 mm broad-based inferobasal left ventricular outpouching with a 51 х 41 mm neck, with a contained myocardial rupture and hemopericardium; findings were confirmed by left ventriculography. He underwent hemopericardium evacuation, pericardium patch reinforcement of left ventricular rupture, left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending coronary artery bypass grafting, and Impella device placed deep in LV cavity as a bridge to recovery. His Postoperative course was complicated by cardiogenic shock with LVEF 40%, secondary to acute hypoxic respiratory failure, and atrial fibrillation. He was not a candidate for transplantation due to friable myocardium. After a successful surgical repair of the LVP, follow-up TTE showed complete exclusion of the basal inferior pseudoaneurysm without residual flow, improved LVEF 50%, and a small pericardial effusion. Presently, he remains clinically stable on partial guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for HFrEF under outpatient cardiology care. DISCUSSION: This noteworthy case illustrates how a potentially lethal contained left ventricular free-wall rupture with a giant pseudoaneurysm can hide behind nonspecific constitutional symptoms rather than classic cardiac symptoms. Early recognition and a multidisciplinary approach is vital, along with an urgent surgical intervention with revascularization in preventing further cardiac complications. Delayed diagnosis in such cases, can lead to hemopericardium, left ventricular free-wall and pseudoaneurysm rupture which may result in sudden cardiac death.
title: Abstract 15770: Contained Myocardial Free-Wall Rupture Manifesting as Constitutional Illness: A Rare Presentation of Giant Left Ventricular Pseudoaneurysm

abstract: Background: Recovery of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) may not reflect complete myocardial recovery, as diastolic dysfunction can persist despite systolic improvement. Galectin-3, a biomarker of fibrosis, may provide incremental insight into post-infarction remodeling. Research question: To evaluate whether early galectin-3 levels are associated with persistent diastolic dysfunction after STEMI, independent of conventional markers of infarct severity and ventricular function. Methods: GALACT-MI is a prospective single-center pilot study including consecutive STEMI patients treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Galectin-3 was measured 24 hours after admission and at follow-up. Echocardiography was performed during hospitalization and follow-up, assessing LVEF, E′ velocity, E/e′ ratio, and diastolic dysfunction grade. Associations between baseline galectin-3 and follow-up echocardiographic parameters were evaluated using Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression adjusted for baseline LVEF, peak troponin, and NT-proBNP. Results: Among 31 enrolled patients, 27 completed follow-up (mean age 59.0±8.0 years; 70.4% male) after 101 [77-192] days. LVEF improved significantly (47.1±8.9% to 53.1±9.3%; p=0.004), whereas diastolic dysfunction remained highly prevalent (92.6%). Baseline galectin-3 was associated with lower follow-up E′ velocity (ρ=–0.559; p=0.002) and higher E/e′ ratio (ρ=0.418; p=0.030). Despite marked NT-proBNP reduction (p<0.0001), E/e′ ratio showed no significant improvement and galectin-3 increased during follow-up (57.79±18.30 to 66.81±21.46 ng/mL; p=0.043). In multivariable analysis, baseline galectin-3 remained independently associated with higher follow-up E/e′ ratio (β=0.125; 95% CI 0.025-0.226; p=0.017). Conclusions: Early galectin-3 levels are independently associated with persistent diastolic dysfunction despite LVEF recovery after STEMI. The discordance between improving LVEF and NT-proBNP and persistently elevated galectin-3 suggests ongoing fibrotic remodeling not captured by conventional recovery markers. Galectin-3 may represent a useful biomarker of residual myocardial remodeling and a potential tool for post-infarction risk stratification.
title: Abstract 15777: GALACT-MI: Early Galectin-3 Identifies Residual Diastolic Remodeling Despite LVEF Recovery After STEMI

abstract: A 72-year-old female with history of atrial fibrillation on warfarin, HFpEF, CAD s/p PCI, subdural hematoma, Sick sinus syndrome s/p PPM presented with NYHA class III dyspnea. Five years prior, she underwent surgical mitral valve replacement with a 29mm Edwards SAPIEN S3 bioprosthesis for severe Mitral Regurgitation (MR) with extensive Mitral Annular Calcification (MAC), requiring pericardial patch reinforcement & chordal preservation. Transthoracic Echocardiogram revealed severe mitral stenosis (area 0.6 cm 2 ) with structural deterioration. The 4D CT imaging revealed Neo-LVOT area 119 mm2; valve frame fracture in the ventricular aspect, which was confirmed on cardiac cath. While she was determined to be at prohibitive risk for surgery, transcatheter approach was also high risk due to the potential for embolization of the distal fractured fragment. Due to high risk for LVOT obstruction, prophylactic alcohol septal ablation was done, increasing neo-LVOT area from 119 mm 2 to 239 mm 2 . A Sentinel embolic protection device was used due to concern of valve fragment embolization. Successful transseptal ViV-TMVR was completed with a 29 mm Edwards SAPIEN S3 valve, post-dilated with a 28 mm TrueBalloon. This case highlights durable long term outcomes of ViV-TMVR in severe MAC, and complex anatomy, enabled by careful pre-procedural assessment and prophylactic LVOT management.
title: Abstract 15778: Transcatheter Mitral Valve-in-Valve Replacement in Extreme Anatomic and Structural Complexity: When Conventional Contraindications Meet Innovative Solutions

abstract: Severe mitral stenosis in pregnancy is high risk because increased plasma volume, cardiac output, and heart rate can worsen gradients across a fixed left-sided obstruction, leading to pulmonary edema, pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction, and cardiogenic shock. A 29-year-old gravida 4 para 3 woman at 21 weeks gestation was transferred for atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, hypotension, pulmonary edema, and undifferentiated shock. Her history included rheumatic valvular heart disease status post bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement, tricuspid valve repair, pulmonary vein isolation, left atrial appendage excision, and atrial septal defect closure. On arrival, she had progressive dyspnea, lower extremity edema, elevated lactate, and cool extremities concerning for mixed cardiogenic and septic shock. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe prosthetic mitral stenosis with restricted leaflet motion and mobile echodensities concerning for vegetation. Mitral valve gradient was 31mmHg at a heart rate of 137 beats per minute, mitral valve area was 0.7cm 2 , right ventricular systolic pressure was 65mmHg, and right ventricular function was moderately reduced. Blood cultures grew Aggregatibacter aphrophilus, consistent with HACEK prosthetic valve endocarditis. A multidisciplinary shock team was activated, and left atrial venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was initiated for systemic perfusion and direct left atrial unloading. Her course was complicated by previable preterm premature rupture of membranes, chorioamnionitis, and intrauterine fetal demise. She underwent redo mechanical mitral valve replacement and was transitioned to venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for persistent hypoxemic respiratory failure and pulmonary edema. She was decannulated and extubated by hospital day 9, underwent cardioversion for recurrent atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter on hospital day 13, and was discharged home on hospital day 18 with warfarin, intravenous ceftriaxone, and secondary rheumatic fever prophylaxis. At 10-month follow-up, she had New York Heart Association class I functional status and a stable mechanical mitral valve. This case demonstrates a rare convergence of severe prosthetic mitral stenosis, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, and HACEK prosthetic valve endocarditis causing mixed cardiogenic and septic shock during pregnancy. Left atrial venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation provided hemodynamic stabilization and lactate clearance as a bridge to redo mitral valve replacement. Early shock team activation and coordinated cardio-obstetric care were essential to maternal survival.
title: Abstract 15797: Left Atrial Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Cardiogenic Shock from Severe Mitral Stenosis in Pregnancy

abstract: Background: PCSK9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) are monoclonal antibodies that substantially lower LDL-C and modestly reduce lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)]. They represent an emerging cornerstone in ASCVD risk reduction. There is a strong association between calcific aortic stenosis and elevated LDL-C and Lp(a) levels. Existing evidence supporting the use of PCSK9i, such as the post hoc analysis of the FOURIER trial, did not yield conclusive results in this regard due to the low event rate of new or worsening AS. This study aims to evaluate the clinical outcomes of PCSK9 inhibitor use in patients with aortic stenosis. Methods: This analysis used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Cohort 1 included patients with hyperlipidemia and aortic stenosis who were prescribed evolocumab, alirocumab, or inclisiran. Cohort 2 consisted of patients with hyperlipidemia and aortic stenosis who did not have these PCSK9 inhibitor medications prescribed. Both groups excluded patients with prior TAVR or TAVI and a heart failure diagnosis. Propensity score matching was used. After matching, there were 5,975 patients per group, and most baseline variables were well balanced. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, STEMI, stroke, atrial fibrillation, ER visit or hospitalization, and ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation (VT/VF). Results: PCSK9i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.386, 95% CI 0.334-0.446; log-rank p < 0.001) and fewer ER visits or hospitalizations (HR 0.800, 95% CI 0.758-0.845; log-rank p < 0.001). Risk analyses also showed lower rates of STEMI (RR 0.772, 95% CI 0.640-0.931), stroke (RR 0.730, 95% CI 0.611-0.872), atrial fibrillation (RR 0.653, 95% CI 0.569-0.751), and VT/VF (RR 0.811, 95% CI 0.737-0.892), although corresponding Kaplan-Meier analyses for these outcomes were not statistically significant. Conclusion: In a large propensity-matched EHR-based analysis of patients with aortic stenosis and hyperlipidemia, PCSK9 inhibitor use was associated with significantly lower all-cause mortality and reduced rates of ER visits or hospitalization. These findings suggest a potential clinical benefit of intensive lipid-lowering therapy in this high-risk population and warrant further prospective studies.
title: Abstract 15798: Association of PCSK9 Inhibitor Use with Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Aortic Stenosis: A Retrospective Electronic Health Record-Based Analysis

abstract: Introduction Staphylococcus epidermidis is mostly considered a contamination, particularly in patients without prosthetic valves or intracardiac devices. However, repeated skin barrier disruption may provide a portal of entry for bacteremia. We present a case of rapidly progressive native aortic and mitral valve infective endocarditis in a young woman whose only identifiable risk factor was recent weekly subcutaneous GLP-1 receptor agonist self-injection. Case A 33 year old woman with no significant past medical history presented with several weeks of intermittent fevers, progressive fatigue, generalized weakness, and worsening exertional dyspnea. She had no prosthetic valve, intracardiac device, recent dental procedure, intravenous drug use, or other clear infectious source. Three months before presentation, she had started weekly self administered subcutaneous tirzepatide injections. Outpatient blood cultures grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis, and serial inpatient cultures remained positive. Initial transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated an anterior mitral valve vegetation with moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) and possible aortic valve involvement. Intravenous antibiotics were initiated. Within approximately 36 hours, she developed sudden hypotension refractory to intravenous fluids. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe metabolic acidosis with bicarbonate 8 mmol/L, lactate 19.5 mmol/L, and pH 6.97. She required intubation, multiple vasopressors, and transfer to a tertiary cardiac surgery center. Transesophageal echocardiography showed mitral leaflet perforation with torrential MR, severe aortic regurgitation, and vegetations involving both native valves. Because profound mixed septic and cardiogenic shock made immediate valve replacement prohibitively high risk, she underwent rescue Left Atrial Veno Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (LAVA ECMO). After stabilization, she underwent bioprosthetic mitral and aortic valve replacement and ECMO decannulation. Operative inspection confirmed extensive destruction and perforation of the anterior mitral leaflet along with aortic valve perforation. She recovered and was discharged home on intravenous oxacillin and warfarin. DiscussionRepeated subcutaneous self injection may represent an underrecognized portal of entry for bloodstream infection. In this patient, examination later documented puncture marks at the injection sites, making repeated skin barrier disruption the most plausible portal of entry, supported by the temporal relationship between initiation of tirzepatide self injections and subsequent high grade S. epidermidis bacteremia. Clinicians should reinforce sterile injection technique and should not dismiss persistent S. epidermidis bacteremia as contamination in patients using self injectable medications
title: Abstract 15805: Fulminant Native Multivalvular Staphylococcus epidermidis Endocarditis After Repeated GLP1 Self Injections Requiring Left Atrial Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation

abstract: Background: Early risk stratification in cardiogenic shock remains challenging. We evaluated the prognostic performance of blood pressure-to-lactate indices for predicting in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with cardiogenic shock. Methods This retrospective study utilized the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database of Adult ICU patients with cardiogenic shock (ICD-9 code 785.51 and ICD-10 codes R57.0 and T81.11XA). Blood pressure and lactate measurements obtained within the first 24 hours of ICU admission were extracted. Invasive arterial blood pressure measurements were preferentially used; otherwise, non-invasive measurements were utilized. Patients with available lactate and blood pressure measurements were included in the final cohort (n=1,909). Four blood pressure-to-lactate indices were evaluated: LSBP, LDBP, LMAP, and LPP, calculated as (lactate х100) divided by SBP, DBP, MAP, and PP, respectively. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Prognostic performance was assessed using ROC analysis with pairwise DeLong comparisons. Optimal cutoffs were determined using the Youden index. Pre-specified Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, SOFA score, vasopressor use, and mechanical ventilation. Results: Among 1,909 included ICU patients with cardiogenic shock, 38.8% died during hospitalization. Non-survivors were older, had higher SOFA scores, lower blood pressure, and higher lactate level than survivors (p<0.01).All blood pressure-to-lactate indices were significantly elevated among non-survivors, with median LMAP nearly doubling compared with survivors (7.3 vs. 3.8,p<0.001). Among evaluated indices, LMAP demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for predicting in-hospital mortality (AUC 0.688), followed by LDBP (0.685), LSBP (0.683), and LPP (0.667). LMAP significantly outperformed LSBP (p=0.008) and LPP (p<0.001), while performing similarly to LDBP (p=0.117). The optimal ROC-derived cutoff for LMAP was 8.45, yielding a sensitivity of 44.9% and specificity of 85.2%. Mortality increased progressively across higher LMAP thresholds, rising from 52.0% at LMAP >5 to 83.1% at LMAP >15. In the fully adjusted model, LMAP >8.45 remained independently associated with mortality (aOR 3.34,95% CI 2.64-4.24, p<0.001). LMAP demonstrated a strong dose-response relationship with mortality. Mortality increased from 25.9% in the Q1 (0.69-2.74) to 66.7% in the Q4 (>8.81) (χ 2 =216.85, p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, only the Q4 remained independently associated with mortality compared with the lowest quartile (aOR 3.57,95%CI 2.63-4.87). p<0.001). Conclusion: LMAP demonstrated the highest predictive performance for in-hospital mortality in ICU patients with cardiogenic shock. An LMAP >8.45 was independently associated with mortality and identified a high-risk population with substantial mortality risk.
title: Abstract 15813: Comparative Prognostic Performance of Blood Pressure-to-Lactate Ratios for Predicting In-Hospital Mortality in ICU Patients with Cardiogenic Shock: A MIMIC-IV Study

abstract: Background: Inflammation and fibrosis are key drivers of ventricular remodeling following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Early identification of patients at risk of incomplete ventricular recovery remains challenging despite successful reperfusion. Integrated biomarker approaches may improve post-infarction risk stratification by capturing complementary inflammatory and fibrotic pathways.Research Question: Can the INFLA-MI score, integrating the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and galectin-3, identify patients at risk of persistent systolic and diastolic dysfunction following STEMI?Methods: INFLA-MI is a prospective single-center study including consecutive STEMI patients treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention. SII, MLR, and galectin-3 were measured 24 hours after admission. Echocardiography was performed during hospitalization and follow-up by operators blinded to biomarker levels and prior imaging data. Persistent systolic dysfunction was defined as follow-up LVEF <50%, and persistent diastolic dysfunction as E/e′ >9. Predictive performance was assessed using ROC analysis, logistic regression, trend analysis, and bootstrap internal validation (2,000 replicates).Results: Thirty-one patients were enrolled, with complete follow-up data available in 27-28 patients. Mean age was 59 years and 71% were male. Median follow-up was 102 [78-189] days. LVEF improved significantly from 47.4±8.9% to 53.1±9.3% (p=0.004). Despite this recovery, persistent systolic dysfunction remained present in 28.6% of patients and persistent diastolic dysfunction in 63.0%. The INFLA-MI score demonstrated strong discrimination for persistent systolic dysfunction (AUC=0.838, 95% CI 0.668-1.000) and persistent diastolic dysfunction (AUC=0.853, 95% CI 0.708-0.998), outperforming individual biomarkers in both analyses. Performance remained consistent after bootstrap validation (systolic: 95% CI 0.656-0.975; diastolic: 95% CI 0.718-0.959). Each one-point increase in score was associated with higher odds of persistent systolic dysfunction (OR=4.74, 95% CI 1.46-15.40; p=0.010) and persistent diastolic dysfunction (OR=10.84, 95% CI 1.66-70.55; p=0.013). Significant dose-response relationships were observed across score categories for both outcomes (p≤0.003).Conclusions: The INFLA-MI Score demonstrated robust internally validated performance for identifying STEMI patients at risk of incomplete ventricular recovery. By integrating complementary inflammatory and fibrotic pathways, the score outperformed individual biomarkers for predicting persistent systolic and diastolic dysfunction. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter cohorts.
title: Abstract 15817: INFLA-MI Score: Early Inflammatory-Fibrotic Profiling Identifies Patients at Risk of Incomplete Ventricular Recovery After STEMI

abstract: Introduction: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis, with stroke representing a recognized neurologic complication. Transient cortical blindness is exceedingly rare following TAVR and is most often described after angiographic procedures involving high contrast exposure. This syndrome causes acute bilateral visual loss with preserved pupillary reflexes and rapid recovery and is thought to result from transient blood-brain barrier disruption. We present a case of transient cortical blindness occurring hours after TAVR. Clinical Case: A 77-year-old female patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pulmonary fibrosis status post lung transplantation, mixed hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease, and severe aortic stenosis underwent elective TAVR. Pre-procedural echocardiography demonstrated moderate-to-severe aortic stenosis (mean gradient 28 mmHg, peak velocity 3.4 m/s, aortic valve area 0.8 cm 2 ). A 26-mm Sapien S3 valve was successfully implanted. Post-procedural echocardiography demonstrated mild anterior paravalvular leak with normal prosthetic valve hemodynamics (peak velocity 1.3 m/s, mean gradient 4 mmHg, valve area 1.8 cm 2 ).Approximately six hours after the procedure, the patient developed acute, bilateral vision loss with preserved pupillary reflexes. Neurologic examination was otherwise non-focal. CTA of the head and neck showed atherosclerotic plaque without large vessel occlusion. Brain MRI demonstrated subtle scattered areas of sulcal FLAIR non-suppression, most prominent in the right frontal and parieto-occipital regions, suspicious for contrast extravasation mimicking subarachnoid hemorrhage. Small areas of diffusion restriction within the right occipital lobe were also noted and interpreted as susceptibility artifact from blood products versus small areas of infarction. Vision began to return spontaneously and fully resolved within 24 hours. Discussion: Transient cortical blindness is a rare, reversible neurologic syndrome most often reported after angiographic procedures involving iodinated contrast. It presents with acute bilateral vision loss, preserved pupillary reflexes, and rapid recovery, distinguishing it from ischemic stroke. The proposed mechanism involves transient blood-brain barrier disruption with occipital contrast extravasation. Although neurologic complications after transcatheter aortic valve replacement are typically embolic, atypical features should prompt consideration of non-ischemic etiologies. In this case, delayed onset after contrast exposure, bilateral symptoms, absence of focal deficits, and complete resolution within 24 hours favored contrast-induced cortical blindness. Neuroimaging may mimic acute ischemia. Differentiation from stroke is essential because management differs.
title: Abstract 15821: Transient Cortical Blindness Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Case of Suspected Contrast-Induced Neurotoxicity

abstract: Introduction Scleroderma-associated heart failure represents a serious and often unrecognized complication of systemic sclerosis (SSC). Pathogenesis involves recurrent ischemia-reperfusion injury, which triggers a cascade of myocardial inflammation and fibrosis. Studies demonstrate that SSC patients face a markedly elevated risk of heart failure compared to the general population. The mortality nearly triples when clinical cardiac involvement develops. Clinical Findings A woman in her 40s with a history of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia presented with one month of progressive cough, dyspnea, and intermittent chest discomfort. She also endorsed symptoms of finger hyperpigmentation, skin tightening, and acid reflux. She had an elevated high-sensitivity troponin of 447 ng/L, and electrocardiography demonstrated atrial tachycardia with non-specific T-wave changes and occasional premature ventricular contractions. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 35-40% with global hypokinesis, reduced right ventricular systolic function, biatrial enlargement, and moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Diagnostic coronary angiography excluded obstructive coronary artery disease. She was found to have a positive antinuclear antibody (ANA) of 1:640 in a nucleolar pattern, with elevated IgG levels. She was readmitted a few months later for acute heart failure. A positron emission tomography/computed tomography scan excluded cardiac sarcoidosis. Post-discharge, she saw rheumatology as an outpatient and was clinically diagnosed with scleroderma. Her third admission, months later, was for cardiogenic shock. A cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed evidence consistent with scleroderma-related myocarditis. Endomyocardial biopsy showed scarring and myocyte hypertrophy. She developed symptomatic bradycardia with left bundle branch block requiring cardiac resynchronization therapy—defibrillator implantation, and inotropic support. Mycophenolate mofetil was initiated. She was admitted for a fourth time with cardiogenic shock requiring Impella placement. She was considered for a dual heart-lung transplant and was declined by multiple institutions. Her Impella was removed, and she subsequently developed multisystem organ failure, colonic perforation, and a right ACA/MCA infarct with midline shift and brainstem herniation. She was subsequently palliatively extubated. Discussion Cardiac systemic sclerosis can be a devastating manifestation of systemic sclerosis that necessitates early recognition. This case underscores the need for further research into standardized immunosuppressive protocols, as traditional therapies may be insufficient to halt myocardial remodeling once scarring and conduction system failure have occurred.
title: Abstract 15839: Primary Myocardial Involvement in Systemic Sclerosis

abstract: Background Post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) comprises pericardial inflammation after cardiac injury. Its two dominant etiologies, surgery-related (S-PCIS, post-pericardiotomy syndrome) and electrophysiology procedure-related (EP-PCIS), differ in mechanism, presentation, and management burden, yet comparative data from a modern referral registry are lacking. We characterized the phenotype, imaging, and baseline treatment of both subtypes. Methods Patients with pericardial disease were identified by ICD-10 codes at a dedicated pericardial center. Research fellows and a nurse practitioner reviewed all codes, with independent secondary review applying standardized definitions before registry inclusion. Results Of 2,831 pericardial disease patients, 530 (18.7%) had PCIS (median age 60, 56.8% male). S-PCIS was most common (n=372, 70.2%), followed by EP-PCIS (n=123, 22.5%), post-PCI (2.5%), post-TAVR (0.9%), and trauma (0.4%). In S-PCIS, the leading etiology was multiple/combined cardiac interventions (49%), followed by isolated CABG (13.4%), aortic valve replacement (13.4%), mitral valve surgery (10.8%), aortic surgery (9.4%), and tricuspid surgery (4%). In EP-PCIS, AF ablation/PVI predominated (42.3%), followed by PPM (31.7%), epicardial/VT ablation (8.1%), ICD (6.5%), and AVN/SVT ablation (6.5%); atrial fibrillation was the most common comorbidity (54.5%). Recurrent pericarditis was more frequent in EP-PCIS (41.5%) than S-PCIS (34%), while constrictive pericarditis occurred in ~13% of both (12.2% vs 13.6%). EP-PCIS showed a high effusion burden (39.8%) and a pericardiocentesis rate of 41.5%, far exceeding the whole registry (5.1%), reflecting drainage to avoid tamponade. Anti-inflammatory use was higher in EP-PCIS (colchicine 77.2% vs 66%, prednisone 37.4% vs 27%, rilonacept 13% vs 8.9%). Conclusion In this large modern referral registry, PCIS represented nearly one-fifth of pericardial disease cases, with S-PCIS being the dominant subtype. However, EP-PCIS demonstrated a distinct and clinically important phenotype, with higher rates of recurrent pericarditis, substantial effusion burden, frequent pericardiocentesis, and greater use of anti-inflammatory therapies. These findings highlight meaningful differences between PCIS subtypes and support the need for etiology-specific recognition, monitoring, and management strategies.
title: Abstract 15841: Post-Cardiac Injury Syndrome (PCIS): A Comprehensive Single-Centre Registry Analysis of Surgery-Related and Electrophysiology Procedure-Associated Pericarditis

abstract: Background: Adverse pregnancy outcomes have been linked to higher long-term cardiovascular risk. Prior studies have examined this relationship across race/ethnicity groups, but evidence remains difficult to compare across cohorts, outcome definitions, and pregnancy complication types. We examined EHR-recorded adverse pregnancy outcomes and incident ASCVD in a pregnancy-evidence cohort from the All of Us Research Program, focusing on race/ethnicity and two common APO subtypes: hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and gestational diabetes. Methods: We analyzed women in the All of Us Research Program with EHR evidence of pregnancy-related care, age 18-50 at pregnancy index, at least 365 days of prior EHR observation, and no ASCVD before index. The pregnancy index was based on a recorded delivery date when available and otherwise assigned from pregnancy-related EHR records. APOs were identified in a pregnancy-associated window and included hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, preeclampsia/eclampsia, and gestational diabetes. Incident ASCVD was defined as myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, PCI, or CABG after index. Cox models adjusted for age and race/ethnicity estimated APO-associated ASCVD risk, with interaction models evaluating whether associations differed by race/ethnicity and APO subtype. Results: Among 36,958 women in the non-Hispanic White, non-Hispanic Black, and Hispanic/Latina groups, 1,108 incident ASCVD events occurred. APO history was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk after adjustment for age and race/ethnicity: HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.18-1.95. This association differed by race/ethnicity. Compared with non-Hispanic White women, non-Hispanic Black women had a stronger APO-associated hazard: interaction HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.05-1.71; p=0.017. No similar interaction was seen for Hispanic/Latina women. In subtype analyses, the signal was driven mainly by hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: HR 1.65, 95% CI 1.27-2.14. Gestational diabetes showed no clear association with ASCVD. The HDP-associated hazard was also stronger among non-Hispanic Black than non-Hispanic White women: interaction HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.05-1.75; p=0.020. Conclusion: In this pregnancy-evidence cohort, EHR-recorded APOs were associated with higher incident ASCVD risk. The association was stronger among non-Hispanic Black than non-Hispanic White women and was driven mainly by hypertensive disorders of pregnancy rather than gestational diabetes.
