These findings point to closer cardiovascular follow-up after hypertensive pregnancy complications, particularly among non-Hispanic Black women.
title: Abstract 15842: Race and Ethnicity Differences in ASCVD Risk After Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes

abstract: Background: Patients with severe ischemic cardiomyopathy are frequently considered for complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), often with adjunctive temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). However, contemporary randomized trials, including REVIVED-BCIS2 and CHIP-BCIS3, did not demonstrate a clear clinical benefit from PCI and tMCS-related strategies in this population. There are limited data on contemporary practice patterns and clinical outcomes for patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy undergoing PCI. Methods: Using the ACC/NCDR CathPCI Registry, we evaluated temporal trends in PCI and tMCS volumes among patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 35% and multi-vessel coronary artery disease or left main disease who underwent PCI between 2018 and 2025, as well as their clinical characteristics, procedural approaches, and in-hospital outcomes. Results: Among 84,704 patients, mean age was 69.7 years, 74.8% were male, and 57.4% had diabetes. The mean LVEF was 23.8% and 24.2% had left main disease. Femoral access was used in 61.9% and most procedures were completed at teaching hospitals (57.9%) and urban centers (58.3%). Quarterly PCI volume increased progressively over the study period (2,250 PCIs in Q3 2018 to 3,450 PCIs in Q2 2025; Panel A). Temporary MCS use also increased from 21% in Q3 2018 to 25% in Q2 2025 (Panel B). The most common tMCS devices were Impella microaxial flow pumps (72.0%), followed by intra-aortic balloon pumps (24.7%), venoarterial extra-corporeal membrane oxygenation (2.9%), and TandemHeart percutaneous ventricular assist devices (0.3%). The rate of post-PCI bleeding was 6.6%, cardiac arrest 5.2%, and new dialysis 2.1%. Overall in-hospital mortality was 7.4%, with higher rates observed in women vs. men (9.5% vs 6.6%; p < 0.01), patients with vs. without diabetes (7.8% vs 6.7%; p < 0.01), and patients with LVEF <20% vs. ≥20% (11.2% vs 6.5%; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Despite neutral randomized trial data, both PCI and adjunctive tMCS volumes have increased over time in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy. Impella microaxial flow pumps were the predominant form of adjunctive tMCS. Patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy experienced substantial in-hospital morbidity and mortality despite these practices, particularly women and patients with severe LV dysfunction.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis in the ACC/NCDR CathPCI Registry, 84,704 patients with LVEF <=35% and multivessel or left main disease, 2018 to 2025.
appraisal.main_limitation: Descriptive in-hospital outcomes without a comparator or adjustment, and no post-discharge follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Registry trends show rising PCI and temporary mechanical circulatory support use in ischaemic cardiomyopathy despite neutral trial data.

title: Abstract 15863: Contemporary Trends and Outcomes of Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support Use in Patients with Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CathPCI Registry

abstract: Introduction: Despite advances in contemporary drug-eluting stents (DES), adverse ischemic events continue to accrue beyond the first year after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The DynamX sirolimus-eluting bioadaptor is designed to restore adaptive vessel function following polymer resorption, potentially improving long-term clinical outcomes. Research Question: Does the DynamX bioadaptor improve clinical outcomes compared with contemporary DES following PCI? Methods: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing the DynamX bioadaptor with contemporary DES. MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and major cardiovascular conference proceedings were searched through June 2026. The primary outcome was target lesion failure (TLF), defined as cardiovascular death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization. Landmark analyses evaluated outcomes after the 6-month vessel-uncaging period. Results: Two randomized trials enrolling 2,845 patients were included. At 12 months, TLF rates were similar between the bioadaptor and DES groups (2.3% vs 2.8%; OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.51-1.31), confirming non-inferior short-term performance. During landmark follow-up beyond 6 months, the bioadaptor was associated with significantly lower TLF through 24 months (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.26-0.85), representing a 53% relative reduction. In long-term follow-up of BIOADAPTOR-RCT, TLF at 4 years was 2.8% with the bioadaptor versus 7.8% with DES (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.13-0.87; NNT=20). Cardiovascular mortality at 4 years was lower with the bioadaptor (0.5% vs 3.7%; p=0.020). No excess risk of device thrombosis was observed. Among patients undergoing LAD intervention, 4-year TLF was 2.7% versus 10.6% (p=0.021). Conclusion: The DynamX bioadaptor demonstrated non-inferior 12-month outcomes compared with contemporary DES and was associated with lower rates of target lesion failure during longer-term follow-up. The emergence of benefit after the 6-month uncaging period supports further investigation of vascular restoration strategies in PCI. Larger randomized studies with extended follow-up are needed to confirm these findings and define the role of bioadaptors in contemporary coronary intervention.
title: Abstract 15866: DynamX Bioadaptor versus Contemporary Drug-Eluting Stents After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials

abstract: Introduction: Triple M Overlap Syndrome (TMOS), consisting of the myocarditis, myositis and myasthenia gravis triad, is a rare immune-related adverse event (irAE) and is associated with high mortality. Myocarditis secondary to ICI therapy may lead to conduction abnormalities, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, new-onset heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Case Presentation: A 67-year-old male with invasive urothelial bladder carcinoma presented to the emergency department for evaluation of blurry vision, dysphagia and generalized weakness that began three weeks after initiation of neoadjuvant Pembrolizumab. The patient was hemodynamically stable on presentation. Physical exam was notable for bilateral ptosis and proximal upper and lower muscle weakness.Initial Troponin I was elevated to 3360 ng/L. An electrocardiogram (ECG) revealed a new right bundle branch block (RBBB) and left posterior fascicular block (LPFB), Figure 1. Creatine Kinase (CK) level was elevated to 5274 U/L. A myositis panel was positive for acetylcholine receptor, striated muscle and titin antibodies. The negative inspiratory force (NIF) was 26 cm H 2 O and the patient was subsequently admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). Management: A Transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) revealed preserved ejection fraction (EF), without any regional wall motion abnormalities. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was notable for increased extracellular volume (ECV) to 36% and increased myocardial native T1 mapping to 1166 msec, though without delayed enhancement. Coronary CTA revealed mild non-obstructive coronary artery disease in the left anterior descending artery.TMOS was suspected based on clinical and laboratory findings. The patient received pulse-dose steroids without significant clinical improvement. Immunomodulatory therapy was then escalated stepwise from intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) to plasmapheresis followed by addition of Rituxumab and Infliximab. Pyridostigme was additionally started for management of myasthenia gravis. Outcome: Repeat ECGs revealed gradual resolution of bifascicular block and normalization of QRS duration. Troponin I continued to trend and normalized by discharge. The patient was discharged on day 13. Pembrolizumab was indefinitely discontinued. Discussion: As the use of ICI therapy for various cancers rapidly expands, early recognition of TMOS is key to allow for timely initiation and escalation of immunomodulatory therapy. Conduction abnormalities require close monitoring for deterioration to life-threatening arrhythmias. A multidisciplinary approach is additionally paramount for management of complex co-morbidities.
title: Abstract 15874: A Case of Triple M Overlap Syndrome with Bifascicular Block Secondary to Pembrolizumab

abstract: Background Cardiopulmonary bypass triggers a systemic inflammatory response that can result in adverse outcomes. The Steroids In caRdiac Surgery Trial (SIRS; n=7,507) demonstrated no benefit with perioperative administration of methylprednisolone. Cardiogenic shock clinical trials have been limited in size with few demonstrating benefit. With mixed results regarding steroid therapy in other shock states, interest remains in the potential benefits for cardiogenic shock. Research Question Is peri-operative steroid therapy in patients with cardiogenic shock undergoing cardiac surgery associated with improved outcomes? Methods We conducted a post-hoc analysis of SIRS among patients with preoperative shock. We defined preoperative shock as the following: (1) preoperative administration of vasopressors or inotropes or (2) preoperative use of an intra-aortic balloon pump or left ventricular assist device. Participants were randomized to receive methylprednisolone 250 mg at induction and initiation of bypass or placebo. Outcomes included: (1) mortality, (2) myocardial infarction, and (3) surgical site infection. We prespecified the following subgroups: (1) patients receiving vasopressor or inotropic support alone (MED) and (2) those receiving mechanical circulatory support alone (MCS). We performed a sensitivity analysis with logistic regression to determine if preoperative shock modified the impact of perioperative steroids. We performed our analyses using R and DataParty. Results Among the 686 patients with preoperative shock (median age 64 years; 38% female), baseline comorbidities included: heart failure (24%), prior myocardial infarction (29%), diabetes (30%), hypertension (63%), and dyslipidemia (32%). Baseline characteristics were similar among those randomized to methylprednisolone or placebo. The median left ventricular ejection fraction was 49% (interquartile range 35-59). Thirty-day mortality occurred in 8.1% receiving methylprednisolone and 8.5% receiving placebo (relative risk [RR] 0.95, 95% CI 0.58-1.57). Mortality at 6 months occurred in 12.3% and 11.9%, respectively (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.69-1.55). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (RR 1.11, 95% CI 0.81-1.52) or surgical site infection (RR 2.12, 0.8-5.58) at 30 days. Subgroup analyses (MED, n=618; MCS, n=127) yielded similar results. A sensitivity analysis demonstrated no significant interaction between steroids and preoperative shock. Conclusions Among patients with preoperative shock undergoing cardiac surgery, methylprednisolone was not associated with a difference in mortality, myocardial infarction, or surgical site infection. These findings align with the overall results of SIRS and do not demonstrate a significant association between perioperative corticosteroid administration and patient-important outcomes in this population.

title: Abstract 15890: Steroids In caRdiac Surgery (SIRS) Trial: Cardiogenic Shock Substudy

abstract: Background Patent foramen ovale (PFO)-associated paradoxical embolism is a recognized cause of ischemic stroke; however, embolization from a catheter-associated right atrial thrombus is rare. Identifying the embolic source is critical, particularly in patients with multiple competing stroke etiologies. Case A 56-year-old female with opioid use disorder on medication-assisted therapy, Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, nonischemic cardiomyopathy, hypertension, dyslipidemia, mitral valve prolapse, and Hodgkin’s lymphoma receiving chemotherapy presented with aphasia, altered mental status, and right-sided weakness. Admission NIHSS was 17. CT angiography demonstrated acute occlusion of the left cervical internal carotid artery extending to the carotid terminus with left M1 occlusion. As she was outside the thrombolytic window, emergent mechanical thrombectomy achieved TICI 2A reperfusion.Despite intervention, neurologic deficits worsened and MRI demonstrated multifocal acute left hemispheric infarctions. Given active malignancy, cancer-associated hypercoagulability was initially suspected. Evaluation for a cardioembolic source revealed an early right-to-left shunt on transthoracic echocardiography. Transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a PFO with large-volume right-to-left shunting and an incidental finding of a large mobile thrombus attached to the distal tip of the chemotherapy port catheter within the right atrium. No left atrial appendage thrombus was identified. Telemetry excluded atrial fibrillation, Doppler studies showed no peripheral venous thrombosis, and blood cultures were negative.Because catheter manipulation carried a high risk of recurrent paradoxical embolization, a multidisciplinary strategy involving cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, vascular surgery, and interventional radiology was pursued. The patient underwent successful percutaneous PFO closure by the structural cardiology team. Post-procedure intracardiac echocardiography confirmed the persistence of the mobile catheter-associated thrombus after device deployment. Eventually, the chemo-port was removed. Conclusion This case highlights a rare instance of ischemic stroke caused by paradoxical embolization of a chemo-port-associated right atrial thrombus through a PFO. Although malignancy-associated hypercoagulability was initially suspected, multimodality imaging identified the catheter-associated thrombus as the likely embolic source. In patients with ischemic stroke and indwelling central venous access devices, catheter-associated thrombus carries a potential nidus for paradoxical embolization. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are essential to prevent recurrent embolic events.
title: Abstract 15900: The Thrombus Next Door: Paradoxical Stroke Caused by a Chemo-Port-Associated Right Atrial Thrombus

abstract: Introduction: Optimal valve sizing relative to the native aortic annulus is critical in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). The SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valve incorporates design modifications to improve sealing and durability, yet the ideal percentage resizing relative to CT-derived annular diameter remains undefined. This study aimed to determine which resizing category yields the most favorable hemodynamic outcomes and lowest adverse event burden following TAVR with the S3UR valve. Methods: A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted on 514 consecutive patients who underwent TAVR with the S3UR valve at three Prisma Health Hospitals (South Carolina). Percentage resizing was calculated as: [(valve nominal diameter – CT annular diameter) / CT annular diameter] х 100. Patients were categorized into five groups: Category 1 (≥0% to <10%), Category 2 (≥10% to <20%), Category 3 (≥20%), Category 4 (≥–10% to <0%), and Category 5 (≤–10%). The primary outcome was post-TAVR mean transvalvular gradient on 90-day transthoracic echocardiogram. Secondary outcomes included composite adverse events: new-onset LBBB, pacemaker implantation (PPI), and paravalvular regurgitation (PVR). A Yuen trimmed mean ANOVA (20% trimming) compared mean gradients across groups with Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted pairwise comparisons. A Kruskal-Wallis test served as confirmatory nonparametric analysis. Results: The trimmed mean ANOVA demonstrated significant differences in post-TAVR mean gradient across groups (F=4.13, p=0.004). The Kruskal-Wallis test confirmed distributional differences (χ 2 =21.92, p=0.0002). Category 2 (≥10% to <20%) had the lowest mean gradient and adverse event burden; Category 5 (≤–10%) had the highest. Adjusted pairwise comparisons showed significant differences: Categories 2 vs 5 (p=0.0096), 2 vs 4 (p=0.02), 2 vs 3 (p=0.03), 1 vs 5 (p=0.0096), 1 vs 4 (p=0.02), and 1 vs 3 (p=0.06). No significant differences were found between Categories 1 and 2 (p=0.66) or 4 and 5 (p=0.42). Results are summarized in the Figures. Conclusions: In 514 patients undergoing TAVR with the S3UR valve, moderate positive resizing (>0% to <20%) was associated with the lowest mean gradients and composite adverse event burden (LBBB, PPI, PVR). Undersizing (≤0%) and excessive oversizing (≥20%) were associated with worse outcomes. A targeted resizing strategy within 0-20% may optimize outcomes with the S3UR platform. Prospective validation is warranted.
title: Abstract 15909: Optimal Percentage Resizing of the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA Valve Relative to CT Annular Diameter: Impact on Hemodynamic Outcomes and Adverse Events After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Multicenter Retrospective Analysis

abstract: Background: Intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) occurs in up to 40% of reperfused STEMIs, indicating severe reperfusion injury. Ferumoxytol, an intravascular iron-based contrast agent with potent T1-shortening properties, enables IMH detection on T1-weighted FLASH cine. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) further quantifies paramagnetic iron within hemorrhagic zones, providing a continuous IMH severity measure. However, the multi-domain cardiac impact of IMH presence and severity remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize associations of ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR (FE-CMR)-defined IMH with acute and follow-up functional, structural, and remodeling domains after reperfused STEMI. Methods: Thirteen reperfused STEMI patients underwent FE-CMR and echo within 72 hours of reperfusion and gadolinium-enhanced CMR at 3-6 months. Patients were classified as IMH+ (n=5) or IMH– (n=8) by post-ferumoxytol FLASH cine with QSM as reference standard. IMH severity was quantified from QSM maps as susceptibility elevation. Groups were compared across acute and follow-up functional, structural, and remodeling domains, with dose-response relationships between susceptibility elevation and these domains assessed within the IMH+ group. Results: In the functional domain, IMH+ patients demonstrated significantly lower acute RVEF (45.0% vs 55.2%, p=0.028) and TAPSE (1.7 vs 2.15 cm, p=0.040), with large-effect trends toward lower acute and follow-up LVEF (39.5% vs 52.1%, p=0.117, ES=0.50 and 37.0% vs 58.3%, p=0.055, ES=0.61). In the structural domain, IMH+ patients had larger follow-up infarct size (19.1% vs 8.0% LV mass, p=0.011) and mass (22.1 vs 8.3 g, p=0.033). In the remodeling domain, IMH+ patients showed a large-effect trend toward adverse LV remodeling (ΔLVEDV +34 vs –9 mL, p=0.149, ES=0.51). Within the IMH+ group, susceptibility elevation correlated significantly with acute LV dysfunction and dilation (LVEF r=–1.00, LVESV r=+0.90), and showed strong correlations with impaired acute strain (GLS r=+0.80, GCS r=+0.70), persistent follow-up LV dysfunction (LVEF r=–0.80), and adverse remodeling (ΔLVEDV/ΔLVESV r=+0.80). Conclusion: FE-CMR-defined IMH identifies a high-risk phenotype with biventricular dysfunction, larger scar, and adverse remodeling. IMH-related susceptibility elevation correlated dose-dependently with LV functional and remodeling indices, supporting its potential as a quantitative tool for IMH severity assessment and risk stratification after reperfused STEMI.
title: Abstract 15920: Bleeding Into Injury: Ferumoxytol-CMR-Defined Intramyocardial Hemorrhage Identifies a Multi-Domain High-Risk Phenotype After Reperfused STEMI

abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) have established cardiovascular benefits in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i), a cornerstone therapy for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (mBC), are associated with clinically significant cardiovascular toxicity, which appears worse amongst patients with T2DM. Whether GLP-1 RA confers cardioprotection in this high-risk population remains unknown. Purpose: To evaluate the association between GLP-1 RA use, mortality and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with mBC and T2DM receiving CDK4/6i. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global research network. Adult women with HR+/HER2– mBC and T2DM who initiated CDK4/6i therapy (palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib) between January 2011 and May 2026 were identified. Patients with type 1 diabetes and prior major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) were excluded. The cohort was stratified by GLP-1 RA exposure (ongoing use at CDK4/6i initiation and continued thereafter) versus non-use. The primary endpoint was a composite of MACCE including acute coronary syndrome (ACS), heart failure (HF), cerebral infarction/ischemia, cardiac arrest, percutaneous coronary intervention, and intravenous loop diuretic use for acute heart failure. Secondary endpoints included the individual components of MACCE, arrhythmia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), and all-cause mortality (ACM). One-to-one propensity score matching (PSM) was performed balancing 32 clinically relevant covariates. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals in the matched cohort over 5 years of follow-up. Results: Among 5,810 eligible patients, 267 were GLP-1 RA users and 1,482 were non-users. PSM resulted in 250 well-balanced pairs. GLP-1 RA use was associated with a significant reduction in MACCE (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.91, p=0.012), HF (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.94, p=0.022), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.34-0.73, p=0.001). No statistically significant difference was noted for VTE (HR 0.65 95% CI 0.39-1.09, p=0.098), arrhythmia (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.5-1.2, p=0.245), or ACS (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.56-1.236, p=0.341). Conclusions: In this real-world, propensity-matched retrospective analysis, GLP-1 RA use was independently associated with a substantial reduction in MACCE, HF events, and all-cause mortality among patients with T2DM and HR+/HER2- mBC receiving CDK4/6i therapy. These findings suggest a potential cardioprotective role for GLP-1 RA in this vulnerable cardio-oncology population and provide a strong rationale for prospective confirmation to guide integration into cardio-oncology care.
title: Abstract 15932: Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonists and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Receiving Cyclin Dependent Kinase 4/6 Inhibitors Therapy for Metastatic Breast Cancer

abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) have been shown to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2DM), obesity, and cardiovascular disease. However, individuals with a family history of premature ischemic heart disease (IHD) are a high-risk population in whom the cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists remain uncertain. This study compares MACE associated with GLP-1 versus non-GLP-1 use among individuals with a family history of premature IHD without T2DM. Methods: The TriNetX U.S. Collaborative Network was used to analyze MACE risk for individuals aged 18 and above with a family history of premature IHD within one year of initiating GLP-1. This was compared to a control of non-GLP-1 users. Individuals with a history of T2DM, prior myocardial infarction (MI)s, or previous coronary revascularization were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographics and covariates including body mass index, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and incident MI. Secondary outcomes included individual primary outcome components. Statistical analyses were conducted with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariate Cox proportional hazard modeling. P-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: After matching, 51,026 individuals were included in each cohort. Baseline patient demographics and clinical attributes were well balanced. Average age of individuals at index was 49. At one year, individuals taking GLP-1 demonstrated significantly lower rates of the primary composite outcome compared to individuals not taking GLP-1 (hazard ratio [HR] 0.19; 95% CI, 0.17-0.22, p < 0.0001). Secondary outcomes of all-cause mortality (HR 0.11; 95% CI 0.09-0.13, p < 0.0001) and MI (HR 0.48; 95% CI, 0.39-0.59; p < 0.0001) were significantly lower in those on GLP-1 compared to those not on GLP-1. The primary composite outcome was also significant through Cox multivariate proportional hazards (HR = 0.30; 95% CI = 0.27-0.33; p < 0.0001). Conclusion: GLP-1 use was associated with significantly lower rates of the composite outcome compared to non-GLP-1 use in individuals without T2DM and with a family history of premature IHD. This suggests that GLP-1s may be useful for risk reduction in those with increased genetic predisposition for incident cardiovascular disease.
title: Abstract 15944: Cardiovascular Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Individuals with Family History of Ischemic Heart Disease

abstract: Introduction: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) during pregnancy is associated with significant maternal and fetal morbidity and mortality. Physiologic changes of pregnancy, including increased blood volume and cardiac output, can worsen PH and precipitate right ventricular failure, arrhythmias, thromboembolic events, and hemodynamic collapse. Pregnancy in patients with PH remains a high-risk condition requiring multidisciplinary management. We present a case of newly diagnosed idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (WHO Group 1 PH) during pregnancy, highlighting the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges involved in optimizing maternal and fetal outcomes. Case description: A 29-year-old woman at 32 weeks’ gestation with pregestational diabetes presented with 3 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea. She had no cardiopulmonary symptoms during a prior pregnancy that resulted in the uncomplicated delivery of a healthy infant one year earlier. On presentation, she was tachycardic (114 bpm) and hypoxic (SpO 2 89% on room air, improved with 5 L oxygen). Electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia, right atrial enlargement, and right ventricular (RV) hypertrophy. Chest imaging was unrevealing. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated severe RV dilation and systolic dysfunction, septal flattening consistent with RV pressure/volume overload, and severe right atrial enlargement, concerning for severe pulmonary hypertension. Interventions: Right heart catheterization demonstrated severe precapillary PH with a pulmonary artery pressure of 108/34 mmHg (mean 67 mmHg), elevated right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) of 81.3 mmHg, and negative vasoreactivity testing. She was emergently transferred to a specialized PH center and initiated on intravenous epoprostenol. Repeat TTE showed improvement in RVSP to 51 mmHg. At 33 weeks' gestation, she underwent cesarean delivery, which was complicated by postoperative cardiogenic shock requiring vasopressor support and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Her subsequent course was further complicated by preeclampsia, cardiac arrest, and sepsis, culminating in maternal death. Discussion: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is characterized by elevated pulmonary vascular resistance that can lead to progressive right ventricular failure. Pregnancy is generally contraindicated in patients with PH because physiologic changes, including increased plasma volume, cardiac output, and a hypercoagulable state, can precipitate right ventricular decompensation, arrhythmias, thromboembolic events, and cardiogenic shock. The peripartum and postpartum periods are particularly high risk due to rapid hemodynamic shifts. Despite advances in therapy and multidisciplinary care, maternal mortality remains significantly elevated, highlighting the need for early diagnosis and specialized management.
title: Abstract 15946: The Failing Right Ventricle: Severe Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Presenting During Pregnancy

abstract: Introduction: Smoking cessation after acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a Class I recommendation, yet prescription pharmacotherapy use remains low, and its real-world cardiovascular effectiveness when added to nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) is poorly characterised. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (67 healthcare organisations). Adults hospitalised with ACS who received NRT within one month, serving as a proxy for active smoking status, were identified. Two co-primary propensity-matched (1:1, 50 covariates, caliper 0.10 SD) comparisons evaluated bupropion + NRT and varenicline + NRT individually versus NRT alone; a supportive analysis evaluated combined pharmacotherapy versus NRT alone. All-cause mortality was the primary endpoint. Secondary outcomes included MACE, heart failure exacerbations, major bleeding, TIA/stroke, emergency rehospitalisations, and cardiac rehabilitation utilisation, assessed at 6 months and 1 year via Kaplan-Meier analysis. Hazard ratios (HRs) greater than 1.0 indicate higher hazard in the NRT-only group. Results: After matching, the combined analysis comprised 8,574 pairs, the bupropion analysis 4,654 pairs, and the varenicline analysis 2,126 pairs. At 1 year, the combined pharmacotherapy group had significantly lower all-cause mortality (HR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16-1.37), MACE (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.12-1.21), heart failure exacerbations (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25), major bleeding (HR 1.18, 95% CI 1.08-1.28), and greater cardiac rehabilitation utilization (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.92; all p < 0.001). TIA/stroke did not differ significantly. Six-month results were consistent. Both varenicline and bupropion individually showed lower mortality and MACE. A urinary tract infection falsification endpoint showed no between-group differences, supporting matching validity. The pharmacotherapy group had higher rates of new-onset depression, driven predominantly by bupropion recipients. Conclusions: In this propensity-matched real-world analysis, adding prescription smoking cessation pharmacotherapy to NRT after ACS was associated with lower mortality and fewer adverse cardiovascular events, supporting broader integration into post-ACS care pathways.
title: Abstract 15948: Addition of Bupropion or Varenicline to Nicotine Replacement Therapy After Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Propensity-Matched Real-World Analysis

abstract: BACKGROUND: SGLT2 inhibitors have shown benefits in HFrEF by reducing cardiovascular death, heart failure hospitalizations, and CKD progression. Their use in ESRD patients who are dependent on dialysis is more limited and nuanced due to reduced glucosuric and natriuretic effects. However, SGLT2 inhibitors have direct cardiac and vascular effects, lowering intracellular sodium and calcium in cardiomyocytes and reducing oxidative stress, fibrosis, and autophagy. There is emerging, albeit limited, randomized trial data indicating a potential benefit. Subgroup data from advanced CKD trials, such as the DAPA-CKD trial and post-hoc analyses, support the persistence of cardiorenal benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors after dialysis initiation. METHODS: This analysis used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Cohort 1 included patients who were age >18 years, had ESRD dependent on renal dialysis, systolic heart failure, LVEF ≤40%, and exposure to an SGLT2 inhibitor: dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, or canagliflozin. Cohort 2 had the same inclusion criteria but was not prescribed any SGLT2 inhibitor. Propensity score matching was used, and both cohorts included 998 patients per group after matching. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, STEMI or acute MI, stroke, atrial fibrillation, heart failure outcome, ER visit or hospitalization, and ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation. RESULTS: All-cause mortality was significantly lower among SGLT2 inhibitor users on Kaplan-Meier survival analysis (HR 0.757, 95% CI 0.666-0.861; log-rank p <0.001). Risk analysis showed lower rates of STEMI/acute MI (RR 0.685, 95% CI 0.534-0.878), atrial fibrillation (RR 0.617, 95% CI 0.470-0.810), and heart failure events (RR 0.838, 95% CI 0.714-0.983), although Kaplan-Meier analyses for these outcomes were not statistically significant. No significant differences were observed in stroke (RR 0.776, 95% CI 0.531-1.133), ER visit/hospitalization (RR 0.980, 95% CI 0.944-1.018), and VT/VF risk (RR 0.963, 95% CI 0.864-1.073). CONCLUSION: There is a potential mortality benefit associated with SGLT2 inhibitor use in patients with ESRD and HFrEF. In this retrospective analysis, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. Given the observational design, these findings warrant further prospective studies.
title: Abstract 15963: SGLT2 Inhibitor Use in ESRD and HFrEF: A Retrospective Outcomes Analysis

abstract: Introduction/Background: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is increasingly recognized outside the setting of acute myocardial infarction (AMI), yet non-AMI CS is often analyzed as a single entity despite substantial clinical heterogeneity. Research Question/Hypothesis: We characterized national trends in mutually exclusive CS phenotypes and compared in-hospital mortality and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use. Methods/Approach: We analyzed adult hospitalizations in the National Inpatient Sample from 2016-2023. CS was identified using ICD-10-CM code R57.0 in any diagnosis position. Hospitalizations were assigned to mutually exclusive phenotypes using a prespecified hierarchy: type 1 AMI-CS, cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS, procedure-associated CS, pulmonary embolism-associated CS, myocarditis-CS, Takotsubo-CS, valvular-CS, arrhythmia-associated CS, heart failure/cardiomyopathy-CS, and other non-AMI CS. Survey-weighted analyses estimated national trends, in-hospital mortality, and MCS utilization. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, year, payer, income quartile, hospital teaching/location status, hospital bed size, and Elixhauser comorbidity burden. Results/Data: We identified 305,871 adult CS hospitalizations, representing 1,529,355 weighted hospitalizations. AMI-CS accounted for 33.2%, followed by heart failure/cardiomyopathy-CS (17.7%), valvular-CS (17.2%), arrhythmia-associated CS (13.8%), cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS (9.2%), and other non-AMI CS (6.5%). From 2016 to 2023, AMI-CS declined from 42.8% to 28.2% of CS hospitalizations, while cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS increased from 7.2% to 13.1%, valvular-CS from 14.6% to 19.9%, and heart failure/cardiomyopathy-CS from 15.3% to 17.6%. Overall in-hospital mortality was 32.9%. Adjusted mortality differed markedly by phenotype and was highest in cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS (adjusted predicted mortality 64.8%) compared with AMI-CS (35.2%). Despite this, adjusted MCS use was substantially lower in cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS than AMI-CS (9.3% vs 36.2%). Compared with AMI-CS, cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS had higher adjusted odds of mortality (OR 3.55, 95% CI 3.44-3.66) but lower adjusted odds of MCS use (OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.16-0.18). Mortality and MCS trends differed significantly by phenotype (interaction p<0.001 for both). Conclusions: From 2016-2023, the national CS population shifted away from AMI-CS toward heterogeneous non-AMI phenotypes, particularly cardiac arrest-associated, valvular, and heart failure/cardiomyopathy-associated CS. Phenotypes differed substantially in outcomes and MCS use, with cardiac arrest-associated non-AMI CS demonstrating the highest mortality but markedly lower MCS utilization than AMI-CS. These findings support phenotype-specific CS surveillance and risk stratification.
title: Abstract 15969: Shifting Phenotypes of Cardiogenic Shock: National Trends, Outcomes, and Mechanical Circulatory Support Use from 2016-2023

abstract: Ventricular assist devices (VADs) are increasingly utilized as bridge-to-transplant, bridge-to-decision, and destination therapy for patients with advanced heart failure. Despite their expanding use, right ventricular failure (RVF) remains a common and clinically significant complication, affecting up to 40% of patients and contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Echocardiography provides a readily available, noninvasive means of assessing RV function, but the utility of post-LVAD quantitative parameters remains unclear. While prior studies have focused on pre-implant RVF prediction, less is known about post-implant quantitative echocardiographic assessment of evolving RV dysfunction. We therefore performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the association between post-LVAD quantitative echocardiographic parameters and subsequent RVF. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception through February 2026 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251121747). Eligible studies included adult LVAD recipients with post-implant quantitative echocardiographic assessment of RV function. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using Covidence. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using mean differences (MD) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Primary analyses examined tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) and right ventricular fractional area change (RV-FAC). Exploratory analyses were conducted for right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RV-GLS) and tissue Doppler systolic velocity (TDI S'). Of 1,982 identified records, 15 studies met eligibility criteria for inclusion. Six studies (747 patients) and five studies (650 patients) contributed to the TAPSE and RV-FAC analyses, respectively. Patients who developed RVF had significantly lower TAPSE values (MD –0.19 cm, 95% CI –0.36 to –0.02; p=0.04), although heterogeneity was substantial (I 2 =73%). RVF was likewise associated with significantly lower RV-FAC (MD –3.34%, 95% CI –5.90 to –0.77; p=0.02), with lower between-study heterogeneity (I 2 =27%). RV-GLS and TDI S' showed trends toward worse RV function in patients with RVF, although neither reached statistical significance. Among LVAD recipients, lower post-implant TAPSE and RV-FAC are associated with the subsequent development of RVF. RV-FAC showed a more consistent association across studies, suggesting utility as a marker of early RV dysfunction after LVAD implantation. These findings highlight the role of standardized quantitative echocardiographic assessment in identifying patients at risk for RVF, supporting its use in longitudinal surveillance following mechanical circulatory support.
title: Abstract 15974: Quantitative Echocardiographic Parameters After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation and Subsequent Right Ventricular Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Background: Percutaneous left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) has expanded rapidly during an era marked by Watchman FLX adoption and evolving guideline recommendations. Contemporary nationally representative data describing changes in procedural utilization and recipient characteristics remain limited. Research question: How have percutaneous LAAO procedural volume, patient complexity, and sex distribution changed nationally from 2019 to 2023? Methods: We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample from 2019-2023 to identify percutaneous LAAO implantations using the ICD-10-PCS procedure code 02L73DK. This code identifies percutaneous intraluminal LAAO and does not distinguish between devices; given Watchman's dominant U.S. market share throughout the study period, identified cases are expected to predominantly represent Watchman implantations. Survey-weighted estimates described annual trends in procedural volume, patient comorbidity burden (van Walraven score), sex distribution, and length of stay (LOS). Results: We identified 254,240 weighted percutaneous LAAO procedures over 5 years. Annual volume increased 3.3-fold, from 26,920 in 2019 to 87,705 in 2023 (Figure 1). Mean comorbidity burden declined significantly over the study period (van Walraven score 10.2 ± 0.13 in 2019 vs. 9.6 ± 0.10 in 2023; β=–0.20 per year, p<0.001). The proportion of female recipients remained stable at approximately 41% throughout (range 40.9-41.8%; p=0.67). Mean LOS declined significantly from 1.36 days in 2019 to 0.78 days in 2023 (β=–0.16 days per year, p<0.001). Conclusions: Percutaneous LAAO volume tripled nationally from 2019 to 2023. Declining comorbidity burden and a 43% reduction in LOS suggest progressive broadening of patient selection and increasing procedural maturity. Despite this growth, the proportion of female recipients remained stable throughout, warranting further investigation into whether this reflects the underlying sex distribution of eligible patients or differences in referral and selection.
title: Abstract 15977: National Growth and Procedural Maturation of Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion in the United States, 2019-2023

abstract: Background: A successful PCI relieves symptoms and is taken, by patients and clinicians alike, as having “fixed” the problem. But atherosclerosis is systemic: concurrent plaque in the carotid and femoral beds marks a polyvascular extreme-risk phenotype with far worse outcomes, for which guidelines mandate a stricter LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) target (<40 mg/dL) than other ASCVD (<55 mg/dL). These beds are rarely imaged, so the phenotype is routinely missed. Research Question: After PCI, does the hidden burden of extracoronary atherosclerosis, and the higher risk it signals, translate into more intensive LDL-C lowering and attainment of the stricter targets these patients are owed? Methods: In a prospective post-PCI registry, consecutive patients seen ≥1 month after PCI (n=889) underwent bilateral carotid and common femoral ultrasound. Plaque was focal luminal encroachment or intima-media thickness ≥2.0 mm (stricter Mannheim adaptation). Patients were ordered by burden: CAD only; CAD + 1 extracoronary bed; or CAD + ≥2 beds (polyvascular extreme risk). Lipid metrics and combination lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) were compared across ordered groups by the Cochran-Armitage test for trend. Results: Of 889 patients, 361 (40.6%) had CAD only, 314 (35.3%) had CAD + 1 bed, and 214 (24.1%) had CAD + ≥2 beds; nearly 1 in 4 carried an unrecognized polyvascular extreme-risk phenotype identified only by imaging. Risk markers rose monotonically with burden (male sex 74.5→86.9%, p-trend<0.001; hypertension 50.1→60.7%, p=0.01; BMI>25 47.6→63.3%, p<0.001), confirming a higher-risk gradient. Treatment did not follow: mean LDL-C (50.1/51.1/52.8 mg/dL) showed no decline; attainment of <55 (69.5/63.4/64.4%) and <40 mg/dL (31.1/31.5/24.8%) did not rise; combination LLT declined with burden (70.9/64.9/63.5%; p-trend=0.05). The highest-risk group, who owed the <40 mg/dL target, met it least often (24.8%). Lp(a) >50 mg/dL was prevalent and flat (47.3/48.1/51.8%), an untreated driver atop undertreated LDL-C. Conclusions: Routine carotid and femoral ultrasound after PCI unmasks a large hidden subgroup with polyvascular extreme-risk anatomy whose risk profile is worse, yet whose LDL-C, target attainment, and combination LLT are no more intensive and, for combination therapy, paradoxically less. This treatment-risk discordance shows that post-PCI reassurance can mask rising residual risk. Embedding non-coronary vascular assessment into post-PCI care is a low-cost trigger to align treatment with risk in those who benefit most.
title: Abstract 15980: Fixed by the Stent? Detecting Hidden Polyvascular Disease and Risk-Adapted Lipid Therapy After PCI

abstract: Background: Coronary artery calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) by promoting stent underexpansion and increasing rates of stent thrombosis, restenosis, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Four principal lesion preparation strategies are available: conventional balloon angioplasty, modified balloons (cutting/scoring), atherectomy (rotational/orbital), and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). Prior evidence derives largely from pairwise trials; no study has simultaneously compared all four modalities. Methods: A systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted per Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines. Eight studies were included: ROTAXUS, ECLIPSE, BALI, PREPARE-CALC, ROTA-SHOCK, ROLLING STONE, COPS, and ROLLER COASTER-EPIC22. Treatment nodes comprised plain balloon angioplasty, modified balloon (cutting/scoring), atherectomy, and IVL. The node structure is depicted in Figure 1. Procedural, angiographic, and follow-up clinical outcomes were analyzed using odds ratios (ORs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Treatment hierarchy was estimated via P-scores/SUCRA. Prespecified sensitivity and node-splitting analyses assessed robustness and consistency. Results: Across 8 studies and 4 lesion preparation strategies, IVL ranked highest for procedural success (P-score 47.9%) and favorable procedure-related MACE (31.5%), while modified balloon ranked best for minimizing periprocedural MI (P-score 46.2%). Atherectomy was the only strategy associated with a statistically significant increase in coronary perforation risk compared to plain balloon angioplasty (OR 2.02; 95% CI 1.08-3.77; p=0.028), with plain balloon ranking most favorably for dissection risk. Procedure-related mortality was comparable across all strategies, with no statistically significant pairwise differences. At follow-up, IVL demonstrated the most favorable profile for all-cause mortality (P-score 89.4%), MI (50.6%), and target lesion revascularization (57.7%), while modified balloon ranked highest for follow-up MACE (58.4%). Sensitivity and node-splitting analyses confirmed robustness and consistency of findings across all endpoints. The results are summarized in Figure 2. Conclusion: In this NMA simultaneously comparing all four calcified lesion preparation strategies, IVL and modified balloon techniques demonstrated consistently favorable profiles across procedural efficacy and follow-up ischemic outcomes, while atherectomy was associated with a significantly higher perforation risk. These findings, to be interpreted in the context of moderate certainty evidence and largely non-significant pairwise comparisons, provide a comprehensive comparative framework to guide operator decision-making for heavily calcified coronary lesions.
title: Abstract 15990: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Calcified Lesion Preparation Strategies for Denovo Calcified lesions: A Frequentist Random Effects Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Studies

abstract: Introduction: Lidocaine is a rare but established cause of medication-induced coronary vasospasm. Although typically transient and self-limited, vasospasm can lead to myocardial ischemia and ventricular arrhythmias. We present a case of refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) following local administration of lidocaine. Patient Information: A 61-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and prior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction attributed to coronary vasospasm during dental procedure presented for elective pulmonary vein isolation. Clinical Findings and Timeline: During the procedure, he received local lidocaine with subsequent ST-elevations on ECG followed by VT and cardiac arrest. He received anaphylactic dose epinephrine after lidocaine administration without effect. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning: Coronary angiography demonstrated diffuse vasospasm as well as RCA lesion which was stented due to refractory VT (Figure 1). His VT did not resolve despite stenting and he was cannulated for VA-ECMO. Therapeutic Interventions: Following stabilization on VA-ECMO he was heavily sedated to minimize adrenergic tone. Amiodarone was initiated; lidocaine and epinephrine were avoided. A stellate ganglion block was performed. Despite these measures, he continued to have salvos of unstable VT, and evaluation for heart transplantation was initiated. In parallel, he underwent bilateral surgical sympathectomy which ultimately led to resolution of VT. Follow-Up, Outcomes, & Adverse Events: Over subsequent days, he was successfully weaned and decannulated from ECMO. He required multiple chest tubes and massive transfusion protocol in the setting of bilateral hemothoraces following sympathectomy. His hospital course was complicated by persistent respiratory failure requiring tracheostomy and gastrostomy tube placement as well as multiple ventilator-associated pneumonias. He received a secondary prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) prior to discharge. Preventive vasodilator therapy was deferred to the outpatient setting due to marginal blood pressure. Discussion and Synthesis: Lidocaine has been independently but rarely linked to coronary vasospasm leading to myocardial infarction (MI). In this case, local infiltration of lidocaine triggered severe coronary vasospasm leading to MI refractory to subsequent epinephrine and vasodilators, with resultant scar tissue as the likely source of refractory VT requiring ECMO and sympathectomy. Although often considered benign, the administration of local lidocaine can have rare but profound complications.
title: Abstract 16010: VT Storm Precipitated by Lidocaine-Induced Vasospasm Requiring VA-ECMO

abstract: Key Words: Thrombectomy, Ventricular Thrombus Abstract: This is a case of novel utilization of the AlphaVac System, an aspiration thrombectomy device, to remove a right ventricular (RV) thrombus. This case is one of the first reported uses of the innovative AlphaVac system for successful RV thrombectomy and highlights its efficacy and range of application. Intro: The AlphaVac System is a novel aspiration thrombectomy tool that has shown great benefit for the management of venous thromboemboli, notably PE. There are few published reports of the use of this system, especially for right ventricular thrombi in transit, and this case demonstrates one of few shown attempts of suction thrombectomy with this system. Patient Info: A 74-year-old female with PMH of prior DVT, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and recent hip hemiarthroplasty. No outstanding family or social history. Clinical Findings & Timeline: The patient presented with progressive bilateral leg swelling and dyspnea weeks after hip hemiarthroplasty. EKG showed normal sinus rhythm. Troponin was elevated to 186, BNP was 166, D-Dimer in 5000’s. Vitals were stable and patient was comfortable breathing on room air. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Lower extremity doppler showed multiple nonocclusive thrombi and occlusive thrombus in left lower extremity, and patient was started on therapeutic enoxaparin. TTE was ordered for NSTEMI, which demonstrated reduced EF of 40-45% and a 2.6 cm x 1.8 cm, mobile, echogeneic structure in the RV, adherent at the mid free wall and extending towards the ventricular apex - it was unclear of this was cardiac in origin, a fibrin clot in transit, or fat emboli in the setting of her recent surgery. Repeat TTE was performed confirming position of this mass. CTA chest showed acute bilateral pulmonary thromboemboli without right heart strain. Therapeutic Intervention: In the setting of this newfound mobile RV thrombus of unclear etiology, the patient underwent suction embolectomy of her RV thrombus due to risk of transit to pulmonary vasculature. The AlphaVac device was used for the procedure with friable, yellow tissue withdrawn with repeat TTE showing normal ventricular function without complication. Tissue biopsy confirmed it was a thrombus and the patient was initiated on apixaban for PE and DVT. Follow-up & Outcomes: The patient continued apixaban with plan for lifelong anticoagulation, planning for repeat TTE in 3 months. Discussion: The AlphaVac device is being used more frequently as a viable, safe, and effective method of suction embolectomy, usually for PE or venous thromboemboli. Large RV thrombi must be managed carefully due to the risk of catastrophic PE and require urgent intervention, and the AlphaVac system proved to be ann effective tool for removal of these clots. As the AlphaVac system continues to be utilized, further studies should be pursued to examine its wide range of clinical applicability.
title: Abstract 16014: Caught in Transit: Aspiration Thrombectomy of a Right Ventricular Thrombus with the AlphaVac System

abstract: Background: Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) is a method of providing short-term cardiopulmonary support to critically ill patients. Short term mortality for pediatric patients on VA-ECMO approaches 50%. Identifying risk factors for clinical decompensation during VA-ECMO can potentially lead to earlier interventions, such as changing ECMO configuration or removal of life support. Objective: Train a machine learning (ML) model to predict death in pediatric patients on VA-ECMO at varying time horizons Methods: We used a single-center, retrospective cohort of pediatric patients (n = 45 with 10 deaths) who received VA-ECMO from 12/31/2020 to 2/10/2025. Children with single-ventricle heart disease were excluded. We estimated time-varying mortality prediction models using repeated patient-level grouped cross-validation. Daily ECMO observations were structured as patient-day rows, and gradient-boosted tree models were trained to predict death within 1, 3, or 7 days using demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and ECMO-related variables, including engineered temporal features such as prior-day values and rolling means. Model performance was evaluated with row-level discrimination and calibration metrics, as well as patient-level metrics. We identified risk factors for mortality using Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), a game-theoretic method to assess feature importance. Results: The 3-day mortality model demonstrated the best overall performance across a sample of 279 patient days with 23 days with death within 3 days (8.24%) with a mean ROC-AUC (receiver operating characteristic area under curve) of 0.680 +/- 0.126 standard deviations and PR-AUC (precision recall area under curve) of 0.287 +/- 0.160 standard deviations. Patient-level performance was modest across horizons, with first-prediction concordance indices of 0.609, 0.583, and 0.525 for the 1-, 3-, and 7-day models, respectively. Top performing variables for the 3-day horizon model by SHAP values included markers of hemolysis, hypothermia, organ perfusion, coagulopathy, and age. The immediate cause of death in nearly all cases was elective decannulation in the setting of multi-organ failure. Conclusion: Among the tested models, the 3-day horizon demonstrated the most favorable balance of predictive performance and stability. These findings suggest that short-term, dynamic prediction of mortality for pediatric VA-ECMO patients is feasible using ML models incorporating common clinical variables. Since most deaths were due to elective decannulation, models strongly predictive of futility could inform decision-making for clinicians and families. Future researchers could investigate larger cohorts, include children with single ventricle heart disease, or assess organ failure specific models as next steps.
title: Abstract 16020: Predicting Outcomes of Pediatric Patients on Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Using Machine Learning

abstract: Background: Accurate 1-year mortality prediction after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is critical for patient selection and futility assessment. The EuroSCORE II and STS/ACC TVT, developed primarily for short-term surgical outcomes, consistently demonstrate suboptimal discrimination for 1-year post-TAVR mortality. Machine learning (ML) may improve risk stratification by capturing complex interactions, yet systematic benchmarking against established scores within a unified framework is lacking. Research Question: Do ML models achieve better discrimination and predictive accuracy for 1-year all-cause mortality after TAVR compared with EuroSCORE II and STS/ACC TVT? Methods: Consecutive patients with native AS undergoing TAVR evaluation (2019-2020) at a single center were retrospectively studied. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality. Using demographics, comorbidities, and echo/CT parameters, we trained 7 survival ML models (random survival forest [RSF], XGBoost survival, gradient boosting survival analysis [GBSA], Lasso-Cox, Elastic Net-Cox, Cox proportional hazards, and support vector survival machine) and 2 binary classifiers (XGBoost, Lasso logistic regression). Internal validation used 10-fold cross-validation across multiply imputed datasets. Discrimination was assessed by 1-year time-dependent AUC (tdAUC); predictive accuracy by Index of Predictive Accuracy (IPA; defined as 1 – [model Brier score / null model Brier score], where the null model assigns the marginal event rate to all patients). Confidence intervals were derived from bootstrap (500 replicates). Performance was benchmarked against EuroSCORE II, and STS/ACC TVT. Results: Among 1,035 patients (age 79 ± 9 years; 41.5% female; 1-year mortality 6.9%), 4 ML models demonstrated significantly better discrimination than both EuroSCORE II (tdAUC 0.576) and STS/ACC TVT (0.556): RSF (tdAUC 0.780; 95% CI, 0.729-0.832), XGBoost survival (0.768; 0.714-0.821), GBSA (0.757; 0.695-0.819), and XGBoost binary classification (0.735; 0.673-0.796; all adjusted p < 0.05) ( Fig. 1 ). RSF achieved the best predictive accuracy (IPA 0.078) ( Fig. 2 ), indicating a 7.8% reduction in prediction error relative to the null model. The most influential covariates associated with 1-year mortality in the RSF model are illustrated in Fig. 3 . Conclusions: Four ML models, RSF, XGBoost survival, GBSA, and XGBoost binary classification, demonstrated significantly higher discrimination than both EuroSCORE II and STS/ACC TVT for 1-year post-TAVR mortality, with RSF also achieving the highest predictive accuracy. These findings support the use of ML-based risk stratification incorporating laboratory, imaging, and cardiopulmonary history and presentations to enhance patient selection, futility assessment, and shared decision-making in TAVR candidates.
title: Abstract 16022: Novel Machine-Learning Models for 1-Year Mortality Prediction After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement and Comparisons with Established Risk Scores

abstract: Background: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a non-infective valvular manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), affecting 15-30% of patients with APS. Triple-positive APS has a high thrombotic risk, however Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are contraindicated, with data demonstrating a 5.4-fold increase in arterial thrombotic events compared to warfarin. Management becomes especially challenging when bioprosthetic valves fail rapidly in this prothrombotic environment. Case: We report the first ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve TAVR following early bioprosthetic failure in APS/SLE-associated LSE. A 63-year-old man with 20-year history of SLE and triple-positive APS underwent elective SAVR with a 27 mm bioprosthesis for symptomatic LSE confirmed by echocardiogram and sterile histopathology. Anticoagulation was transitioned from warfarin to rivaroxaban for compliance. Four months post-SAVR, bilateral arterial thromboses required thrombectomy; confirming DOAC failure, prompting permanent return to warfarin. At five months, he presented in cardiogenic shock with severe bioprosthetic obstruction (mean gradient 79.6 mmHg; valve area 0.30 cm 2 ) and LVEF decline to 25-29%. Given prohibitive redo-surgical risk (STS-PROM 18.2%), venoarterial VA-ECMO was instituted and he underwent transfemoral valve-in-valve TAVR with a 26 mm SAPIEN 3 Resilia valve. Immunosuppression and anticoagulation were optimized on leflunomide, mycophenolate mofetil, rituximab, warfarin, and hydroxychloroquine. Post-TAVR imaging confirmed a well-seated valve without paravalvular leak. LVEF improved from 25-29% to 55-59% at 4.5 months, sustained at 50-54% at 8 months. Valve hemodynamics normalized (mean gradient 12 mmHg; valve area 1.51 cm 2 ). Right ventricular function showed improving trajectory (TAPSE 1.1 → 1.5 cm). The patient was asymptomatic (NYHA class I) with no recurrent thrombosis at 8 months. Conclusion: This first reported VA-ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve TAVR for early bioprosthetic failure in LSE demonstrates three key findings: DOACs fail in triple-positive APS, mandating warfarin-based anticoagulation; prophylactic venoarterial ECMO enables safe TAVR in cardiogenic shock with prohibitive surgical risk; and combined immunosuppression with rituximab may help prevent recurrent prosthetic valve dysfunction in autoimmune valvulopathy.
title: Abstract 16027: VA-ECMO-Assisted Valve-in-Valve TAVR in Libman-Sacks Endocarditis: A Case Report

abstract: Introduction Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), or marantic endocarditis, is a rare manifestation of malignancy-associated hypercoagulability characterized by sterile valvular thrombi and high rates of systemic embolization. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is among the malignancies most strongly associated with NBTE. Diagnosis is often challenging because blood cultures are negative and echocardiographic findings may be subtle. Patient Information A 44-year-old man with recently diagnosed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma involving the liver developed recurrent venous thromboembolism despite therapeutic Eliquis. He had no known history of valvular heart disease. Clinical Findings and Timeline Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a right atrial mass, prompting transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). TEE revealed a 2.72 х 2.78 cm right atrial thrombus attached to a chemotherapy catheter and, unexpectedly, abnormal thickening of the aortic valve leaflets with moderate aortic regurgitation. Blood cultures remained negative aside from contaminant growth. The patient had no fever, persistent bacteremia, or other clinical features of infective endocarditis. Catheter-directed thrombectomy was performed, and pathology confirmed thrombus without evidence of tumor or infection. Diagnostic Assessment and Reasoning The differential diagnosis included catheter-associated thrombus, infective endocarditis, cardiac metastasis, and NBTE. Histopathology excluded metastasis, while negative cultures and the absence of an infectious syndrome argued against infective endocarditis. In the setting of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, recurrent thrombosis despite anticoagulation, new aortic valve thickening, and moderate aortic regurgitation without prior valvular disease, NBTE was considered the most likely explanation for the valvular abnormalities. Therapeutic Intervention(s) Catheter directed thrombectomy was performed for the right atrial mass. Pathological examination confirmed thrombus. Mortality in cancer-associated NBTE remains high (55% in one year), with treatment focusing on systemic anticoagulation, preferably with LMWH and management of the underlying malignancy. Discussion and Synthesis This case highlights probable NBTE in a young patient with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma and profound cancer-associated hypercoagulability despite therapeutic Eliquis. New aortic leaflet thickening accompanied by moderate aortic regurgitation in the absence of infection or pre-existing valve disease should raise suspicion for NBTE. Recognition of these findings may facilitate earlier diagnosis and optimization of anticoagulation in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 16046: When the Mass is Not the Vegetation: Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis and Recurrent Thromboembolism in Metastatic Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma

abstract: Left ventricular free wall rupture (LVFWR) is a catastrophic, life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The incidence of LV free wall rupture has declined markedly in the reperfusion era, with reported rates as low as 0.01%, although the burden may be greater given many cases result in out-of-hospital sudden death [1, 2, 3]. Contained rupture, where the myocardial tear is temporarily sealed by pericardium or thrombus, can present with subtle physical and imaging findings [4]. Recognition of this post-MI complication early, coupled with prompt surgical intervention, can be critical for survival. A 58-year-old man with known CAD and prior inferior MI (PCI to RPL), HTN, and HLD presented with hypotension and anterior ST depressions. Field STEMI activation was deactivated, and he was admitted as a stable NSTEMI. TTE revealed new LV dysfunction and a small pericardial effusion. Coronary angiography revealed severe disease in the LCx, distal LAD, and RPL. He was medically stabilized, and surgical evaluation was planned based on anatomy and function. Two days later, he developed chest pain and anterior ST elevation. Repeat angiography showed unchanged coronary anatomy, but subtle contrast extravasation on the LV gram raised concern for a contained rupture (Fig 1A). Interestingly, no pericardial expansion was seen. An urgent TTE in the cath lab revealed a large pericardial thrombus with RA/RV collapse, consistent with tamponade (Fig 1B). An IABP was placed, and the patient was transferred for emergent surgery.A median sternotomy revealed clotted hemopericardium and inferobasal LV rupture. A felt patch repair and CABG х2 (LAD and PDA) were performed. The patient was weaned off support postoperatively and had significant improvement in ventricular function. A retrospective review of his CT chest from admission revealed a contained LV free wall rupture with pericardial hematoma (Fig 2). He was discharged in stable condition. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of contained LV rupture post-MI, especially when the patient presents deceptively stable with clinical findings that are subtle. A leak on the LV gram and cath lab TTE prompted rapid escalation of care. Cross-disciplinary coordination, surgical intervention, and mechanical support led to a life-saving outcome with full recovery.
title: Abstract 16056: Hidden Behind the ST Elevation: A Contained Left Ventricular Rupture Detected in the Cath Lab

abstract: Introduction: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognized cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and is traditionally considered a disease predominantly affecting women. However, contemporary data evaluating sex-specific differences in clinical characteristics and outcomes among patients with SCAD remain limited. Research Question: We sought to compare baseline characteristics and 90-day outcomes between male and female patients presenting with SCAD-associated ACS. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adult patients diagnosed with SCAD in the setting of ACS were identified and stratified by sex. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were compared between males and females. Ninety-day outcomes included all-cause mortality, recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), cardiac arrest, stroke/transient ischemic attack (TIA), percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), bleeding events, and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) device utilization. Relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated. Results: A total of 5,538 patients were identified, with 1,997 (36.1%) males and 3,541 (63.9%) females. Compared with females, males were older (61.00±13.70 vs 56.60±14.40 years) and exhibited a greater burden of several cardiovascular comorbidities, including chronic kidney disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and prior MI. At 90 days, males experienced significantly higher all-cause mortality (8.00% vs 5.20%; RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.26-1.89; p<0.001), cardiac arrest (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.15-1.81; p=0.002), bleeding events (RR 1.43, 95% CI 1.12-1.81; p=0.004), and MCS utilization (RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.15-1.81; p=0.001). Males also underwent PCI more frequently than females (RR 1.74, 95% CI 1.57-1.93; p<0.001). No significant differences were observed in recurrent MI (p=0.175) or stroke/TIA (p=0.423). Conclusion: Male patients presenting with SCAD-associated ACS exhibited a substantially greater burden of baseline comorbidity and experienced worse outcomes compared to females. Despite SCAD being predominantly recognized as a disease of women, these findings suggest that men with SCAD may represent a higher-risk phenotype. Recognition of these sex-based differences may aid in risk stratification and inform clinical decision-making in this patient population. Further studies are warranted to validate these findings and better characterize factors associated with adverse outcomes.
title: Abstract 16112: Sex-Based Differences in Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes Among Patients Presenting with SCAD-Associated Acute Coronary Syndrome

abstract: Introduction: Cardiac myxomas are the most common primary cardiac tumors and typically present with obstructive, embolic or constitutional symptoms. Large left atrial (LA) myxomas may produce dynamic obstruction across the mitral valve, resulting in severe hemodynamic compromise. Case Presentation: A 68-year-old male with hypertension and longstanding atrial fibrillation/flutter presented with 2 weeks of progressive dyspnea, reduced exercise tolerance and palpitations. Transthoracic echocardiography (Figure 1) revealed a large (4.5 х 8.2 cm) echogenic LA mass prolapsing through the mitral valve during diastole, causing functional mitral stenosis (MS) and moderate mitral regurgitation. Additional findings included LVEF 36-40%, severe biatrial enlargement, moderate-to-severe tricuspid regurgitation, severe right ventricular (RV) dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension (PH). Right heart catheterization confirmed severe PH (RA 28 mmHg; PA 84/55, mean 67 mmHg), and coronary angiography showed non-obstructive disease. The patient underwent urgent surgical resection of the mass with mitral and tricuspid annuloplasty and LA appendage clipping (Figure 2). Histopathology confirmed atrial myxoma. Postoperatively, pulmonary pressures improved significantly (RA 4-10 mmHg; PA 33/23, mean 26 mmHg). However, his course was complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring vasopressors and VA-ECMO (intra-aortic balloon pump deferred due to incidental aortic dissection) (Figure 2), renal failure requiring hemodialysis (HD), prolonged mechanical ventilation, and septic shock due to mediastinal wound infection requiring washout and delayed chest closure. He also developed recurrent atrial fibrillation requiring cardioversion and ventricular tachycardia treated with lidocaine followed by mexiletine, ultimately requiring placement of a secondary prevention subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. After a 3-month hospitalization he was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation with outpatient HD. Discussion: This case highlights a giant LA myxoma causing a “ball-valve” effect across the mitral valve, resulting in functional MS, severe PH and RV failure. Relief of obstruction led to marked hemodynamic improvement (Figure 3), supporting the reversible impact of tumor-related inflow obstruction. While myxomas cause profound hemodynamic derangements, arrhythmic complications in advanced cases can be attributed to the tumor's anatomical effects on the cardiac chambers and valves. Conclusion: Giant LA myxomas can present with severe obstructive physiology and advanced cardiopulmonary compromise. Early recognition and surgical intervention are critical; however, significant postoperative morbidity may occur, particularly in advanced presentations with multiorgan failure.
title: Abstract 16124: Obstruction at the Mitral Gate: A Giant Left Atrial Myxoma with Hemodynamic Collapse

abstract: Abstract Fungal endocarditis is a rare condition with high mortality despite combined medical and surgical therapy. We present a case of Candida albicans endocarditis after surgical repair of a post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal defect (VSD). A 54-year-old male had a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) complicated by a VSD requiring patch repair. Months later, he developed Candida albicans endocarditis involving the VSD patch, requiring repeat surgical repair. Due to incomplete source control, lifelong antifungal suppression therapy was required. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of fungal endocarditis, the value of multimodal imaging, and the need for individualized surgical and antifungal management. Introduction Fungal endocarditis accounts for about 1.5% of all infective endocarditis cases, with a reported survival of under 20%. Current guidelines focus on valvular endocarditis as literature on ventricular septal defect patch-associated fungal endocarditis consists of isolated reports in young patients with congenital heart disease. Our case described a unique presentation of Candida albicans endocarditis after patch repair of an acquired VSD. Patient Case A 54-year-old male with dyslipidemia and pre-diabetes presented with a week of chest pain and dyspnea and was admitted for NSTEMI due to multivessel coronary artery disease. Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) demonstrated an acute VSD in the mid-inferior septum (Figure 1) requiring Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) and VSD patch repair. Six months later, he returned with sepsis due to Candida Albicans fungemia. Multimodal imaging revealed severe mitral regurgitation, partial patch separation with an associated vegetation and recurrent marked left-to-right shunting (Figure 2&3). The patient underwent a repeat VSD repair and mitral valve replacement. Patch dehiscence appeared to have occurred due to a stitch tearing through necrotic infarcted tissue, for which complete excision of the prior VSD patch was avoided due to lack of viable myocardium. An additional patch was placed to reinforce VSD closure instead. Histopathology and intra-operative tissue cultures confirmed Candida albicans . The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged home on postoperative day 8. Due to incomplete source control, lifelong fluconazole therapy was required. Discussion Ventricular septal rupture is a fatal post-MI complication. Surgical patch repair remains the standard treatment, with few long-term defects reported. This case describes Candida albicans endocarditis involving a VSD patch where complete resection was not feasible. It highlights diagnostic challenges, the value of multimodal imaging, and the need for individualized surgical and antifungal management when complete source control cannot be achieved.

abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2024 ESC guidelines adopted CHA 2 DS 2 -VA (a sex-neutral modification of CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc) for initial stroke risk stratification in atrial fibrillation (AF) patients, whereas the 2023 AHA/ACC guidelines retain female sex as an independent risk criterion. We assessed whether this current divergence is supported by data. Research QUESTION: How does the discriminative performance of CHA 2 DS 2 -VA compare with CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc for thromboembolic risk prediction across anticoagulation settings? METHODS: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020, CHARMS, and PROBAST. Five databases were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies compared C-statistics of both scores for thromboembolic events (ischemic stroke or systemic embolism) in adults with non-valvular AF. Per study, ΔAUC and standard errors were derived from DeLong p-values to account for paired within-study comparisons. Given clinical heterogeneity across scenarios and outcomes, quantitative pooling was not performed; findings were summarized using a structured narrative synthesis stratified into three pre-specified anticoagulation-based scenarios. ResultS: Nine studies (N=1,035,740; 47.1% women; 8 countries; 2009-2024) were included: five in Scenario A (N=1,007,544), three in Scenario B (N=28,035), and one in Scenario C (N=161). Thromboembolic event incidence ranged from 1.50 to 2.83 per 100 patient-years.Scenario A, OAC-naïve (k=5, N=1,007,544): One study showed significantly higher discrimination with CHA 2 DS 2 -VA (ΔAUC=+0.029; 95%CI +0.005 to +0.053; p=0.020); the remaining four showed no significant difference. The remaining four showed no clinically relevant difference; one large registry showed small but statistically significant differences favoring CHA 2 DS 2 -VA in recent periods (ΔAUC ≤+0.013, all within ±0.02).Scenario B, real-world OAC (k=3, N=28,035): All three showed no significant difference in discrimination (ΔAUC –0.008 to +0.005; all p>0.05). Net reclassification improvement was inconsistent and non-significant (range –0.137 to +0.110).Scenario C, post-stroke (k=1, N=161): One cohort assessed a different construct—stroke-severity discrimination rather than incident thromboembolism—with no significant between-score difference (ΔAUC=–0.030; p=0.09); because of outcome differences, this study was not directly comparable to scenarios A and B. ConclusionS: CHA 2 DS 2 -VA demonstrated discriminatory performance comparable to CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc across AF populations, both OAC-naïve and anticoagulated, although formal equivalence was not tested. Available evidence did not show a consistent loss of discrimination after removal of femal sex as an independent score component. These findings may help contextualize the current ESC-AHA/ACC guideline divergence in AF stroke-risk assessment.
