abstract: Background: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) received FDA approval in April 2024 for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Pivotal trials (TRILUMINATE Pivotal, Tri.Fr) systematically excluded patients with pulmonary hypertension, concomitant left-sided valve disease, and advanced renal dysfunction. Whether real-world practice extends beyond these boundaries and with what outcomes, remains unknown. Methods: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (174 healthcare organizations, ~179 million patients), we identified adults undergoing T-TEER (CPT 0569T/0570T) from January 2021 through June 2026. Patients with concomitant surgical tricuspid valve procedures (CPT 33460/33463/33464/33465), transcatheter mitral valve repair (CPT 33418/0345T), or tricuspid valve replacement were excluded. Annual volumes include repeat procedures; outcomes were restricted to index procedures (n=496 unique patients). Baseline comorbidities were ascertained from ICD-10 codes prior to procedure. All-cause mortality was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier at 30 days and 1 year. Results: A total of 496 patients across 35 institutions underwent T-TEER. Annual procedure volumes increased markedly: 26 (2021), 50 (2022), 50 (2023), 87 (2024), and 250 (2025), representing a 188% increase in the year following FDA approval. Mean age at procedure was 76.9 ± 11.5 years (median 80); 63% were female and 76% White. The cohort carried a high comorbidity burden: heart failure 95%, atrial fibrillation 90%, ischemic heart disease 73%, pulmonary hypertension 70%, CKD 55%, and cardiomyopathy 41%. Notably, 68% had concomitant mitral valve disease, which were excluded from pivotal trials. 30-day mortality was 2.3% (vs. TRILUMINATE Pivotal: 0.6%). Despite higher comorbidity burden, 1-year all-cause mortality was 12.7% — lower than bRIGHT (15.1%), EuroTR (~17.9%), and TriValve (20%). Conclusions: T-TEER utilization increased 188% following FDA approval, now spanning 35 global institutions. Compared with pivotal trial populations, the real-world cohort is more female-predominant (63%) and includes substantially higher proportions of pulmonary hypertension (70%), ischemic heart disease (73%), and CKD (55%), phenotypes largely excluded from trials. Additionally, 68% had concomitant mitral valve disease (excluded from pivotal trials). Despite this higher-risk profile, 1-year mortality (12.7%) was lower than European real-world registries (bRIGHT 15.1%, EuroTR 17.9%, TriValve 20%), suggesting T-TEER in trial-ineligible patients may achieve outcomes comparable to or better than earlier registries. These findings underscore the need for prospective outcome data in underrepresented phenotypes.
title: Abstract 17566: Real-World Adoption, Patient Characteristics, and Outcomes of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair: A Global Multi-Center Analysis from the TriNetX Network (2021-2026)

abstract: Background: Vascular and bleeding complications remain the leading source of procedural morbidity in transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Ultrasound-guided femoral access enables real-time visualization of the common femoral artery and facilitates optimal anterior-wall puncture above the bifurcation, theoretically reducing wall injury. However, most prior meta-analyses predate the contemporary TAVR device era of smaller sheath profiles, and whether the magnitude of benefit varies across procedural eras is unclear. Methods: We performed a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies of ultrasound-guided versus conventional (fluoroscopy- or landmark-guided) femoral access in adult transfemoral TAVR. Six databases plus ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through March 2026. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird τ 2 ) with Hartung-Knapp adjustment was applied to primary outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses by procedural era (early ≤2018, transitional, contemporary ≥2022) and VARC definition were performed. Results: Nine studies (n=6,355; 3,234 ultrasound, 3,121 conventional) were included. Ultrasound guidance was associated with significant reductions in minor vascular complications (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.61-0.95; P=0.023; I 2 =0%), major or life-threatening bleeding (RR 0.52; 95% CI 0.30-0.90; P=0.027; I 2 =61%), and the composite of any vascular complication or bleeding (RR 0.67; 95% CI 0.48-0.95; P=0.032). Major vascular complications (RR 0.70; 95% CI 0.39-1.26; P=0.19) and stroke (RR 1.02; 95% CI 0.57-1.84; P=0.90) did not differ significantly. Era-stratified analyses showed directionally consistent reductions for both primary outcomes — major bleeding: early RR 0.39, transitional RR 0.62, contemporary RR 0.55 (Pinteraction=0.42); minor vascular complications: early RR 1.04, transitional RR 0.72, contemporary RR 0.73 (Pinteraction=0.17). The minor vascular complication benefit was the most internally consistent finding (I 2 =0%). A lower mortality risk was observed (RR 0.54; 95% CI 0.36-0.80; P=0.013), likely reflecting residual confounding from observational temporal-comparison designs rather than a causal treatment effect. Conclusions: Ultrasound-guided femoral access is associated with consistent reductions in minor vascular complications and major bleeding across procedural eras in transfemoral TAVR, supporting routine consideration in contemporary practice. The observed mortality reduction should not be interpreted as a causal treatment effect of ultrasound guidance.
title: Abstract 17575: Ultrasound-Guided versus Conventional Femoral Access in Transfemoral Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Across Procedural Eras

abstract: Introduction: Large-bore arterial access, such as that required for percutaneous transvalvular microaxial flow pump placement, carries a significant risk of limb ischemia due to arterial occlusion. Patient information and Clinical Findings: A forty-eight-year-old female presented with syncope and was found to be in new onset cardiogenic shock from an acute myocardial infarction on bedside echocardiography. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: The patient was taken emergently to the catheterization lab due to cardiogenic shock for immediate invasive angiography and mechanical support device placement. Therapeutic Interventions: A novel, entirely percutaneous technique was employed to preserve distal perfusion in right leg using a 7 French guideliner catheter advanced over the aortic bifurcation from contra-lateral left femoral access and positioned across the occlusive percutaneous transvalvular microaxial flow pump sheath within the right common femoral artery. The proximal port of the guideliner was placed in the right common iliac artery, and the distal port in the right superficial femoral artery distal to the occlusive 14 French access. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: This technique restored distal perfusion, confirmed by angiography and doppler in the distal extremity. The percutaneous transvalvular microaxial flow pump was maintained for seventy two hours during which limb perfusion was maintained without any concerns for ischemia. Discussion and Synthesis: Post removal, this contralateral femoral approach facilitated hemostasis using a dry-closure strategy. This approach may represent a technically simple and feasible option in venous and arterial-occlusive large-bore access management.
title: Abstract 17590: A Novel Endovascular Bypass Technique Utilizing a Guideliner Introduced via Contralateral Femoral Artery for Distal Perfusion in Veno Occlusive Large Bore Femoral Access

abstract: Background: Bempedoic acid and ezetimibe are both used as non-statin lipid-lowering options in patients with hyperlipidemia and statin intolerance, but real-world comparative data on clinical outcomes are limited. Hypothesis: Among adults with hyperlipidemia and statin intolerance, bempedoic acid is associated with different 3-year cardiovascular outcomes than ezetimibe. Methods: Retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network (67 healthcare organizations). Adults with hyperlipidemia and statin intolerance who initiated bempedoic acid were compared with those who initiated ezetimibe. Propensity score matching was comprehensive: cohorts were balanced 1:1 across demographics, diagnoses, medications, and laboratory values, yielding well-balanced groups of 20,985 each (all standardized mean differences below 0.10 after matching; for example, baseline atorvastatin use balanced from a standardized mean difference of 0.29 to 0.01). Outcomes were assessed over 1,095 days. Risk ratios (RR) were derived from event proportions; hazard ratios (HR) used Cox models with log-rank p-values. Results: Compared with ezetimibe, bempedoic acid was associated with lower 3-year all-cause mortality (2.0% vs 3.3%; RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.55-0.70; HR 0.56, 0.50-0.63; P<0.001) and lower 3-point MACE (10.8% vs 12.3%; RR 0.88, 0.83-0.92; HR 0.81, 0.76-0.85; P<0.001). Safety signals were more frequent with bempedoic acid: new or worsening gout (3.7% vs 3.0%; RR 1.21, 1.09-1.34; HR 1.12, 1.01-1.24; P=0.040) and creatine kinase elevation (10.4% vs 9.2%; RR 1.13, 1.07-1.20; P<0.001). Attainment of LDL-C below 70 mg/dL was lower with bempedoic acid (22.6% vs 26.7%; RR 0.85, 0.82-0.88; P<0.001). By risk ratio, no significant differences were seen for acute myocardial infarction (RR 0.94; P=0.098), ischemic stroke (RR 0.96; P=0.355), coronary revascularization (RR 1.11; P=0.138), or tendon injury (RR 1.11; P=0.161); however, survival analysis favored bempedoic acid for myocardial infarction (HR 0.87; log-rank P=0.001) and stroke (HR 0.89; log-rank P=0.011). Conclusions: In comprehensively propensity-matched adults with hyperlipidemia and statin intolerance, bempedoic acid was associated with lower mortality and MACE than ezetimibe, accompanied by higher rates of gout and creatine kinase elevation. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective head-to-head evaluation.
title: Abstract 17612: Bempedoic Acid versus Ezetimibe and 3-Year Cardiovascular Outcomes in Statin-Intolerant Adults with Hyperlipidemia

abstract: Introduction: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognized non-atherosclerotic etiology of acute coronary syndrome, particularly in women and in those with systemic inflammatory diseases. A background of inflammation influenced by hormonal, catecholaminergic, and toxic causes underlies its pathogenesis. Malignancy-related inflammation however has not been extensively explored as precipitating factor for SCAD. Pericarditis, on the other hand, is a well-documented cardiovascular manifestation of cancer, often through pericardial inflammatory syndrome. Here, we present a case of SCAD and pericarditis as initial presentation with active malignancy, suggesting common inflammatory mechanism. Patient Information: 70-year-old female patient with history of non-obstructive coronary artery disease, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and prior 20 pack-year tobacco use presented with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest discomfort. Clinical Findings with Diagnostic Assessment: Transthoracic echocardiogram performed demonstrated new moderate pericardial effusion. Cardiac catheterization demonstrated a focal area of filling defect in distal segment apparent of Type III SCAD with TIMI grade 2 flow in the distal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery. Cardiac MRI demonstrated a small segment of near transmural late gadolinium enhancement involving the apical inferior wall and apical septum, consistent with distal LAD myocardial infarction and a moderate sized pericardial effusion with enhancement of parietal pericardium consistent with concomitant pericarditis. CT of the chest demonstrated new pulmonary nodules, which was ultimately positive for metastatic lung adenocarcinoma on lung biopsy. Patient was found to have Type III SCAD, pericarditis, and metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. Therapeutic Interventions: Pericardiocentesis was deferred by the patient following goals of care discussion. The patient was started on colchicine for pericarditis treatment. She was continued on aspirin and statin for SCAD therapy. She was referred to oncology for treatment options of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. Follow-up/Outcome: The patient elected for palliative and comfort care. She subsequently passed away. Discussion: SCAD may occur in the setting of systemic inflammation induced by malignancy. Pericarditis in cancer patients may represent an early marker of paraneoplastic inflammatory cardiovascular involvement. Dual cardiovascular pathology, SCAD and pericarditis, should prompt consideration for non-traditional, systemic risk factors, such as malignancy.
title: Abstract 17614: SCAD by Association: Cancer-Driven Inflammation and the Overlap of Pericardial and Coronary Injury

abstract: Background: Patients with end-stage heart failure (ESHF) frequently experience ventricular tachycardia (VT), recurrent hospitalizations, and substantial symptom burden. Although palliative care is increasingly incorporated into advanced heart failure management, its impact on post-discharge outcomes among patients with ESHF and VT remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association of palliative care utilization with 30-day readmissions and healthcare utilization in a nationally representative cohort. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Adult hospitalizations with ESHF and VT were identified using ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes and stratified by receipt of inpatient palliative care consultation during the index hospitalization. Survey-weighted analyses generated national estimates. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission among index survivors. Multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify independent predictors of readmission. Results: Among 1,892 weighted hospitalizations with ESHF and VT, 25.2% received palliative care consultation. Patients receiving palliative care were older (64.8 vs 61 years) and demonstrated substantially greater illness severity, including higher rates of acute decompensated heart failure (84.4% vs 73.5%), acute kidney injury (76.3% vs 57.5%), sepsis (16.4% vs 9.3%), cardiogenic shock (58.5% vs 41.2%), mechanical ventilation (19.1% vs 10.9%), and ICU-level care (66.4% vs 46.2%) (all p<0.05). Palliative care utilization was associated with significantly lower hospitalization charges ($293,827 vs $437,773; p=0.022) and lower 30-day all-cause readmission among index survivors (11.8% vs 26.5%; p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, palliative care remained independently associated with reduced odds of readmission (aOR 0.39, 95% CI 0.22-0.69; p=0.001). End-stage renal disease independently predicted increased readmission risk (aOR 3.31, 95% CI 1.39-7.86; p=0.007), whereas mechanical circulatory support was associated with lower readmission risk (aOR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24-0.94; p=0.034). Conclusion: Among patients hospitalized with ESHF and VT, palliative care consultation was associated with substantially lower 30-day readmissions despite being utilized in a markedly sicker population. These findings support earlier integration of palliative care in ESHF patients with VT and suggest a potential role in reducing recurrent healthcare utilization while facilitating goal-concordant care.
title: Abstract 17626: Palliative Care Utilization and 30-Day Readmissions Among Patients Hospitalized with End-Stage Heart Failure and Ventricular Tachycardia: A Nationwide Readmissions Database Analysis

abstract: Background: Intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a therapeutic challenge, as systemic anticoagulation may be insufficient to prevent hemodynamic deterioration while catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) carries concerns regarding bleeding complications. Recent randomized and comparative observational studies have provided additional evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of CDT in this population. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the impact of CDT compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with intermediate-risk PE. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating CDT versus anticoagulation in intermediate-risk PE. Studies involving high-risk (massive) PE, surgical embolectomy, mechanical thrombectomy without thrombolysis, pediatric populations, case reports, and single-arm studies were excluded. The primary efficacy outcome was clinical deterioration. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality and major bleeding. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and Tau 2 statistics. Sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the impact of influential studies and adjusted versus unadjusted models. All quantitative analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan) version 5.4. Results: Nine studies comprising 29,024 patients were included. CDT was associated with a significant reduction in clinical deterioration compared with anticoagulation alone (RR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.63; P<0.0001; I 2 =0%). A favorable trend toward reduced all-cause mortality was observed with CDT, although statistical significance was not reached (RR 0.57, 95% CI 0.26-1.23; P=0.15; I 2 =19%). Major bleeding was numerically higher in the CDT group but did not differ significantly between treatment strategies (RR 1.33, 95% CI 0.82-2.16; P=0.25; I 2 =0%). Heterogeneity was low across all major analyses. Conclusions: In patients with intermediate-risk PE, CDT significantly reduces clinical deterioration compared with anticoagulation alone while not demonstrating a statistically significant increase in major bleeding. Although mortality demonstrated a favorable trend toward CDT, more clinical trials are needed to determine whether these improvements translate into a survival benefit. These findings support CDT as an effective treatment strategy for carefully selected patients with intermediate-risk PE and highlight the need for larger prospective studies to further define its impact on survival and safety outcomes.
title: Abstract 17639: Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Anticoagulation for Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

abstract: Introduction: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain at high risk for peri-procedural myocardial injury and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Current guidelines recommend early high-intensity statin therapy because of its lipid-lowering and rapid pleiotropic effects. However, evidence regarding its efficacy and safety remains inconsistent. We performed a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the impact of statin preloading in ACS patients undergoing PCI. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020. Electronic databases were searched upto April 2026 to identify eligible studies comparing statin preloading with controls. Primary outcome was MACE, while secondary outcomes included mortality, reinfarction, revascularization, and stroke. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Data were pooled using a random-effects model to calculate risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic. Prespecified subgroup analyses (dose, statin type, follow-up duration) and meta-regression (year, age, hypertension, LDL levels) were performed. Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis and trial sequential analysis were performed to assess robustness and control random error. Publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots (≥10 studies) and Egger’s regression test. Certainty of evidence was appraised using the GRADE approach. Results: A total of 13 studies (n=2982) were included. Statin preloading significantly reduced MACE (RR 0.55, 95% CI 0.46-0.67; I 2 =0%) as shown in figure 1, mortality (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.24-0.78; I 2 =0%), reinfarction (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.38-0.69; I 2 =0%), revascularization (RR 0.54, 95% CI 0.37-0.79; I 2 =0%), and stroke (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.37-0.94; I 2 =0%). Subgroup analyses showed no differences by dose or follow-up, while statin type influenced MACE (p=0.028). Meta-regression demonstrated no significant effect modification by year, age, hypertension, or LDL levels. No publication bias was observed except for possible bias for stroke. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses and Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA) confirmed robustness. Certainty of evidence was moderate for MACE, low for mortality, reinfarction, and revascularization, and very low for stroke. Conclusion: Single high-dose statin preloading prior to PCI in ACS patients significantly reduces MACE and key ischemic outcomes. While mortality and other secondary outcomes also favor statin preloading, the certainty of evidence remains variable. These findings support its use as an adjunct to guideline-directed therapy, though further high-quality trials are warranted to strengthen the evidence for less certain outcomes .
title: Abstract 17662: Efficacy and Safety of Single High Dose Statin Preloading in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndrome: A GRADE Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

abstract: Background: The Watchman FLX Pro left atrial appendage occlusion device was released in September 2023 with changes compared to the FLX device, adding prominent visualization markers, expanded sizes up to 40 mm, and a longer fluoropolymer-coated PET fabric covering. This PET fabric led to thromboresistance while promoting endothelialization in animal studies but lacks similar human evidence. There is limited data comparing the peri-device leak (PDL) and patency rates between the two devices. Hypothesis: The PDL and patency rates of the Watchman FLX Pro are lower than those of the Watchman FLX device. Method: This is a retrospective, single-center, observational study evaluating patients who underwent echocardiography-guided left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) with intraprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) assessment using a Canon Aquilion One scanner. Patients received Watchman FLX from August 2020 to December 2023, while Watchman FLX Pro was implanted exclusively thereafter. Post-implantation surveillance was performed at 1-year using CTA. Every CTA was analyzed by at least 2 expert cardiovascular imagers to determine device patency, endothelialization, and PDL. Result: A total of 331 patients received Watchman FLX Pro, mean age 79.75 ± 3.03 and 65% male; And 414 patients received Watchman FLX, mean age 75.8 ± 7.9 and 64% male; Comprising a cohort of 745 patients with BMI 31.42 ± 11.53 and CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score 4.61 ± 1.47. Atrial fibrillation was classified as paroxysmal (55%), persistent (34.8%), and long-standing persistent (9.8%). At 1-year CTA surveillance, visible peri-device leaks were significantly lower in the FLX Pro cohort compared to the FLX cohort (6% [20/331] vs. 10% [43/414], p=0.047). Differences in incomplete endothelialization (26.5% [99/331] in FLX Pro vs. 29.9% [110/414] in FLX, p=0.35) and overall patency (35.9% [119/331] in FLX Pro vs. 36.9% [153/414] in FLX, p=0.083) between the two devices were not statistically significant. Conclusion: The Watchman FLX Pro demonstrated a significantly lower rate of visible peri-device leaks compared to the Watchman FLX, primarily driven by a reduction in large leaks at 1-year surveillance. Surprisingly, there was no difference in overall patency rates, despite lower PDL rates which can imply that the fluoropolymer may not enhance endothelialization as preclinical studies would suggest.
title: Abstract 17677: Comparison of Peri-Device Leak and Patency Rates After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion with Watchman FLX versus Watchman FLX Pro

abstract: Introduction: American and European societal guidelines recommend urgent surgery for large mitral valve vegetations (≥10mm) in endocarditis. The limited spatial resolution of transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) may create diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to inability to distinguish vegetations from other, rarer lesions such as valvular aneurysms. Patient Information: A 55-year-old male with a history of remote three-vessel CABG, type 1 DM, ESRD on hemodialysis status-post left arm arteriovenous graft excision and a course of IV vancomycin two months prior due to MRSA infection was admitted with Corynebacterium striatum bacteremia. Clinical Findings & Timeline: Initial TTE demonstrated a 1.7x1.9cm mobile vegetation on the posterior mitral valve leaflet with moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) and a mean mitral valve gradient of 8mmHg with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65%. However, cardiac CT scan and transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) clarified the lesion to be an aneurysm of the posterior mitral leaflet with no evidence of vegetation. Diagnostic Assessment & Reasoning: Urgent surgical intervention with valve replacement was deferred in favor of antibiotic therapy to promote infection resolution and maturation of the mitral valve tissue. This facilitated delayed open mitral valve repair rather than replacement after a three-month interval. Therapeutic Interventions: The patient underwent open mitral valve repair via redo median sternotomy. Intraoperatively, a large aneurysm at the P2 segment of the posterior mitral valve leaflet with perforation was identified. The aneurysm was resected and annuloplasty was performed using a 32 Edwards Physio II ring, thus restoring valve competence. The patient had an unremarkable recovery and was discharged home on post-operative day 7. Follow-up, Outcomes & Adverse Events: Three months post-operatively, TTE revealed LVEF 65%, trace MR, and a mean mitral valve gradient of 10mmHg. Nine months post-operatively, the patient had an orthopedic ankle surgery complicated by osteomyelitis with MRSA hardware infection and bacteremia requiring hardware removal but has not developed cardiac complications. Discussion: As of 2023, European Society of Cardiology gives a Class IC recommendation for routine use of TEE, but this is not yet reflected in American guidelines. While TTE is widely used, its limited spatial resolution may mischaracterize structural abnormalities such as vegetations versus aneurysms, which dictate different treatment plans. In this patient’s case, valve repair demonstrated durable results and he has not contracted infective endocarditis - of which there is greater risk in patients with mitral valve replacement compared to repair - despite multiple episodes of subsequent bacteremia associated with his orthopedic surgeries and osteomyelitis.
title: Abstract 17695: Aneurysm of Posterior Mitral Leaflet Initially Thought to Be a Vegetation

abstract: Background: Early detection resulting in treatment of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced heart failure (HF) is still challenging. Echocardiographic variability remains a bottleneck in standard use. We performed a novel application of a validated AI-ECG Pulmonary Hypertension Early Detection Algorithm (PH-EDA) that generates a PH likelihood score (0-1) from a standard 12-lead ECG. Whether this score can predict PH prior to right heart catheterization (RHC) in HF patients has not been explored. Methods: A retrospective study of 31 advanced HF patients who underwent RHC prior to Impella 5.5 implantation at Mayo Clinic Florida between January-December 2025. For each patient, the AI-ECG PH-EDA score (at the pre-specified threshold of 0.38 indicating a positive likelihood of PH development) obtained within 8 months of RHC was compared to invasive hemodynamics. Group 2-PH was defined as mPAP ≥30 mmHg. Results: Median age was 56 years (IQR 46-63); 84% were male; the majority were African American (55%). AI-ECG scores were obtained a median of 223 days (IQR 13-565) prior to RHC. Median AI-ECG PH-EDA score was 0.85 (IQR 0.76-0.93). At RHC a total of 22 patients (71%) met criteria for PH. AI-ECG PH-EDA showed a sensitivity of 97%. Before invasive measurement, 97% were categorized as having PH via AI-ECG alone. The AUC for prediction of mPAP ≥30 mmHg was 0.65 (95% CI 0.43-0.86) in this population. mPAP >30 mmHg showed higher AI-ECG scores compared to those with mPAP ≤30 mmHg (mean 0.834±0.138 vs 0.724±0.274, p=0.226), with a trend toward higher scores that did not reach statistical significance. Conclusions: In this pilot cohort of advanced heart failure patients undergoing right heart catheterization, we demonstrate earlier and equally sensitive detection of WHO-2 PH via a novel AI-ECG PH-EDA score correlates to invasive RHC. These findings support prospective evaluation of PH-EDA as an early screening tool.
title: Abstract 17702: AI-Enabled ECG Detection of Pulmonary Hypertension Precedes Invasive Confirmation in Advanced Heart Failure Patients - A Pilot Study

abstract: Background: Optimizing antithrombotic therapy after complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients at high bleeding risk (HBR) remains a critical clinical challenge. While dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) reduces ischemic events, it carries higher bleeding burden in this population. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy has emerged as a potential strategy to achieve a more favorable risk-benefit balance, yet long-term comparative evidence in HBR patients undergoing complex PCI is limited. Methods: Using longitudinal data from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified HBR patients who underwent complex PCI and received either DAPT or P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. The cohorts were propensity-matched 1:1 (greedy nearest-neighbor matching, 0.1 standard deviation caliper) for baseline variables including demographics, comorbidities, medications, and laboratory data. Outcomes assessed over 5-year follow-up included: major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), all-cause mortality, ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction (MI), GI bleeding, and intracranial bleeding. Summary estimates were reported as hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). All statistical analyses were conducted using the in-built statistical tool on the TriNetX platform (TriNetX, LLC, Cambridge, MA). Results: After propensity matching, both cohorts had 11,524 patients each. P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was associated with significantly lower rates of MACE (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.52-0.62, p<0.001), all-cause mortality (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.81-0.91, p<0.0001), ischemic stroke (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.31-0.42, p<0.0001), acute MI (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.21-0.3, p<0.0001), GI bleeding (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.45-0.58, p<0.0001) and intracranial bleeding (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.39-0.62, p<0.0001). Conclusions: P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy was associated with significantly lower 5-year risk of both ischemic and bleeding events, including all-cause mortality, compared with DAPT among HBR patients undergoing complex PCI. These findings support further investigation of P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy as a preferred long-term antithrombotic strategy in this high-risk population.
title: Abstract 17706: Outcomes of P2Y12 Inhibitor Monotherapy versus Dual Antiplatelet Therapy in High Bleeding Risk Patients Undergoing Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis

abstract: Background: Everolimus is an mTOR inhibitor commonly used in combination with endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer. Noninfectious pneumonitis is a recognized adverse effect; however, acute right ventricular (RV) failure associated with everolimus-induced pneumonitis is rarely reported. Case Presentation: A 67-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer receiving everolimus and tamoxifen presented with dizziness, hypotension, and nonproductive cough. Laboratory evaluation revealed elevated cardiac troponin levels. Computed tomography angiography excluded pulmonary embolism but demonstrated extensive bilateral ground-glass infiltrates. Transthoracic echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular systolic function (ejection fraction 55%), right atrial enlargement, and significant RV dysfunction with only mild pulmonary hypertension (RVSP 25 mmHg). Given the elevated troponin and RV dysfunction, right and left heart catheterization were performed. Coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive coronary artery disease, while hemodynamic assessment revealed preserved cardiac output and only mild pulmonary artery hypertension, findings insufficient to explain the severity of RV dysfunction. Infectious, ischemic, and thromboembolic etiologies were excluded.Everolimus-induced pneumonitis with associated cardiopulmonary toxicity was suspected. Everolimus was discontinued and systemic corticosteroids were initiated. The patient experienced rapid clinical improvement with resolution of hypotension and respiratory symptoms. Follow-up imaging demonstrated marked improvement of pulmonary infiltrates, and repeat echocardiography showed recovery of RV function. Discussion: Everolimus-induced pneumonitis is a well-recognized complication of mTOR inhibition; however, acute RV failure in the absence of significant pulmonary hypertension is uncommon. Extensive evaluation excluded alternative causes of RV dysfunction, including pulmonary embolism, acute coronary syndrome, left-sided heart failure, and severe pulmonary hypertension. Several mechanisms may contribute to RV dysfunction, including direct myocardial toxicity, pulmonary endothelial injury leading to an inflammatory cardiopulmonary response, and cytokine-mediated myocardial depression. The rapid improvement following drug discontinuation and corticosteroid therapy supports a reversible inflammatory process. Conclusion: Everolimus-induced pneumonitis may present with reversible acute RV failure despite minimal pulmonary hypertension. Early recognition, discontinuation of the offending agent, and prompt corticosteroid therapy may result in rapid recovery and prevent significant morbidity.
title: Abstract 17708: Reversible Acute Right Ventricular Failure Associated with Everolimus-Induced Pneumonitis in Metastatic Breast Cancer

abstract: Background: The management of severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) remains challenging, with limited comparative data across transcatheter, surgical, and medical treatment strategies. No prior network meta-analysis has simultaneously compared transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (TTEER), transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), surgical intervention, and medical therapy (MT). Methods: A systematic review and frequentist, random-effects, design-adjusted network meta-analysis was performed comparing TTEER, TTVR, surgical intervention (repair or replacement), and MT in adults with severe TR. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational comparative studies reporting 1-year outcomes were included. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality (ACM). Secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and procedure-related major bleeding events. Heart failure hospitalization (HFH) was analyzed as an exploratory endpoint. Transitivity was evaluated through assessment of key effect modifiers and exploratory meta-regression. Certainty of evidence was graded using the CINeMA framework. Node structure depicted in Figure 1. Results: Fifteen studies (3 RCTs, 12 observational) comprising 18,974 patients were included. In the design-adjusted network, TTEER was associated with significantly lower 1-year ACM compared with MT (odds ratio [OR] 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.53-0.78). Neither TTVR (OR 0.52; 95% CI 0.20-1.36) nor surgical intervention (OR 0.70; 95% CI 0.47-1.03) demonstrated a statistically significant mortality benefit versus MT. Results are summarized in Figure 2. No significant differences in ACM were observed between the active treatment strategies; Surgical intervention was associated with significantly higher MACE than both MT (OR 2.78; 95% CI 1.10-4.55; P = 0.02) and TTEER (OR 3.34; 95% CI 1.28-5.39; P = 0.03), and with significantly higher procedure-related major bleeding events than TTEER (OR 1.49; 95% CI 1.26-2.41; P = 0.002). HFH analyses were exploratory and imprecise. Conclusions: In this network meta-analysis, TTEER was associated with a significant reduction in 1-year all-cause mortality compared with medical therapy, a finding driven predominantly by observational evidence, as individual RCTs have not demonstrated a mortality benefit. Surgical management was associated with significantly higher MACE than both MT and TTEER, and with higher procedure-related major bleeding events than TTEER. These findings highlight the potential role of transcatheter interventions in contemporary TR management but underscore the need for adequately powered randomized trials to confirm the observed mortality signal and define optimal treatment strategies.
